A fixed-schedule navigation pass first refreshes a `UsfTravelNeighborhood`, derives the nearest body and a `TravelEnvelope`, then evaluates flight safety, resolves Cruise requests, and prepares locomotion; the game explicitly orders these sets ([cross-domain schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/mod.rs#L103-L125>), [navigation observe/plan chain](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/mod.rs#L74-L100>)). The neighborhood measures candidate bodies and media, selects a bounded subset by both absolute and feature-relative proximity, and refreshes after movement reaches its margin, on scale change, or after 0.5 s. Its refresh source is still a query over every `UsfTravelInfluence`, so the cache bounds downstream work but does not replace the global scan with a spatial index ([cache invalidation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/neighborhood.rs#L98-L169>), [candidate scan and selection caps](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/neighborhood.rs#L248-L360>), [query-backed refresh](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/context.rs#L7-L69>)).

The navigation layer's hard-body envelope uses semantic-surface clearance, a handoff distance, a capture speed and a braking-acceleration profile to cap Cruise speed with a stopping-distance formula ([envelope](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/policy.rs#L21-L159>)). A hard body may expose a `UsfTravelBoundary`; if sampling fails, measurement falls back to the coarse spherical extent ([optional boundary and fallback](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/influence.rs#L146-L216>)). The fixture registers `CelestialVoxelField` as both the canonical body field and travel-boundary provider, but its actual field constructor is spherical at this snapshot ([fixture registration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/scenery/celestial.rs#L74-L109>), [sphere and travel adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_field/mod.rs#L23-L45>), [surface sample adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_field/mod.rs#L130-L143>)). This boundary is a travel-policy measurement, not the physics collider or the collision response.

The separate flight supervisor uses signed radial closing speed, time to contact, required deceleration and interaction readiness to classify Advisory/Emergency; its output never resolves contact itself. In manual flight, thrust adds bounded acceleration along the requested direction. RCS damping is applied only when no translational thrust is active, so simultaneous thrust suppresses that damping. In Cruise, the controller smooths a throttle-squared target speed, then constructs a velocity at the commanded magnitude and heading; this is assisted travel, not the same physical acceleration model ([safety evaluation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/flight/model/safety.rs#L72-L135>), [safety inputs and policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/flight/runtime.rs#L25-L129>), [manual flight/RCS policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/policy.rs#L90-L129>), [Cruise velocity policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/cruise.rs#L23-L101>)). Proximity-only `TravelState.critical_dropout` is one conservative Cruise gate; directional closing-risk is a separate input to emergency dropout, so “near a planet” and “on collision course” are intentionally not one signal ([body handoff state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/travel.rs#L101-L158>), [dropout decisions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/travel.rs#L13-L95>)).

Canonical flight movement finally submits a swept displacement. A contact clips its inward velocity component; an unknown/missing result uses safe fraction zero and zero velocity, failing closed rather than committing unchecked movement ([sweep submission](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/mod.rs#L237-L291>), [sweep resolution](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/mod.rs#L293-L360>)). The focused tests cover isolated safety classification, stale-chart travel-body measurement, Cruise dropout speed capping, and charge/cooldown state. I found no test that joins neighborhood refresh, a moving Moon/surface provider, Cruise braking or dropout, accepted sweep response, and the reported 147 km/s approach. Tests are present in source but were not run. Therefore these foundations are materially more complete than “no terrain collision” or “no emergency dropout,” while the historical player report is still unresolved runtime evidence—not a demonstrated fix.

The lineage matters: September 22 `8bae4ab` replaced a broad player-control implementation with a 2,258-insertion navigation/locomotion tranche; October 6 `ab65b8e` introduced the cached influence neighborhood and hard-body speed-envelope policy; October 8 `d806e3d` added canonical sweep handling; October 9 `46e1eac` moved observation to canonical semantic motion and connected the flight safety supervisor to automatic Cruise dropout. This is a sequence of converging mechanisms, but it has not yet become one tested physical arrival transaction. The earlier note that the reported collision/braking issue had not been replayed remains correct; this section identifies what now exists without changing that status.

The per-subject control model makes several different meanings of “flight capability” explicit, but they are separate component families: [FlightCapabilities and policy requests](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/flight/model/control.rs>) describe available physical systems and attitude law; [FlightControlIntent, FlightThrottle and FlightActuation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/flight.rs>) carry transient device-independent input and persistent throttle/actuator state; [LocomotionCapabilities and inhibition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/capability.rs>) determine which regime can run and whether it is temporarily held. The distinction is sound in intent, though the repeated “capability/actuation/enablement” vocabulary requires readers to understand three layers. Pilot-facing [FlightMode/contact/landing state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/flight/model/mode.rs>) stays orthogonal to [resolved locomotion request and handoff snapshot](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/state.rs>): `FlightMode` uses a 2×/4× body-radius clearance hysteresis; it is not the motion kernel. [FlightTelemetry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/flight/model/telemetry.rs>) is a typed snapshot for presentation and reports safety/readiness fields, but it does not grant control or prove those values are fresh at the point of collision.

The state resolver centralizes the active kernel, collision policy, velocity semantics and `UsfMotionAuthority` decision ([state module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/state/mod.rs>), [decision policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/state/policy.rs>)); its request/output types remain in the separate [locomotion state model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/state.rs>). The [runtime system](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/mod.rs>) snapshots motion before the handoff and copies between canonical SI velocity and Avian's chart-local velocity when authority changes. But `runtime_collision_ready` is `Option<&Collider>::is_some()`, while `sync_locomotion_runtime` queues collider changes through `Commands`; presence is not equivalent to verified query coverage, and the newly selected representation may not exist until deferred commands apply. That timing/meaning gap is directly relevant to the earlier user-observed transition symptom, but source inspection cannot establish it caused that report.

The single [flight commit adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/commit.rs>) uses Avian MoveAndSlide for runtime-local motion and canonical relative-position integration plus the USF collision-sweep result for large/unrepresentable motion. The two paths therefore share `UsfCanonicalMotion` as semantic velocity authority but have different collision providers and acceptance logic. Manual RCS is bounded damping only when computed translational thrust is inactive; `FlightThrottle` persists across input release, so a nonzero signed throttle may continue to count as active thrust and suppress RCS damping. That interaction follows from the control/policy code; no input sequence or reported Moon approach was reproduced. The detailed source entrypoint is [the fixed-step flight orchestrator](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/mod.rs>), with the [manual velocity integrator](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/flight/policy.rs>). This narrows a plausible behavioral seam without treating it as the diagnosed cause.

### Travel assistance, approach refinement, relocation, and view scale are related but separate owners

The `NavigationCapabilities` flag controls Cruise availability, while `TravelAssistanceRequest` is the typed entrypoint for pilot/script/developer adapters and `TravelAssistanceState` owns spool, cooldown, emergency-capture and transition reason ([assistance state machine](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/travel/assistance.rs>)). Its unit tests cover charge/cancel and emergency cooldown/capture in isolation. `TravelProfile` groups manual, Cruise, planetary handoff, approach refinement and flight dynamics settings ([profile model and defaults](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/travel/profile.rs>)); however `TravelProfile::spacecraft()` currently returns `Self::character()` unchanged. The type supports per-subject policies, but the reference spacecraft does not currently use distinct tuned values. Two public configuration fields—`refinement_rate_decades_per_second` and `interaction_handoff_coverage_radius_native`—have no consumer in the inspected current source tree; only declaration/default initialization were found. This makes those profile knobs misleading and leaves unresolved whether the systems were intended to consume them or whether they are stale remnants.

Approach state is explicitly a pre-realization request, not a chart change: [ApproachRefinementState](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/travel/approach.rs>) tracks whether refinement is active, the minimum supported slice and the target slice. [The planner](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/approach.rs>) selects the nearest eligible refinable hard-body influence, computes a target from future clearance and a profile divisor, and requests spatial refinement; a requested relocation resets old-location approach intent. The [runtime module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/mod.rs>) groups context, presentation, travel and audit adapters but does not itself define their global transaction. A separate [presentation profile/audit model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/presentation.rs>) owns automatic view-scale response and exposes a compact `NavigationAudit`; its `healthy` predicate checks finite positive characteristic length and finite/initialized view scale, not collision coverage or safe physical arrival. The [presentation adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/presentation.rs>) maps characteristic length to log10 view exponent and smooths later changes by `response_decades_per_second`. The [audit adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/audit.rs>) is observation-only.

### October 26 — spatial navigation has bounded measurements, but context priority and boundary refinement remain coarse

The public [Spatial navigation module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/mod.rs>) and [travel module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/mod.rs>) re-export observer context, influence, provider and neighborhood types from their domain implementations. The game [context adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/runtime/context.rs>) supplies the controlled semantic subject and a Bevy query over all available influences. The generic [travel influence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/influence.rs>) converts each extent and feature length from its declared scale to metres, optionally asking a type-erased boundary provider for a hard-body sample; failure falls back to the authored sphere. A [neighborhood cache](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/neighborhood.rs>) scans available influence components only on expiry/material movement, retains bounded nearest candidates by absolute and relative distance, and still re-probes an empty result because world discovery may be incomplete. This is a cache over a global ECS scan, not a spatial index or complete-world query.

The [context resolver](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/context.rs>) prefers any local hard body/medium within a 12× relative-proximity threshold, then any region, then any remaining structure. Consequently, a region can set manual characteristic pace before a nearer-but-not-local hard body or medium; whether this is intentional broad-scale context or an undesirable region-priority override is an unresolved policy question. The source does not establish a reproduced user-visible speed error. Stable ties also have no explicit entity-ID tie-break after candidate sorting, so exact ties may inherit ECS query order.

The [navigation boundary adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/navigation/travel/boundary.rs>) deliberately exposes only one nearby point, outward vector and measurement scale. The current [celestial fixture](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/scenery/celestial.rs>) registers its authority as a sphere and attaches both travel influence and provider. The [celestial navigation implementation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_field/mod.rs>) supplies `surface_near`, which is radial. Separately, the [volumetric projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_field/boundary.rs>) projects onto the canonical field’s nearest reachable zero crossing; current source search finds it used by voxel contact preparation, not by `UsfTravelBoundary::sample_near`. Both paths coincide for the current sphere-only fixture. If caves/non-radial surfaces return, Cruise clearance/context can therefore remain radial while voxel contact demand follows volumetric boundaries. This is a source-confirmed integration gap for future field shapes, not an active mismatch in the current fixture or a collision guarantee.

History begins with `d559e3e6` (September 21), which introduced scale-aware travel influences and replaced a fixed body-radius speed floor. `0e46041f` (September 27) then introduced a reusable travel-boundary resolver; the October 6 Spatial reorganization moved its generic contract under `spatial/navigation`. The later voxel SDF projection landed as a separate physical-contact capability. The architecture has two boundary consumers with different jobs—travel policy and physical demand—but the field adapter has not yet unified their geometry source. See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and the [current navigation cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#spatial-navigation-derives-a-bounded-context-from-a-global-influence-scan).

### October 26 — Scale Slices are semantic partitions, but their debug geometry mixes coordinate units

The [slice model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/slice/mod.rs>) creates 71 named roots, stores the registry in `UsfScaleSlices`, and relates scale-local entities under the root selected by `UsfScaleLayer`. The relationship adds navigable ECS organization; the docs explicitly deny transform parenting and distinguish persistent Scale Slice membership from LOD or separate universes. A `u128` mask covers the fixed 71-slice domain. The [Spatial plugin](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/mod.rs>) starts roots and runs membership synchronization in PostUpdate alongside other spatial changes. This is a useful semantic layer over hot-path scale tags, with two representations of the same partition (layer exponent and relationship target) kept in sync by a system.

The [canonical-position synchronizer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/systems.rs>) projects local `Transform.translation` back through the runtime chart only when frame/transform/realization/layer changes. It skips canonical-kinematic entities; if realization ownership cannot resolve, it logs and leaves the prior semantic position intact. That is an explicit error path with stale canonical state as the consequence; whether downstream authority remains safe depends on how the malformed ownership is handled elsewhere, and it was not reproduced.

The [devtools owner](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/devtools/mod.rs>) registers both visualizations disabled by default, spawns the panel at Startup, renders it after rebase, and collects demand geometry in the shared World Draw set. The two [spatial debug adapters](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/devtools/panel/mod.rs>) and [demand World Draw collector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/devtools/world_draw/mod.rs>) are therefore consumers of shared developer tooling rather than standalone overlays. The panel selects only the first matching spatial anchor, while several simulation systems require a unique `Single`; multiple anchors would therefore be hidden by diagnostics rather than rejected. More materially, World Draw projects scope centers using `relative_native_bounded` (shared-leaf native units), then uses `half_extent_native` unchanged even though each scope documents that its extent belongs to `scope.scale()`. The renderer receives a box with center and extent from potentially different charts whenever leaf and scope scales differ. This is a source-level unit mismatch in cross-scale visualization; no rendered runtime output was inspected. The debug panel's fixed 620 px width is another unverified layout constraint.

The history is informative about verification loss: September 19 `da6c985` extracted the panel and World Draw from a single module; September 22 `9de6680` grew the Scale Layer/refinement model; October 5 `e987230` removed two mask tests that asserted full-domain coverage and order-independent inclusive ranges; October 6 `0e48843` renamed `UsfChartMask` to `UsfScaleSliceMask`, clarifying that this is a spatial partition mask rather than a chart abstraction. The current mask logic still implements those asserted properties, but no equivalent test is present in the inspected current source. The deletion records lost regression evidence, not a demonstrated mask failure.

### October 26 — voxel manifestation cleanly splits presentation from physical authority, with deferred retirement and stale profiling hooks

The [manifestation plugin](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/mod.rs>) says its scope directly: materializations with presentation geometry get disposable ECS shells; uniform air/solid facts remain store-backed; collision aggregates independently. The [frontier](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/frontier.rs>) derives six-face coarse/fine boundaries from active presentation-role manifestations and a semantic coverage revision. It recomputes only when that revision changes, then tests six same-scale neighboring materialization keys per ready cell. This is distinct from the physical collision aggregate and does not itself mean a neighboring fine cell is physically collision-ready.

The [lifecycle adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/lifecycle/mod.rs>) reads removal of `VoxelScaleRealization`, removes active registry mappings, hides each associated root, and recycles it up to a 512-shell pool before despawning overflow. The state is split among active entity/revision maps, dirty keys, a pool, component `active`, and visibility; source makes the transition understandable, but there is no identified owner-level transition record spanning presentation, collision and capability coverage. The current scope intentionally retires only presentation shells here; collision/coverage are separate consumers.

For presentation clipping, the [material plugin](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/material/mod.rs>) installs an extended material and orders buffer initialization before mesh rebuild, then syncs clips after capability/frontier refresh and view-anchor selection. The [asset model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/material/asset.rs>) keeps one base material plus opaque/translucent extended materials and an owned shader buffer per realization-local component. [Clip compaction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/material/clip.rs>) merges equal-size cells only when world, authority, fine scale and exposed-face mask match; the [sync system](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/material/systems.rs>) projects cached canonical boxes through the current view and publishes them to each scale material. The [WGSL adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/shader/refinement_clip.wgsl>) discards the parent material inside those projected boxes while retaining a one-fine-native support band at exposed faces. This is presentation-only aperture clipping; collision readiness and mesh contact authority remain elsewhere.

One exact cleanup residue is visible in the registry/rebuild boundary: five `record_*` methods are no-ops in the current [manifestation registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/mod.rs>), while the [rebuild path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/rebuild/mod.rs>) still calls them around spawn, rebuild, mesh publication, transform and visibility writes. History explains the residue rather than justifying it as active telemetry: `a91c670` adds Tracy pressure counters; `eaef138` removes their counters/plot system under a `first-touch-profiler-decontamination-v2` marker but retains empty inline hooks and all call sites. These calls should either regain an explicit instrumentation owner or be removed; currently they imply observability that does not exist.

The regression record is also specific. October 5 `e987230` removes the pool reuse test, the refinement interaction/view presentation-policy tests, and the runtime pose update test. The current inspected manifestation subtree has no replacement test module for frontier construction, clip-box compaction, role routing, pooling, or CPU/GPU clip synchronization; no tests were run in this audit. This is loss of focused evidence, not proof those implementations fail. The October 8 material extraction (`d806e3d`) reorganizes a roughly 590-line material file into asset, clip and system modules while carrying the same core policy into the current split; subsequent October 8 cleanup includes a frontier correction. See [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and the [voxel authority cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-manifestations-are-disposable-presentation-while-collision-and-coverage-have-separate-owners).

### October 26 — voxel realization is demand-driven, but some policy is stale and the view cap is advisory

The [realization facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/mod.rs>) explicitly mediates between generic spatial interest and voxel-specific capability scopes. The [domain](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/domain.rs>) independently configures scales that can realize, collide and edit; `contiguous` grants realization only, so fixtures must opt into physical roles. A repository-wide callsite search found no reader of `refinement_activation_native`: its getter and validated builder are currently a dead policy surface. The local-patch extent remains used as a fallback when a spatial source has no refinement footprint.

The [intent collector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/intent.rs>) combines marked spatial sources, active view demands, semantic celestial authorities and standalone realizations. Every requested voxel scale receives presentation; only the current `UsfPrimaryInteractionSlice::target_scale()` receives collision/editing, when the domain permits those capabilities. This lets a pending destination receive physical prep before the handoff commits. The [contact policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/contact.rs>) separates full-field signed clearance from exterior-shell clearance, expands work up to 1.5 seconds of closing travel plus a two-chunk guard, and centers exterior preparation on the nearest boundary rather than creating a body-sized dense volume. Inside the outer envelope (including cave void), it stays near the source; if no boundary can be sampled, it falls back to the local scope.

The view path estimates surface chunks against a nominal budget of 512, then selects a supported coarsest scale as a fallback even if no candidate met that estimate. Thus 512 is not a hard upper bound; the world-aligned cap box, padding and fallback can exceed it. The [intent/demand snapshot model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/model.rs>) sorts requests by realization/source/scale/roles and uses contiguous runs to avoid rescanning every request per resident world. The [resolver](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/demand.rs>) maps semantic authority+scale targets to disposable realization entities and drops unresolved targets. `VoxelScaleDomain::refinement_activation_native` is the more direct stale knob: no current callsite reads it, so changing it currently cannot alter activation behavior.

The surrounding lifecycle makes the ownership flow concrete. [Voxel schedule wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/mod.rs>) collects intent, reconciles realization containers, resolves entity-targeted demand, and then reconciles context residency in ordered Update stages. [Celestial realization reconciliation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_realization.rs>) parks temporarily undemanded containers and their bounded warm materialization cache, reanchors cache on translation, and retires/rebuilds when the semantic frame changes because the current canonical-axis lattice cannot honestly preserve arbitrary rotation. The [streaming demand system](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/systems.rs>) consumes the resolved scopes; [coverage publication](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/coverage.rs>) publishes readiness roles from dense/derived revisions and collision policy. This is a multi-stage capability pipeline, not a single “terrain loaded” flag.

History records a material architectural change. `20b9576` first extracts realization policy from the streaming-demand module; `9de6680` connects that scale policy to coverage and the broader voxel graph. The October 5 cleanup `e987230` removes the monolithic module's tests, including demand inside/far-outside behavior, tip-scale footprint conversion, parent-chain bounds, pending physical-target roles, and scale-role isolation. On October 8, `f588206` removes unconditional whole-body root demand and its test, along with the associated unused shell planning; this prevents a celestial authority alone from triggering dense whole-body materialization. Current visible terrain instead follows view footprint and local spatial/capability interest. The same day, `d806e3d` removes the standalone pinned-materialization intent path and builder helpers, leaving explicit spatial sources as the standalone demand path. These removals reduce implicit work and redundant pathways, but the current realization subtree has only one narrow role test; there is no current focused test covering boundary-contact geometry, view-budget fallback, target handoff, realization parking/reanchor or demand sorting. This is reduced verification evidence, not a demonstrated runtime defect. See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [realization cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-realization-turns-spatial-and-view-interest-into-scale-specific-capability-work).

Relocation has a distinct path from continuous flight: [ControlledRelocationRequest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/relocation.rs>) resolves one controlled semantic subject and can request view exponent, interaction scale and velocity semantics; when a destination is near a refinable hard-body, it asks the transition owner for REALIZATION and COLLISION coverage around destination boundary plus hull radius. This plan does not certify a swept route. [PrimaryBodyContext](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/travel/body.rs>) stores travel geometry/identity separately from gravity; the runtime can reset it to an unresolved default. These boundaries clarify that body selection, scale refinement, view-scale projection, Cruise speed/dropout and collision are coordinated data paths, not one “navigation ready” boolean.

### Camera, input, and HUD projection add a presentation shell around the same flight state

The player control path samples hardware once into a semantic `PlayerInputFrame` after cursor/focus arbitration; gameplay is inactive when the cursor is not captured, another interface claims focus, or an exclusive freecam owns input. The action vocabulary is a fixed 42-action bitset and the bindable physical vocabulary is keyboard plus three mouse buttons, not a general device/action graph ([input module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/mod.rs>), [action IDs](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/action.rs>), [button mapping](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/button.rs>), [frame sampling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/frame.rs>)). The binding resource initializes from compiled defaults and mutates in memory; this path shows no persistence. Its [binding facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/bindings/mod.rs>), [mutable model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/bindings/model.rs>) and [target/default registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/input/bindings/registry.rs>) distinguish semantic action binds from arbitrary console-command strings. The default `+jump` maps to Jump, Ascend and TakeOff together; `+duck` maps to Crouch and Descend; `+speed` maps to Sprint, Boost and FastModifier. Some user-facing help chooses the first binding only, while runtime input accepts all bindings.

The camera model supports FirstPerson, ThirdPerson and Orbit, but the input control is one F5 cycle, not a chooser or named-rig manager. Camera profile follows the viewed target; character first/third-person use controller-look, while the reference spacecraft uses physical ship attitude, horizon-stabilized chase and observer-owned orbit ([camera module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/mod.rs>), [camera/profile model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/model.rs>), [camera input](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/input.rs>)). Third-person zoom keeps authored distance, user offset and collision-resolved distance separate; the boom casts a sphere in the current physics slice and walks through active portals with an eight-hop cap ([third-person resolver](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/third_person/mod.rs>)). The physical camera derives vertical FOV from horizontal FOV and viewport aspect and scales its near plane from metres at the active Scale Slice ([presentation module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/presentation/mod.rs>), [FOV](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/presentation/fov.rs>)); its pose is composed from LocalViewTarget, PlayerAim and the target profile ([pose](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/presentation/pose.rs>)). A separate USF projection camera mirrors that local view from a bounded semantic anchor, while freecam has separate Exclusive/Passthrough control and Follow/Frozen/Disabled projection policies ([projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/presentation/projection.rs>), [freecam module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/freecam/mod.rs>), [freecam policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/freecam/policy.rs>)). Self-hiding is a primary-view RenderLayers projection policy and is restored for non-self/other views ([visibility](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/camera/presentation/visibility.rs>)). These are substantial functional foundations; they do not make camera selection or input discoverability complete.

Human control adaptation is separate from the reusable locomotion/flight contracts: [control facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/controls/mod.rs>) routes [regime/actuator toggles](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/controls/modes/mod.rs>), movement sampling and [view-intent adapters](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/controls/view/mod.rs>). The orbit pointer changes camera rotation; in inertial flight, ordinary PlayerAim look is deliberately ignored and ship attitude instead comes from separate semantic actions. Scroll is split among camera zoom, view-scale bias, throttle, pace and descend-context zoom. This is operationally rich but relies on modifier precedence and contextual help staying synchronized; the earlier review found the displayed hints use literal labels in places rather than the current binding model.

The flight HUD projects `FlightTelemetry` into two text wings, one central alert and a velocity marker. It refreshes textual metrics at 20 Hz, while alert and marker projection update every frame ([HUD module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/hud/mod.rs>), [formatting](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/hud/format.rs>), [fixed layout](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/hud/layout.rs>), [projection cadence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/hud/systems.rs>)). The wings are each 260 px, offset 125 px from screen center, use 15 px text, and include a Unicode diamond marker; this yields a fixed-width authored composition rather than a viewport-adaptive layout. Narrow-window clipping, glyph coverage, visual balance and actual legibility remain unassessed because the game UI was not launched. The `SURF READY/PENDING` label is sourced from a nearby coverage probe, not proof of a clear full approach path; the alert logic likewise formats telemetry and does not itself enforce landing/collision policy. This is a useful example of correctly separated model/presentation code with a remaining product-integrity risk at the meaning of the displayed status.

## October 26 — navigation flight recorder is useful but local, ephemeral telemetry

The navigation module owns a bounded `NavigationFlightRecorder`, initialized enabled with a 160-sample ring. It samples the one `LocalControlSubject` every 0.5 seconds and on changes to interaction scale/request, interaction affinity, refinement target, view scale, locomotion regime or motion kernel. A sample retains canonical position, subject/current/requested scales, view exponent, primary-body clearance and a three-bit realization/presentation/collision coverage summary; `navtrace [count|clear|on|off|status]` exposes or resets the in-memory history ([resource and registration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/mod.rs#L25-L56>), [sample policy and stored fields](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/devtools.rs#L11-L110>), [sampling and coverage projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/devtools.rs#L230-L327>), [command surface](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/console_commands/observation/runtime.rs#L5-L50>)). The October 1 performance change deliberately moved canonical projection and the three coverage queries behind the sample/change gate, rather than paying those costs on every Update; this is documented intent and code structure, not measured profiling evidence ([`8bea1d67`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/8bea1d67b4b0084c2ccd424199a484d561ecfdb2)).

This is a concrete domain-specific debugging tool, not a durable flight recorder or the shared Vapor console/telemetry stream. It exists only in the game process, loses old samples at the ring bound or on restart, and observes exactly one locally controlled subject plus one primary-body audit; it cannot compare multiple subjects or prove that an entire route had collision support. The command formats a bounded selection as text; no serialization, export, cross-session correlation, or shared-service projection appears in the inspected path. This narrows the claim that spatial instrumentation is absent, while preserving the larger integration gap: the useful trace is bespoke to navigation and is not joined to operation-origin logging, the Vapor console record schema, or a reproducible scenario capture. No navigation trace was collected or runtime inspected in this review.

## October 26 — voxel cancellation discards results; it does not stop compute

The current voxel worker boundary separates admission, execution, result publication and ECS task lifetime. Admission counts queued plus running jobs per lane, with a limit of twice worker capacity for Generation and Derivation and one for PresentationPlanning. A compute lease begins only when a worker starts the closure and releases running/outstanding counts when that closure exits; the ticket independently controls whether its result remains observable ([admission and lease](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/admission.rs>), [ticket](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/ticket.rs>), [executor](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/executor.rs>)). Dropping a stale generation or surface task drops its ticket and suppresses publication, but does not interrupt a queued/running closure; the closure still consumes its bounded slot until it exits. That is a stale-result safety contract, not preemptive cancellation.

There are two scheduling layers. Generation re-ranks work across voxel worlds each round and limits each world's contribution by its load budget; surface derivation separately selects dirty addresses by streaming rank. The shared executor then arbitrates three lanes with a fixed Generation/Derivation/PresentationPlanning/Generation/Derivation service wheel, rotating critical lanes, and a maximum four-job critical burst before normal work is served when available ([generation scheduling and stale retirement](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/mod.rs>), [surface scheduling and stale retirement](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/async_pipeline/mod.rs>), [queue policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/queue.rs>)). This is meaningful bounded/fair service machinery, but its rank is local to each layer; it is not one end-to-end deadline scheduler. Tracy reports capacity, running/outstanding/queued work and per-lane mean duration, but does not expose per-job queue age or result wait-to-publication time ([worker profiling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/profiling.rs>)). The source establishes policy and observability boundaries, not measured starvation, latency, or frame impact. No worker trace or runtime experiment was performed.

## October 26 — the in-game editor has reusable semantic inspectors, but they are not the Vapor IDE

The in-game editor is not just an egui wrapper around raw ECS reflection. Its shell explicitly separates the Bevy Inspector tab from semantic Structure navigation, domain inspector sections, contextual Gizmos and the Game viewport ([module ownership map](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/mod.rs>), [docked tabs and view setup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/mod.rs>), [semantic inspector/gizmo panels](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/inspector/mod.rs>)). A type can opt into `Inspect` and publish static field metadata through visitors; applications explicitly register types; egui hosts separately register a default or named widget for a Rust type. Widget resolution prefers the named override, then the type's default. This makes the model presentation-independent and permits value controls to be customized without giving the model egui callbacks ([metadata/access vocabulary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>), [visitor contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/traits/mod.rs>), [explicit type registration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/registry/mod.rs>), [type-directed widget registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/registry/mod.rs>)). It is a concrete reusable semantic-inspector facility, not merely aspirational UI.

Mutation authority is deliberately richer than a read-only/editable switch. The visitor's direct mutable route only exposes fields marked `Direct`; `Validated`, `Transactional` and `Command` access remain observable through that route and require an adapter. The in-game semantic Inspector instead draws a frame of typed sections, emits `InspectEditRequest`/`InspectActionRequest`, and lets the owning domain validate and commit them. Generic Transform editing follows the same principle: visibility does not grant write permission, parented Transforms stay read-only without a parent-aware adapter, and approved edits become requests ([access modes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>), [frame request contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/frame/mod.rs>), [request-emitting semantic widgets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/sections/mod.rs>), [Transform authority](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/inspector/mod.rs>), [gizmo adapter/scheduling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/mod.rs>)). This is an important design precedent for the planned semantic editor: preserve meaning and ownership separately from presentation and mutation.

There are also strict boundaries. The runtime `InspectTypeRegistry` stores Rust `TypeId` registrations inside the Loo-Cast Bevy `App`; `InspectionFrame`, `DeveloperFocus`, `StructureSelection`, widget registries and edit messages are process-local ECS state. Nothing inspected exports these types through Vapor's local service, maps them to Rust Analyzer symbols, or lets the Vapor IDE register them. They therefore demonstrate a strong in-process extension pattern, not a cross-process IDE semantic-object protocol. The editor also has two compatible inspection paths: visitor-backed direct editing for explicitly `Direct` fields, and request-backed semantic panels for fields requiring domain policy. Both are deliberate authority-aware mechanisms; neither should be mistaken for a universal reflected mutation API.

The check uncovered an important verification regression in this facility's own history. On September 19, `da6c985` extracted inspection frame, metadata, model, registry and visitor modules and added focused tests. Those tests exercised the `Inspect` derive's field metadata, `skip`, widget/range metadata and the rule that only Direct fields receive mutable visitor access. `1f13176` separately extracted the editor shell, semantic inspector/gizmo panels and type-directed egui widget registry. On October 5, `e987230` deletes the 80-line inspection test module and the 13-line widget test module; a current search of `devtools/inspect` and `inspect_ui` finds no remaining `#[test]` coverage for these contracts. No corresponding replacement was found in the Vapor macro crate or current game source. This documents lost regression coverage; it does not prove the code is broken or explain why the owner removed the tests. The October 9 hierarchy update adds `EditorGroupOf` as a semantic editor-only relationship, explicitly avoiding Transform parenting and simulation ownership. That choice is a small but concrete example of the editor maintaining a UI organization graph separate from runtime spatial hierarchy. See [`da6c985`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/da6c985a09f763bf111339837bc9115a3981ae06), [`1f13176`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/1f13176b8a94163dd6242575fe040b8f5455914a), [`e987230`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), and [`46e1eac`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/46e1eacb33c18f6ff274f4d6acf6c98f45fe87b6).

The script workbench is another in-game editor surface, but it is separate from the Rust semantic inspector: the October 2 addition (`05f5a55`, expanded/refactored by `1f6d356`) created a file-oriented Rhai workbench; on October 5 (`e987230`) its host, storage and UI responsibilities were split into modules while the Inspector tests were removed. The current workbench's one live host hook is documented separately in the [scripting/Rhai review](#october-25--the-in-game-rhai-workbench-executes-a-narrow-committed-hook). Neither the workbench nor the semantic inspector is the future Vapor IDE itself, and the project has not yet joined these authoring models through one typed semantic-object contract. No game editor, Rhai workbench, or tests were run for this review.

## October 26 — the Wheel Salvage graph proves a hand-wired static composition, not generic Pack realization

The current `Vapor-Examples` workspace contains six authored content projects: two reusable Crates, a terminal Engine, a Game, a Game Mod, and a non-default Packagepack. Its Packagepack Cargo binary directly depends on the Engine, Game and Mod by local path; the Game depends on the Engine and `wheel-rules`, the Mod depends on the Game, and `wheel-rules` depends on `wheel-core` ([workspace and target list](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/Workspace.vapor.toml#L3-L39>), [Packagepack Cargo graph](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/Cargo.toml#L1-L17>), [Game Cargo dependencies](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-game/Cargo.toml#L1-L11>), [Mod dependency](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/tiny-game-mod/Cargo.toml#L1-L10>), [rules-to-core dependency](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/wheel-rules/Cargo.toml#L1-L10>)). At runtime the Packagepack entrypoint passes an installation closure to the Engine, and that closure installs the selected Game and Mod ([entrypoint](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/src/main.rs#L1-L5>), [composition function](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/src/lib.rs#L1-L7>)). This is a real statically linked example composition, but the chosen graph is duplicated in hand-authored Cargo dependencies and Rust calls. Changing Pack manifests alone does not synthesize a different executable graph. The focused test asserts that this specific Game+Mod produces nine sectors, but it was not run here.

The Vapor manifests independently declare typed identities and edges: Game requires this Engine and `wheel-rules`, Packagepack selects the Engine and Game plus the Mod, and the Mod depends on the Game. They also declare Steam PublishedFileIds and `visibility = "public"` for each content item ([Game manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-game/Game.vapor.toml#L3-L25>), [Engine manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/terminal-engine/Engine.vapor.toml#L3-L16>), [Packagepack manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/Packagepack.vapor.toml#L3-L30>), [Mod manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/tiny-game-mod/Game-Mod.vapor.toml#L3-L20>), [Crate manifests](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/wheel-core/Crate.vapor.toml#L3-L16>, </home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/wheel-rules/Crate.vapor.toml#L3-L21>)). The October 21 history matters: `07ae8f0` converted old generic `Vapor.toml` files to the typed artifact manifests and expanded the wheel; `aca638c` completed the private Workshop graph; `c157496` added a runnable Packagepack-owned Cargo binary; and `80a30d2` changed content versions to alpha `0.5.0` and declared the Workshop items public. These are repository declarations and historical changes, not a live Steam query or proof the current depots contain compatible executable/library artifacts.

The two version families are intentionally distinct in the current docs: Vapor content manifests inherit workspace version `0.5.0`, while Rust package versions and exact Cargo path-dependency requirements remain `0.1.0` ([workspace version and declared Linux/Windows targets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/Workspace.vapor.toml#L3-L18>), [Packagepack Cargo versions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/Cargo.toml#L1-L10>), [version policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/README.md#L18-L20>)). This is not, by itself, an inconsistency: Cargo crate identity and Vapor content identity are separate version domains. It does mean a successful Cargo build would not alone establish that the released Vapor content dependency graph resolves or that both target payloads are staged correctly. No Steam state, artifact receipt, cross-target build or runtime launch was checked.

The remaining Engine and Game source clarifies what the example is actually proving. `terminal-engine` owns Crossterm acquisition, terminal lifecycle, a Bevy `App`, a small ordered Configure/Input/Simulate/Present schedule, variable measured frame delta with a 33 ms pacing target, and a plain-character framebuffer; it exposes game-neutral key/input/time/frame resources and `try_run` so setup errors can be returned ([Engine host and public API](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/terminal-engine/src/lib.rs#L1-L239>), [runtime loop and terminal session](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/terminal-engine/src/lib.rs#L241-L547>), [Engine binary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/terminal-engine/src/main.rs#L1-L3>)). The host is deliberately compact, but its “frame” is not a fixed simulation step: elapsed time is measured and passed through while sleeping only caps the nominal render cadence. It redraws every row each tick, has no style/color model, and counts Unicode scalar values rather than terminal display-cell widths when centering/clipping; those are confirmed source limits, not observed rendering failures. The Engine binary is only a three-line wrapper around the same library runtime.

The Game owns an eight-sector weighted wheel and a compact Expedition state machine; input requests spin/extract/restart, animation advances before outcome resolution, and the Game exposes one registration set where a statically linked Mod can add a sector ([wheel state and run rules](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-game/src/lib.rs#L17-L241>), [seeded installation, schedule integration, input and presentation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-game/src/lib.rs#L243-L363>), [mod registration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/tiny-game-mod/src/lib.rs#L1-L15>)). `wheel-core` and `wheel-rules` keep reusable identifiers and wheel/loot structures outside the Engine/Game runtime, while the Mod's test demonstrates the intended extension seam ([identifier types](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/wheel-core/src/lib.rs#L1-L34>), [domain types and operations](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/wheel-rules/src/lib.rs#L1-L83>), [mod composition assertion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/tiny-game-mod/src/lib.rs#L17-L33>)). The abstractions are intentionally narrow; for example, `GameModeId` has no current consumer, and wheel outcomes are an ordered vector with no validation against duplicate IDs or a missing table reference. More importantly, no explicit ordering is declared among multiple `WheelGameSet::Register` contributors, so registration order is not yet a stated extension contract; this can affect sector ordering even when the same sectors are present. The tests exercise deterministic game rules, synthetic input and schedule integration, but this audit did not run them. This slice cites every executable source file in the six-project example; it does not establish the published Workshop payloads, cross-platform terminal behavior, or arbitrary mod compatibility.
## October 26 — content identity has two lexical contracts

At the inspected Client checkout (`5743065`), `VaporId::as_str()` is documented as returning canonical ID text, but its constructor only rejects an empty string or whitespace; `ContentReference` deserialization routes through that same check. It does not normalize case, constrain separators, or establish one segment grammar ([identity type and constructor](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/identity.rs#L10-L25>), [reference validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/identity.rs#L79-L120>)).

Source discovery has a narrower authoring contract. It rejects explicit `id` fields and constructs a content identity as `{source-root-prefix}/{local-name}`; global and local names are trimmed and limited to lowercase ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_` ([ID inference](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/manifest.rs#L343-L390>), [name validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/manifest.rs#L537-L591>)). Thus IDs discovered from source cannot use every spelling accepted by the general API/persistence identity type. The observed route may be intentional if source-generated IDs are a constrained subset of opaque ecosystem IDs, but the distinction is not represented as separate types or documented as an explicit policy. The word “canonical” currently overstates what the shared constructor guarantees.

This contract predates the shared Client extraction. `fedee52` (September 4) introduced `VaporId` with the non-empty/no-whitespace rule; `c65f1e7` (September 5) renamed `ResolvedContentId` to `ContentVersionId` and clarified that exact identity is independent of resolution; `f9e8b13` (October 18) moved the type into `vapor_content` while introducing the current provider source-manifest parser. The history shows continuity of the permissive constructor and a later adjacent, stricter discovery grammar—not an October 18 invention of the identity concept.

The material question is whether Vapor IDs have one global canonical syntax, with source names as a subset, or whether provider/source identity is a distinct namespace that needs an explicit conversion/alias rule. Rename and workspace-move stability also remain open: source-derived IDs include the source prefix and local name. This is a confirmed contract distinction and a design gap; it is not evidence of an exploit, a failed lookup, or runtime damage. No tests, builds or runtime actions were performed.

## October 26 — Workshop review protects a local stage, but receipts do not identify a release

The current service does have an explicit build-before-review step. A `Stage` operation marks itself Building, calls the managed authored-workspace build for the selected target triples, then changes to Staging and asks the application to package the selected source artifact ([service sequence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/workshop.rs#L1260-L1303>)). The lower-level provider package function does not invoke Cargo itself: it validates source, resets the app-owned package output directory, copies the authored tree, stages already-built binaries/libraries under target-specific directories, writes one deployed role manifest and computes a tree fingerprint ([package operation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/packaging.rs#L74-L124>), [tree and runtime staging](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/packaging.rs#L275-L315>)). This distinction resolves the apparent “no build before Workshop” reading: the typed service Stage path builds; direct provider packaging is a separate lower-level operation with prebuilt-output assumptions.

The review object is meaningfully specific. It includes source artifact ID/version, Steam app and PublishedFile IDs, title/visibility/dependencies, target string, staged path, file/byte counts, paths and the package-tree fingerprint ([preview projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/publishing.rs#L579-L624>)). Publish re-stages the package and compares the preview, then the provider stages again, copies that package to a reviewed temporary directory, compares the expected fingerprint, emits the SteamCMD VDF and accepts a successful SteamCMD exit as upload success ([application confirmation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/publishing.rs#L626-L683>), [provider recheck and upload](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/workshop.rs#L505-L628>), [SteamCMD exit contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/workshop.rs#L732-L755>)). For item creation, the returned PublishedFileId is read from the generated VDF and written back into the authored source manifest ([ID update](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/workshop.rs#L878-L905>)). These are real protections against accidental local drift between review and upload.

The staged folder is not a binary-only payload: `copy_tree` copies the source artifact tree while excluding only `.git`, `target`, and `output`, then overlays built runtime outputs and the deployed manifest ([stage](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/packaging.rs#L275-L303>), [exclusions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content.rs#L2451-L2453>)). This can serve the owner's Packagepack source-plus-runnable goal, but it applies identically to all kinds. The current generic publisher can therefore stage source and executable/library payload for non-Pack content and Pack kinds alike; it does not implement the owner's kind-sensitive rule that Packs are manifests while reusable Content owns compiled implementations. That remains a semantic contract gap, not proof any specific uploaded item contains unwanted files.

The review fingerprint is `vapor-fnv1a-64-v1`, a non-cryptographic tree consistency hash over relative paths and bytes ([algorithm and traversal](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content.rs#L53-L66>), [hash implementation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content.rs#L2362-L2392>)). It is useful for detecting ordinary stage changes but is not a signed release identity or tamper-proof provenance record. Durable state is weaker than the in-memory review: `PackageReport` exposes its fingerprint, but the `package` receipt stores only the package path and target label; `OperationReceipt` itself has generic action/ID/status/second-resolution timestamp/free-form detail fields ([package receipt](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/packaging.rs#L109-L124>), [receipt schema and writer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/storage.rs#L90-L99>), [receipt path/write](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/storage.rs#L209-L236>)). The Workshop receipt includes the local fingerprint and script path but not a source revision, manifest digest, toolchain/build configuration, complete target set, remote content digest or Steam item revision. No remote read-back occurs in the checked publish path; `uploaded` follows SteamCMD's successful process status.

There is also a narrow receipt collision: the filename is `{timestamp-seconds}-{action}-{slug(id)}` and the writer uses `fs::write`, so two writes for the same action and artifact within one second target the same path and the later replaces the earlier. The source proves this overwrite behavior; no collision was reproduced. In the Stage→Publish flow, repeated `package` receipts for the same artifact are possible on both sides of a review, so the record design does not guarantee a durable per-operation history even when the review/upload itself succeeds.

Chronologically, the end-to-end-shaped lifecycle began as a 2,193-line `content.rs` monolith in July (`8464f463`), combining local packaging, install/cache state and SteamCMD operations. The October 18 provider extraction and October 19 shared-service move split the implementation and added an explicit Stage/Publish operation boundary, but the result is still a local review protocol plus a generic Steam upload, not one authoritative release record joining typed graph, source provenance, build target/toolchain, remote item revision and Registry/Identity authority. The accepted “Registry catalog; Identity authorizes” direction remains unimplemented here. All findings are source- and history-backed; no builds, Steam operations or runtime behavior were exercised.



## October 26 — spatial transitions are canonical transactions with backend-specific admission

The transition facility is a concrete authority boundary, not a universal scale scheduler. Callers submit either a one-shot `relocate` request or continually refresh an `UsfInteractionRequirement`; the resource keeps those in separate stores. For a subject with multiple queued relocations, `take_latest_relocation_for` consumes the newest and discards the older requests. Capability planners can inspect the latest pending relocation before it commits, so destination demand can be generated while the old chart remains active ([transition module wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/mod.rs>), [intent queue and public request shape](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/intent.rs#L34-L225>), [pending destination demand](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/demand/systems.rs#L57-L115>)).

Admission has two distinct gates. Requested capability roles are checked against the destination `UsfScaleCoverageSnapshot`; a miss retains and requeues a one-shot request, while continuous requirements must be republished by their provider. For physical coarsening, a separate physics provider blocks continuous interaction handoffs when a destination-scale hull probe overlaps existing collision geometry. It also delays the first probe frame so newly created acceleration-structure entries can appear. That guard only iterates continuous interaction requirements, and its own module explicitly limits itself to coarsening; it is not a generic relocation collision veto or a finer-scale contact-transfer protocol ([admission and wait fingerprint](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/admission.rs#L1-L231>), [coarsening guard](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/interaction_handoff.rs#L1-L106>)). This distinction may be correct for teleport-like relocation, but the source does not state a general safety policy for every relocation producer. Do not equate “coverage-gated” with “overlap-vetoed.”

Before readiness completes, `UsfPrimaryInteractionSlice` records the requested target separately from its committed current scale. Capability/demand consumers can plan for the target while runtime transforms still use the old chart. On admission, one system updates the semantic `UsfPosition`, re-expresses all projections belonging to the subject at the destination scale, applies an explicit velocity policy (`PreserveCanonical`, `PreserveNative`, or `Zero`), reanchors the runtime chart at the canonical position and emits `UsfSpatialTransitionApplied`. Voxel collision aggregates consume that event and rebuild their runtime transforms; the schedule then refreshes backend acceleration data. This is a strong transactional shape across authority and projections, although the downstream work is distributed among event consumers rather than enclosed by one rollback-capable transaction ([interaction current/requested state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/interaction/mod.rs#L52-L105>), [apply and velocity policies](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/apply.rs#L1-L201>), [spatial schedule DAG](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/mod.rs#L130-L189>), [collision aggregate refresh](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/manifestation/collision/mod.rs#L220-L269>)).

Two boundaries deserve follow-up rather than an immediate defect label. First, motion reanchors are selected before continuous interaction requirements; admitting one cancels the pending interaction handoff for that frame. If a subject repeatedly needs an unrepresentable runtime step and reanchor, this ordering could defer a scale handoff indefinitely. Whether the movement policy can produce that persistent state is not established here. Second, the transition applier takes the first `UsfSpatialAnchor` it finds, while floating-origin rebase refuses multiple anchors and the Game control layer separately audits exactly-one local anchors. That makes the low-level transition resource single-focus in practice; multi-observer use would need an explicit chart/subject selection model. The control audit is evidence for the intended current invariant, not proof that every temporary ECS state is safe ([motion-reanchor precedence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/admission.rs#L77-L180>), [single-anchor rebase check](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/chart/rebase.rs#L15-L48>), [local-control invariant](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/control/runtime.rs#L215-L279>)).

Verification is narrower than the architecture claim: the demand collector has a focused test proving a pending relocation causes destination coverage demand, but the inspected transition modules have no local tests for queue coalescing, failed-coverage retry, guard behavior, velocity conversion, multi-projection commit, or event-driven backend refresh. The October 5 `e987230` deletion removed older spatial rebase tests, not a transition-integration suite. No build, test or runtime scenario was run in this research pass. Consequently this boundary is source-traced and partially unit-tested at its demand edge; it is not proof that high-speed Moon arrival, safe collision handoff or repeated-reanchor liveness works end to end.

## October 26 — engine diagnostics publish typed snapshots through an optional, lossy telemetry bridge

The current engine diagnostics plugin is separate from developer UI: it samples frame/system and physics data every 0.25 seconds, ECS/world structure every 5 seconds, and publishes only when `VAPOR_TELEMETRY_ADDR` is present and a broker connection succeeds. Runtime metrics include FPS/frame time, process/system CPU and memory, physics step/collision/solver/contact/body values; world metrics include entity/archetype/component counts and estimated inline component bytes, with a snapshot of the largest 24 components. That memory estimate is inline ECS component layout multiplied by instances; it excludes heap-owned allocations. Vapor tags each event with source `spacetime-engine`, timestamps it, and brokers it over localhost into the active development session; the Studio Devtools page looks for this source's frame/CPU/memory keys. The bridge is bounded and lossy under pressure, so missing samples do not imply the game never produced them. These are source-level transport and sampling contracts, not a proven live session, correct graph, or Tracy capture ([engine plugin and cadence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/mod.rs#L33-L88>), [world/inline-memory semantics](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/world/mod.rs#L1-L76>), [metric projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/telemetry/mod.rs#L1-L201>), [source-tagged event and bounded emitter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_telemetry/src/lib.rs#L29-L44>, [emitter queue](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_telemetry/src/lib.rs#L217-L262>), [lossy session bridge](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/development_telemetry.rs#L10-L89>), [Studio live metric keys](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_devtools/src/app.rs#L216-L236>)).

The diagnostic lineage is a redesign rather than simple continuation. September 13 `78354d3` replaced an older observability/telemetry registry with this typed runtime snapshot; September 18 `7f52d4a` connected it to Vapor telemetry and added process/world sampling; September 19 `c187ac7` split the module and added an eight-line low-FPS test, and `4c9721f` added physics measurements. On October 5 `e987230` removed that diagnostics test; the current helper remains but has no checked-in focused test in its module. The old observability architecture's generic `DebugMetrics` registry/unit labels and older longer FPS history are not the current contract. This history explains why data exists without making UI/session behavior proven. Nothing here establishes that `--profiling` alone starts telemetry: the service bridge polls an active Vapor development session and consumes its broker address, while the Engine's emitter is optional. The Engine attempts its producer connection once during plugin construction; absent env configuration or startup-time connection failure is not retried by this plugin. No build, test, launch, or capture was run.

## October 26 — portal apertures are realized by rebuilding the authoritative collider

`physics::collision_topology` separates authored stencil intent from Avian's derived collider. Portal placement fits a rectangular aperture to an immutable clip source; the fit only accepts cuboid faces at unit host scale, snaps orientation to a face axis and quarter-turn, and clamps the aperture inside the face. A change-driven index groups enabled stencils by target and sorts them by entity bits before fingerprinting, so unchanged hosts avoid rebuilds ([fit policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/stencil_fit/mod.rs#L1-L94>), [target index and fingerprint](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/state.rs#L42-L139>)).

The CSG routine subtracts each oriented rectangular prism from convex pieces by splitting against six planes, then turns the remainder into convex hull colliders and, when needed, an Avian compound collider. This is the actual collider supplied to contacts, character casts and ordinary spatial queries; the system does not rely on portal-specific query filters. The integration is concrete and useful, but deliberately narrow: the only source primitive is a cuboid, moving/non-unit-scale support geometry is not supported, and no input-count cap is apparent for the cut loop ([source type](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/source.rs#L1-L32>), [CSG subtraction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/csg/mod.rs#L1-L120>), [ECS rebuild](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/systems.rs#L12-L90>)).

Failure favors retaining solid collision: unsupported transforms or an empty/invalid hull result return `None`, and the caller substitutes the original cuboid collider. That is a conservative physics fallback, but it can leave a visually open portal blocked; no diagnostic is emitted by this fallback path. A lifecycle edge is also visible: reconciliation tracks removed `CollisionStencil` components, but not removed `CollisionClipSource` components. If a host keeps its collider after its clip-source component is removed, the already-rewritten collider has no source-driven path back to its original shape. Current inspected portal/geometry call sites do not establish that this sequence occurs in gameplay, so this is a conditional cleanup gap, not a reproduced failure. The module defines no local unit tests; no build, collision scenario, perf bound, or runtime portal traversal was verified here.

The history anchors the implementation to September 12 `62414407`, which introduced CSG, source geometry and stencil clipping as one 588-line addition. Later commits made small CSG corrections and reorganized the file into submodules; the behavior remained a focused portal-support mechanism rather than a general collision-boolean API. This strengthens the existing conclusion that portal collision has a real backend realization, while leaving geometry breadth, failure observability, lifecycle restoration and runtime safety unproven.

## October 26 — Scale-Slice collision filters have an implicit global case

`UsfPhysicsSliceQuery` resolves a collider's slice from its direct `UsfScaleLayer` or its attached rigid body's layer. `filter_for_slices` excludes entities only when that lookup succeeds and the resolved slice is outside the requested mask; a collider with no resolvable layer is absent from the exclusion set and therefore remains visible to every scale-filtered spatial query. The ECS metadata sync also skips unresolved colliders rather than rejecting or classifying them. The ordinary Avian pair hook has the same incomplete-state policy: it vetoes only when both collider scales resolve and differ ([query filter and metadata sync](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/slice/mod.rs#L1-L97>), [pair hook](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/topology/hooks/mod.rs#L1-L59>)).

This is not just hypothetical input: authored geometry spawns solid colliders without adding a `UsfScaleLayer`, and the generic `Chunkloading Cube` gameplay item spawns a dynamic USF manifestation with a collider but no scale layer. These entities therefore have no explicit partition identity at their creation sites ([authored geometry spawn](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/runtime/spawning/mod.rs#L5-L92>), [chunkloading cube spawn](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/chunkloading_cube/mod.rs#L80-L150>)). The source proves that missing scale metadata behaves as query-visible-to-all and is not rejected; whether these particular items are intended global colliders or accidentally cross-slice is not stated. A universal collider may be a valid capability, but the current API expresses it through missing data rather than an explicit global/universal policy, so omitted tagging silently widens physical interaction.

The history shows the partition intent becoming explicit on September 26 `e97d0232`, which introduced the Scale-Slice filter adapter, then October's cleanup extracted topology hooks into their own module. The current source does provide exact slice identity, pair filtering and tool-visible ECS membership, but those protections are opt-in by correctly resolving a layer. This narrows the claim that “collision is Scale-Slice partitioned”: it is partitioned for tagged collider pairs and queries, with an undocumented unknown/global fallback. No cross-scale contact scenario or tagged-versus-untagged query test was run.

## October 26 — the character motor is a custom SI-policy adapter around Avian queries

The playable Character kernel does not delegate movement to an Avian character component: `CharacterMotor` requires a kinematic body with custom position/velocity integration, and its fixed-step adapter resolves an SI-authored `CharacterMovementConfig` into the current Scale Slice's native units, then uses Avian `MoveAndSlide` and shape queries. The motor owns velocity integration, grounded-state transitions, jump input consumption and motion response; Avian supplies query/move primitives and rigid-body contacts.
