Penetration is reconciled before intent movement while preserving tangential/outward velocity; grounding scans all hits and selects the nearest walkable support; a step route is attempted only on grounded planar movement and wins only if it produces more planar progress ([motor/plugin contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/plugin.rs#L20-L100>), [chart-resolved policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/config.rs#L1-L157>), [fixed-tick orchestration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/mod.rs#L1-L216>), [grounding](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/grounding/mod.rs#L1-L180>), [step selection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/stepping/mod.rs#L1-L128>)).

The `source_2013` preset is explicitly a lineage and tuning starting point, not exact Source parity: the config documents stronger ground friction, a higher jump and a response multiplier that maps Earth gravity to a 20.32 m/s² fall response. Fields are public and resolution clamps only selected inputs; no invariant-enforcing constructor or complete finite/range validation was found. Groundedness has one source of truth (`contact.is_some()`), but that contact stores only collider entity and normal; the current motor does not consume platform velocity or a semantic support owner. Dynamic-body interaction is an arcade adapter: outgoing pushes use an 80 kg effective character mass and 0.35 impulse scale, while incoming normal-impulse response is capped at a 12 m/s delta. Those are deliberate game-policy values, not reciprocal rigid-body simulation ([movement preset and validation surface](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/config.rs#L17-L157>), [ground state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/state.rs#L1-L116>), [push adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/pushing/mod.rs#L1-L150>)).

This decomposition has useful ownership boundaries, but its regression evidence was cut back. September 12 `9a0ce7f9` raised ground friction from 4 to 8. October 5 `e987230f` deleted ten inline character tests: two for historical gravity response and SI/chart conversion, four for gravity/control-frame settling, and four for acceleration, air cap, friction and vector rejection. The present `physics/character` subtree has no inline tests. No movement, scale-slice, step, moving-support, invalid-config or dynamic-push runtime case was exercised in this review. The deletion is evidence loss, not proof that the implementation is broken; the owner-reported Moon-approach failure belongs to the distinct `InertialFlight` path, not this on-foot motor.

## October 26 — gravity is canonical, but its runtime sample is a pre-fixed-loop snapshot

The physics plugin explicitly disables Avian's uniform gravity. `RadialGravitySource` stores canonical radius and surface gravity; its direct evaluator uses an interior linear field and exterior inverse-square field, while `GravityFieldQuery` sums every source in canonical `DVec3`. Its `field_scale` selects a numerically bounded chart for displacement conversion; it does not decide which subsystem owns gravity. This replaces an older context/cache gravity path, but the current per-sample cost scales with source count and no hierarchy or source broad phase is present ([backend ownership](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/mod.rs#L31-L83>), [radial source](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/source.rs#L1-L78>), [direct summation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/query.rs#L1-L105>)).

The important cadence distinction is schedule placement. Gravity projection and character reference-frame resolution are in `RunFixedMainLoop`'s `BeforeFixedMainLoop` phase, then Avian character motors consume their `GravitySample` in `FixedUpdate`. Bevy documents this pre-loop set as running exactly once per frame, while `FixedMain` runs zero to many times per frame; the sample is therefore reused during catch-up ticks, not sampled on every physics tick despite `GravitySample`'s “fixed-tick” documentation ([Bevy 0.19.1 schedule contract](https://docs.rs/bevy_app/0.19.1/bevy_app/enum.RunFixedMainLoopSystems.html), [fixed schedule contract](https://docs.rs/bevy_app/0.19.1/bevy_app/struct.FixedMain.html)). The Game deliberately orders orbit propagation before gravity sampling, then navigation/flight decisions, then character-frame synchronization, and finally character intent before entering the fixed loop. This gives one coherent pre-physics snapshot, but makes gravity and gravity-aligned `up` piecewise constant across catch-up substeps. The source establishes the cadence; its movement/error impact has not been measured ([gravity schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/mod.rs#L27-L64>), [character frame schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/plugin.rs#L61-L87>), [cross-domain Game ordering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/mod.rs#L103-L125>), [fixed-step consumer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/mod.rs#L59-L111>)).

Character movement is likewise an Engine-owned adapter rather than Avian's stock character controller: `CharacterMotor` requires a kinematic body with custom position/velocity integration, and the fixed system uses Avian `MoveAndSlide` plus a Scale-Slice filter, gravity/config policy, grounding, step selection and separately emitted dynamic-body pushes. Stable locomotion-up, transient control orientation and physical transform are intentionally distinct, allowing topology-mapped roll to settle without replacing gravity/jump semantics. This is a carefully decomposed foundation, but adds multiple state owners that must remain synchronized at the game schedule boundary. The inspected character and gravity modules contain no inline unit tests; no catch-up schedule, multi-source accuracy, load scaling or runtime body behavior was verified. The direct-gravity pivot in `b454b6f7` and later shared-sample ordering are documented in the earlier commit ledger; current code confirms that the direct evaluator survived, not that its performance or cadence is adequate at scale.


## October 26 — combat and health look generic, but remain in the Engine crate's Game tree

`CombatPlugin` owns projectile movement, hit discovery and conversion from `Hit` to `health::Damage`; `HealthPlugin` owns health mutation and the alive-to-dead transition. The Game schedule orders collision before consequence and consequence before damage application ([Game schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/mod.rs#L103-L125>), [combat registration and ordering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/mod.rs#L1-L100>), [health ownership](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/mod.rs#L1-L112>), [damage application](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/damage/mod.rs#L1-L22>)). This is a useful request/effect boundary, but does not establish an extracted reusable Vapor Engine artifact.

Projectile motion is endpoint-tested: each update advances by `velocity * dt`, then checks whether the new endpoint lies inside candidate Avian colliders. There is no segment sweep, so sufficiently fast travel can cross a sufficiently thin collider between observations. That is a source-derived tunneling risk, not a reproduced failure ([projectile movement and hit query](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/projectile/mod.rs#L1-L81>)). Candidates are constrained by scale and instigator, then the nearest collider center among containing colliders wins. `DamageableBounds` marks eligibility; collider geometry decides containment, while the marker's extents position the health bar ([damage adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/damage/mod.rs#L1-L19>), [world health presentation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/world/mod.rs#L1-L80>)).

The generic-looking Health plugin also unconditionally installs a thermal-injury bridge described in code as a test-game adapter; it converts temperature injury into generic damage ([thermal bridge](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/thermal_injury/mod.rs#L1-L47>)). Health construction panics for invalid maxima, whereas applied damage rejects non-finite/non-positive values and dead targets. Presentation reads health from semantic owners rather than duplicating it on runtime manifestations. No tests were found in either subtree.

The package seam is explicit: `loo-cast-game` installs `spacetime_engine::game::LooCastGamePlugin`, but Combat and Health live under `spacetime-engine/src/game` ([Game facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-game/src/lib.rs#L1-L17>)). The September 10 chain was already called generic; September 19 extracted Health and damage application; October 5 changed hit testing to Avian colliders; October 6 reorganized modules. These improved internal structure without moving gameplay ownership across the Engine/Game content boundary. See [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md#september-10october-6-2026--combat-and-health-gain-modules-without-crossing-the-enginegame-package-boundary). The source was inspected; no tests or runtime experiment were performed.

## October 26 — the Game crate is still an install shim over gameplay housed in the Engine

The current Loo-Cast Game root calls itself a composition over Engine domains, and its plugin wires a single cross-domain schedule plus a list of child facilities. That list mixes plainly Loo-Cast-facing areas (`player`, `world`, `playground`, `console_commands`, `devtools`) with modules whose own docs promise generic controlled-subject or simulation facilities (`control`, `locomotion`, `navigation`, `flight`, `orbit`, `health`, `combat`, `spacecraft`, `surface`) and Engine-level USF, physics-adjacent portal, thermal and presentation assets ([Game module and schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/mod.rs#L1-L214>), [Game content facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-game/src/lib.rs#L1-L17>)). Names and module documentation establish an intent to reuse some domains, not independent packages or proven APIs.

The dependency direction complicates that intent. Generic-claiming `control`, `locomotion`, `navigation`, `flight` and `health` modules use schedule sets declared by `game::mod`; `flight` directly imports both `GameSet` and `PresentationSet`, while the plugin that defines those sets owns the orchestration of Engine and game modules ([control](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/control/mod.rs#L1-L60>), [locomotion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/mod.rs#L1-L90>), [navigation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/navigation/mod.rs#L1-L90>), [flight](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/flight/mod.rs#L1-L70>), [health](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/mod.rs#L1-L112>)). This is an actual source-level upward coupling: “generic” capabilities depend on the aggregate Game scheduling vocabulary. Whether those sets belong in Engine orchestration, a Game-owned schedule adapter, or separate runtime phases is an architecture decision not settled by the current implementation.

The `loo-cast-game` crate does not contain the gameplay implementation in this snapshot. It exports identity/title and an `install` function that registers `spacetime_engine::game::LooCastGamePlugin` plus developer adapters. Its Cargo library depends only on `spacetime-engine`; the Packagepack executable calls `spacetime_engine::run(loo_cast_game::install)` and directly depends on both crates ([Game Cargo package](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-game/Cargo.toml>), [Packagepack entrypoint](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-packagepack/src/main.rs#L1-L5>), [Packagepack Cargo graph](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-packagepack/Cargo.toml>), [typed Game manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-game/Game.vapor.toml>)). Therefore the authored Game library is currently a registration shim, not the compiled home of the game logic; the final executable is Packagepack-owned, but most Game systems are compiled from the Engine crate.

This exact transitional state was documented when the `loo-cast-game` workspace member first appeared on July 7 (`afe1d77`): the comment said implementation was “temporarily housed” under `spacetime_engine::game` while the runtime/composition boundary was proven, with physical relocation deferred. September 24 (`32b05dc`) renamed the installed plugin to `LooCastGamePlugin` but retained the Engine-owned code; October 17 (`4551c53`) made the Packagepack executable the actual launch entrypoint without moving the implementation. The current structure thus does not prove that the earlier transition was completed: it proves the Packagepack launch path was completed while the explicitly temporary Game-source placement remained. This is a concrete contradiction between artifact identity and source ownership, and it directly intersects the owner's invariant that Packs describe selection while Content owns implementation. It does not imply every current Engine/Game file should move mechanically; the generic modules' schedule back-edge and ownership must be resolved semantically first. See [history](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md#july-7--october-17-2026--a-game-content-crate-is-created-but-implementation-stays-inside-the-engine).

## October 26 — player, spacecraft and scenario bootstrap are Game policy composed from Engine primitives

The current Player module is explicitly local-human identity, input/controller tuning, aim and presentation. Generic controlled-subject locomotion and navigation are documented elsewhere; a Player is one controller/body specialization, not the generic motion owner ([Player module contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/mod.rs>), [Player components](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/components.rs>)). The Spacecraft module describes a reference ship assembled from generic USF/control primitives, but its implementation directly consumes `Player`, `PlayerInputFrame`, `GameScenario`, `GameSet`, control, flight, locomotion, navigation and surface types. Its startup system creates one named Reference Spacecraft, waits for the celestial scenario's detailed chart and collision readiness, makes the player a semantic constituent, disables/hides the body manifestation, and requests an ordinary local-control transfer ([Spacecraft plugin and dependency surface](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/spacecraft/mod.rs>), [reference ship spawn/ownership transfer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/spacecraft/spawn.rs>), [boarding transactions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/spacecraft/boarding/mod.rs>), [landing policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/spacecraft/landing.rs>)). The underlying control-transfer API may be reusable; this hard-coded reference craft and its lifecycle are Loo-Cast game policy. A generic-looking label does not make the implementation content-independent.

Likewise, `GameScenario` is a compiled enum with `Selection`, `Playground` and `CelestialFixture`. The startup selector creates a fixed UI for the two scenario choices, and its own contract states gameplay plugins remain active regardless of selected world. The celestial fixture module then composes authored Earth/Moon scenario facts, arrival policy, landmarks and fixture cleanup over semantic runtime facilities ([scenario root](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/mod.rs>), [hard-coded scenario selector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/selection/mod.rs>), [fixture composition and lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/mod.rs>)). This is a real bootstrap boundary, but not yet discoverable/authorable Vapor content resolution: scenarios are selected from the Game's Rust enum, and the same plugin set stays resident. That may be appropriate for a test/development composition; whether production Loo-Cast should expose scenario choice as Game content is an unresolved product/model decision, not inferred as a missing content type.

The history reinforces the transition-incomplete reading. The current spacecraft path first appears in the September 22 USF experimentation sequence (`71867eb` onward), after the July Game artifact had already been explicitly marked as a temporary shim. September 25's `e14e928` makes celestial fixture geometry and canonical-coordinate ownership more coherent; October 6's `0e48843` reorganizes the spacecraft/player/world integration, and October 9's `46e1eac` adds the final recorded control/camera/landing-related refinements. Those iterations deepen one Loo-Cast scenario on shared Engine mechanisms; they do not turn the scenario or reference ship into separately resolved Vapor content. See [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md#september-22--october-9-2026--reference-spacecraft-and-authored-worlds-grow-inside-the-game-facade).

## October 26 — world generation currently means stable construction facts; celestial terrain is a sphere

The current `worldgen` module provides a persistent root seed, stable phenomenon/field-derived sampling, exact-versus-procedural construction constraints, provenance and a sparse catalog. Its own module contract limits it to “the first reusable construction inputs”; it explicitly does not own semantic identity, authority, chunk loading or simulation ([worldgen contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/worldgen/mod.rs>)). The Earth/Moon fixture calls the same resolver for body radius, but both current constraints are `Exact`; changing the `WorldSeed` therefore changes neither radius nor center. Its test asserts those authored values are seed-independent ([authored bodies and constraints](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/definition.rs>)). This is deterministic typed construction scaffolding, not a script-defined world recipe or an active procedural planetary terrain generator.

The current semantic field makes the distinction especially clear. `CelestialVoxelField::sphere` stores only radius and coarsest numerical detail scale; the doc says detail and caves are not authored there. The backing sampler returns radial distance from that sphere and chooses only ROCK inside or VOID outside. Dense voxel chunks, surface meshes, collision and per-scale realizations are downstream representations of this same simple semantic truth ([field contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_field/mod.rs>), [canonical body sampler](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/base/celestial/field.rs>), [backing-field materialization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/base/mod.rs>), [scale realization lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_realization.rs>)). Thus the current globe is not merely a low-detail rendering of a richer field: the source's authoritative terrain itself is spherical, with two materials and no elevation bands, caves or authored surface recipe.

This is a substantial intentional retreat in the checked-in history, not a capability that simply has not yet been moved into a UI. October 7's `69780e1` (“removed unoptimized af terrain shit”) changed fixture construction from `CelestialVoxelField::new(radius, detail, noise key, profile)` to `CelestialVoxelField::sphere(radius, detail)`. The same commit deleted the rocky/lunar profiles, terrain bands, caves, cave noise helpers, presentation detail layers, and most of the GPU density path; the commit stat is 78 insertions and 2,701 deletions across 21 files. That is evidence the previous morphology and GPU implementation were removed in an optimization pass; it does not prove the earlier implementation was correct, performant enough, or production-ready. The later October 8 worldgen/field restructuring establishes canonical deterministic construction and keeps scale as a numerical/representation choice, but does not restore the removed terrain features ([`69780e1` diff](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/69780e125ca9149548a408e9a55447eb0e6bc451), [current field evolution](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e48843), [history summary](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md#october-7-2026--performance-pruning-removes-authored-planetary-relief-and-caves)). This is a key prerequisite for the owner's terrain-authoring goal: separate reusable sampling/streaming/collision machinery from authored field algorithms, then decide what artifact and authoring interface owns recipes. Current sources do not define that interface or prove prior GPU performance was the only reason to remove the morphology.


## October 26 — release review mutates the installed app before producing its review

`stage_application_release` is documented as staging a source distribution “for review,” but before it computes the distribution review it builds Rustdoc into the installed app root and calls `sync_release_assets`. The documentation builder clears/replaces generated Rustdoc output and removes an obsolete cache; asset sync removes the existing installed script/tool subtree before copying its replacement, while launch scripts are copied in place ([review-stage order](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/publishing.rs#L411-L439>), [documentation install and cleanup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/documentation.rs#L14-L80>), [asset replacement behavior](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/app_root.rs#L20-L97>)). The same asset operation is part of local deployment and package assembly ([deployment callers](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/deployment.rs#L35-L55>), [package caller](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/deployment.rs#L58-L110>)). This means a review-stage failure can leave the installed app modified even though no release review is returned; a copy failure after `remove_dir_all` can leave a source-owned tree absent or partial. That is a non-transactional staging boundary, not evidence that a particular deployment or publish failed. A safer contract would build into a release-owned temporary tree and promote only after staging succeeds. No failure injection or filesystem recovery scenario was run.

## October 26 — Studio Browse mixes two authorities and sends an unused search projection

The local Browse page combines installed/acquired Catalog entries with unregistered source-project folders in one “On this device” pane and even reports them together as “content items” plus “project folders ready to add.” The candidate rows are clearly labeled and explicitly promise not to move the files, so this is not a false claim that source is installed content; the product boundary is nevertheless nested inside the same browse surface and detail context ([Browse composition and counts](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/discover.rs#L90-L205>), [combined list/detail panels](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/discover.rs#L290-L322>), [source-project adoption rows](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/components/catalog_list.rs#L72-L130>)). It preserves three independently sourced failure statuses (Catalog, registered projects, unregistered scan), revealing that the apparent single “local content” operation is actually several authorities ([discovery status surfaces](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/discover.rs#L48-L88>)).

There are also two search states: each keystroke updates Studio's local query and sends `CatalogAction::Search` to the service; the service returns `catalog_search` in snapshots, but the inspected Studio catalog projection does not read that result, and Browse filters its local Catalog/source copies itself. Some empty-state “Clear search and filters” buttons clear the local query without sending the matching empty service query (the top-level Clear filters button does send it). Therefore Studio and the shared service can retain different query state; the visible page currently relies on the local filter, so this is a confirmed synchronization inconsistency rather than a demonstrated wrong result ([local query action and filters](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/discover.rs#L90-L175>), [service query projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/catalog.rs#L10-L53>), [snapshot field](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_protocol/src/state.rs#L104-L116>), [Studio snapshot application](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/catalog.rs#L379-L445>), [empty-state clear handlers](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/discover.rs#L213-L236>)).

The screen's evolution supports, but does not prove, the cause: October 17 `9ee09b5` explicitly unified workspace candidates and catalog content in one discovery view; October 19 `55f1afa` continued player-facing catalog presentation. This is a coherent convenience surface with visible labels, but it mixes source-authoring and acquired-content operations and duplicates query ownership. No visual/runtime pass was performed.

## October 26 — the Studio Library exposes only cached/installed runtime content

The Library page is not a raw view of every locally known content kind. Its `CatalogFilter::library` admits only entries whose service-projected role is `RuntimeContent` and which have a Cache or Installed location; it excludes `PlayableComposition` (Packagepack) and `CreatorCrate` (Crate). The UI then describes these as content “available to add to a composition,” while Compositions owns playable roots and Creator Tools owns authored projects ([Library page contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/library.rs#L9-L16>), [role/location filter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/catalog.rs#L733-L790>), [service role projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/catalog.rs#L498-L621>)). Packagepack separation is explicit and matches the book's composition model. Crate visibility is less settled in the documentation: Crate is defined as statically composed Rust library source, while the product Library is defined broadly as locally available content ([kind and Library definitions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/docs/books/vapor/src/concepts/content-types.md#L1-L36>), [book's player Library definition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/docs/books/vapor/src/README.md#L15-L28>)). The current role filter may be intentional progressive disclosure—Crate belongs to Developer tools—or may hide a Composer dependency that must be selected. No authored policy found in these checked-in pages settles which. This is a documented/UI contract ambiguity, not a claim that the filter is incorrect.

## October 26 — character orientation is split into gravity, body, and control frames

The current character system deliberately carries three related but non-identical orientations. `CharacterLocomotionFrame.up` is the stable movement/gravity axis; `CharacterControlFrame.rotation` supplies the view-relative basis and can temporarily retain portal-induced roll/pitch; the physical `Transform.rotation` is aligned to locomotion-up only while grounded. The player movement writer applies local yaw after the control basis, projects forward onto the locomotion plane, scales commanded movement during a settle, and suppresses jump input until that scale reaches 0.5. Existing momentum is not attenuated by that input factor. The split therefore encodes a real policy distinction—camera/control recovery can be gradual while gravity, grounded classification, and body alignment use the stable frame—rather than three interchangeable copies of rotation ([frame types and settle policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/frame/mod.rs>), [frame update schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/plugin.rs#L61-L87>), [gravity/body synchronization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/frame/systems.rs>), [input projection and jump gate](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/controls/movement/mod.rs#L119-L193>)).

The scheduling is significant: control settling advances from render `Time::delta_secs()` in `PreUpdate`; gravity-up and grounded-body alignment run in the once-per-frame `RunFixedMainLoop` environment stage; the resulting movement intent is sampled immediately before the fixed character motor loop. During fixed-step catch-up, movement intent and reference-frame samples are held for the repeated physics ticks, while the settle timer advances once per outer frame. This is consistent with the broader pre-fixed snapshot described above, but the two time cadences mean portal-control recovery and physical movement are not one fixed-tick state machine. A portal crossing starts the same settle policy in both whole-body and split traversal paths; vehicle exit and fixture placement can explicitly `snap_to` a newly resolved control basis. These are source-backed transitions, not proof of camera feel or transition behavior under pause, low frame rate, or rapid repeated crossings ([whole-body traversal](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/traversal/mod.rs#L68-L111>), [split crossing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/character/resolution/crossing/mod.rs#L49-L83>), [fixed intent sampling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/controls/movement/mod.rs#L119-L193>)).

History clarifies why this distinction exists. September 12 `67160378` introduced `CharacterControlFrame`, moved view-relative movement away from the body transform, and started a transition after portal placement; the previous control path read body rotation directly. Current code retains that semantic separation after later module restructuring and adds explicit snapping for pose transactions. It also adds a gameplay threshold (`movement_input_scale >= 0.5`) for jump suppression that was not part of the original frame split. The design is intentional and internally connected, but no direct regression test or rendered/runtime review in this audit verifies its player-facing result; do not infer from the component model alone that camera roll, movement, or jumping “feels right.” See [the dated timeline entry](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md#september-12-2026--portal-orientation-settling-introduces-a-third-character-frame).

## October 26 — USF view demand and presentation are separate from camera and physics authority

### Current ownership

The observer has three coordinate-bearing concepts. `UsfViewAnchor` marks the runtime transform whose canonical `UsfPosition` is the semantic observation origin. `UsfViewRenderAnchor` marks the render-space origin. `UsfViewObservationOverride` is a global optional presentation override with one canonical/runtime position pair; its contract explicitly leaves gameplay subject, interaction scale, refinement, collision/editing authority and generic spatial demand unchanged ([anchor and override](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/anchor.rs>)). `UsfViewContext` is attached to a view entity and stores canonical position, runtime and render anchors, SI velocity, projection eye offset, discrete spatial scale and continuous zoom ([context](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/context.rs>)). The projection subtracts the camera-eye/boom offset in SI metres before scale conversion; it is designed so zooming the same view rescales the scene around the physical camera ray instead of manufacturing parallax.

`UsfScalePresentation` describes canonical semantic-anchored geometry; `UsfLocalScalePresentation` describes scale-authored geometry on a child whose parent already has a runtime position. Their conversion handles native-scale units versus SI-authored mesh dimensions ([contracts](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/presentation.rs>)). `project_local_scale_presentations` and `project_scale_presentations` mutate presentation transforms, visibility and render layers only. Local presentations follow role readiness and observer contribution. Semantic presentations use direct bounded projection where possible; otherwise far-field compression is allowed only when the presentation resolves to a semantic authority that publishes explicit conservative bounds. One owner-wide uniform ratio preserves chunk seams/angular shape. Physical-local terrain is selected only when view, interaction and presentation scales agree; otherwise terrain is projected contextually under presentation-role gating. Projection failure hides that representation. This is a fairly explicit authority split, but the renderer still writes Bevy presentation transforms directly and currently has one central context/projection owner.

### Demand is not residency

`UsfViewDemand` records one observer's canonical anchor, scale, SI motion, eye offset, frustum, camera basis and (for perspective) FOV/aspect/viewport density. Its `requests_scale` gate applies to native capability relevance. A separate presentation-relevance test can keep coarser scenery present independent of the observer's current scale; it rejects sub-0.75-pixel cells and uses perspective side planes while deliberately ignoring near/far clipping as a semantic residency boundary. Orthographic/custom projections remain conservative after bounded conversion ([demand model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/demand/model.rs>)). `UsfViewDemandPolicy` has Live, Frozen and Disabled modes, but is one global resource. The demand submodule owns its public re-exports and capture schedule ([demand module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/demand/mod.rs>)). Capture runs in `PostUpdate` after Bevy frusta update. It queries every active view anchor, sorts entries by entity bits, and publishes a reusable multi-entry snapshot; observer/frustum changes increment its revision, while velocity-only changes update entries without incrementing observer revision ([capture and policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/demand/capture.rs>), [policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/demand/policy.rs>)). Voxel realization iterates the snapshot to append view-originated celestial intents, and the demand-plan key consumes the same snapshot ([intent collection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/intent.rs#L241-L295>), [plan key call site](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/plan/mod.rs#L214-L227>)). These are presentation relevance requests, not grants of collision/edit authority.

One captured field currently stops at that boundary: view velocity is stored, compared and exposed, but the predictive voxel planner does not read it. View-originated realization scopes use the camera entity as their source; `demand_plan_key` looks velocity up in `SpatialDemandMotionSnapshot`, which is populated only for entities with `SpatialDemandSource`. The spawned projection camera has no such component. As a result, view-owned demand follows current camera/frustum state and invalidates on observer change, but its predictive lookahead remains stationary even when the view context reports subject motion ([view intent construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/intent.rs#L10-L91>), [motion snapshot collection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/demand/systems.rs#L21-L57>), [planner motion lookup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/plan/mod.rs#L365-L399>), [camera spawn components](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/spawn/mod.rs#L260-L286>)). This is a source-confirmed dataflow gap, not evidence of visible pop-in; the current-view scope is still recomputed and the actual streaming result was not run.

### Multi-view capability is partial, not absent or complete

The snapshot/culling side is multi-view: capture has a `Query` and stores a vector, while voxel realization loops all entries. The projection side is singular: `sync_view_context`, `project_local_scale_presentations`, and `project_scale_presentations` each take `Single<...With<UsfViewRenderAnchor>>`; sync additionally rejects more than one semantic anchor. The override and policy are global, and rendered entities are projected through one selected context/render-layer arrangement. Thus the code has a multi-view demand representation but not independent per-camera semantic contexts, projection realizations, policies or render outputs. The `UsfViewContext` comments call split-screen/spectator/portal contexts future support; those comments agree with the source cardinality. It would be inaccurate to describe the current pipeline as either simply “single-view” (demand is not) or “multi-view supported” (projection is not).

The debug freecam is another useful cross-check: it changes local camera pose and can set an observer override but does not become physical or semantic control. Its usual Frozen demand mode retains the last view snapshot as the camera moves. Live mode with override would update the position, but `sync_view_context` supplies zero semantic velocity for the override; predictive view demand therefore has no freecam velocity source in this path. This is a limitation derived from source, not evidence that the user encountered a streaming failure.

### History and confidence

October 6 `ab65b8e2190a42e81f1bbae6b22a090297d8d987` split the previous view module into anchor, context, presentation and probe files, with 543 insertions and 514 deletions across those view paths; this made the contracts individually inspectable but did not itself validate their behavior ([commit](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/ab65b8e2190a42e81f1bbae6b22a090297d8d987)). October 8 `d806e3dc7c8f6bd30e0bc23578c1b9eeb0acacff` extracted observer demand into capture/model/policy modules and removed the old `lod.rs`, with 398 insertions and 826 deletions across the view paths ([commit](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/d806e3dc7c8f6bd30e0bc23578c1b9eeb0acacff)). The same day, `0f153c5e17342d4ff293f10f3c9b05dfe2990ea9` added conservative far-field similarity projection and focused tests for distant angular-ratio preservation and nearby rejection ([commit](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0f153c5e17342d4ff293f10f3c9b05dfe2990ea9)). October 21 `5730ab23abc171c471868c1c304c47f6f5c93e76` reformats the view code and test expressions. Comparing each file after removing whitespace confirms the `context.rs` and `systems.rs` token streams are identical across that commit. The commit as a whole is not formatting-only: it also changes configuration, worldgen, fixture and USF code outside this view slice.

The source contains focused distant-projection tests, but they were not run in this audit. No multi-camera, freecam-demand, scale-transition, visibility seam or runtime frustum/streaming case was executed. Therefore the ownership and cardinality findings above are source-confirmed; numerical quality and user-visible behavior remain unverified. Relevant files also include [module wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/mod.rs>), [presentation probe](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/probe.rs>), [view projection systems](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/systems.rs>), [spatial schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/mod.rs#L180-L199>), and [view demand planning](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/plan/mod.rs#L214-L227>).

## October 26 — recursive portal rendering has a depth-bound mismatch and per-frame mesh churn

### Current rendering contract

`PortalRenderingPlugin` loads the custom surface shader and installs five responsibilities: startup pair/surface setup, activation-derived endpoint visibility, light layer adaptation, split-body visual rebuilding, camera-path mapping and render-target resizing ([plugin](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/mod.rs>)). The setup creates two fixed endpoint entities from `PortalConfig`, rectangular collision stencils, frame meshes/materials and one recursive directed-face render tree. The visible frame is three-sided by design so a floor-touching aperture has no bottom bar ([setup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/setup/mod.rs>), [frame](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/frame/mod.rs>), [presentation tolerances](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/layout/mod.rs>)). A face is an ordinary one-sided rectangle; front/back use separate directed faces and transforms. The shader derives sample UV from viewport coordinates, so the whole virtual view maps through the aperture shape rather than stretching to its mesh UV ([surface](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/surface/mod.rs>), [material](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/material/mod.rs>), [WGSL](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/shader/portal.wgsl>)).

A recursive render node chooses each permitted directed face, allocates one image/material and child camera unless it has reached the configured terminal depth, in which case the aperture is black. The child path records the exact face sequence; camera updates replay the same rigid `map_transform` for each step, derive a clip plane from the final exit and copy the primary clear color. Deeper camera orders are more negative so inner textures are rendered before their parent views. Every camera starts dormant; visibility sync activates the whole camera set and reveals both endpoint hierarchies only when both ends are active. Ordinary world lights preserve their authored layers while also joining derived and USF presentation layers ([tree](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/tree/mod.rs>), [path model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/path/mod.rs>), [camera mapping](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/camera/mod.rs>), [visibility and lights](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/visibility/mod.rs>)). This is a real recursive view mechanism, but it is created for one `PortalPair` and derives from one `PortalView`; it is not an arbitrary portal graph or per-view tree manager. The current camera path also returns unless the primary projection is perspective. The primary player camera currently uses `Camera3d::default()` and carries both `PrimaryGameView` and `PortalView` ([primary camera creation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/spawn/mod.rs#L215-L235>)).

`PortalRenderTargets` owns a flat vector of image handles. Startup sizing reads the primary window; the ongoing resize path instead reads `PrimaryGameView::physical_viewport_size`, supporting embedded viewport resize without a `WindowResized` event. Resizing mutates the images and touches materials that reference those handles so Bevy rebuilds their bind groups ([targets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/targets/mod.rs>)). That is a well-targeted adapter to the editor viewport. No independent target allocation or release occurs on runtime config changes; setup is a Startup system, so `visual_recursion_depth`, sidedness, pair transforms/size and surface tree are fundamentally a startup snapshot unless another explicit rebuild path is added. The public mutable config makes this a conditional reconfiguration seam; no current authoring route was found that mutates it after setup.

### Confirmed layer-index contract mismatch

`PortalConfig::validate` accepts a maximum visual recursion depth of four and defaults to two ([config](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/config.rs>)). `build_node` uses a radix-four node ID: root is `1`, and each child is `node * BRANCH_FACTOR + branch_index`, where the branch factor is four. It then uses `RenderLayers::layer(child)` while creating child cameras; surfaces similarly call `RenderLayers::layer(layer)` ([tree construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/tree/mod.rs>), [surface layer constructor](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/surface/mod.rs>)). At depth 1 node IDs are 4–7; depth 2 gives 16–31; depth 3 reaches 64–127. The pinned dependency is Bevy `0.19.1`; its `RenderLayers::layer` computes `layer / 64` and asserts the result is below its one inline block, while docs direct dynamic/high indices to `with` or `from_layers` ([locked constructor source](</home/leslieghf/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/bevy_camera-0.19.1/src/visibility/render_layers.rs#L54-L69>)). Thus depth 3 or 4 passes Vapor's own validation but necessarily reaches a constructor assertion when the recursive tree is built; the configured default depth 2 remains within range. This is a source-proven bound mismatch with a direct panic path, not a runtime reproduction. The permitted one-sided configuration uses fewer branches but shares the same radix-four encoding and does not make high depths safe.

The mismatch also reveals an architectural cost hidden by the one-number setting. With the default two-sided config, depth 2 creates 4 + 12 = 16 render images/cameras before either portal is placed; at depth 4 the theoretical accepted tree would create 160 nonterminal image/camera nodes (4 + 12 + 36 + 108) before reaching the terminal surfaces, if layer construction supported them. The code does not cull branches by the primary camera or create targets lazily when a face enters view. These counts are derived from the recursive loop and branch suppression; allocation size, GPU cost and measured startup/frame impact are not available here.

### Split visualization cost and physical alignment

The visual split implementation selects the same positive/negative point sets returned by `partition_box_by_plane`, and its mesh builder omits only the cut-plane face so the visual opening can continue through the complementary peer. Physics uses closed convex hulls, so the two representations intentionally share the partition while differing at the cap ([split visual system](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/split/mod.rs>), [flat-shaded mesh builder](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/split/mesh/mod.rs>), [physics split implementation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/aperture/mod.rs>)). This is a meaningful geometry-sharing foundation.

However, `sync_split_visuals` runs in `Update` with an unconstrained query over every `PortalSplitVisual`. For an ordinary non-peer authority whose `split.active` is `None`, it sets visibility and assigns a newly generated `full_box_mesh` every time. Active splits likewise rebuild `convex_polyhedron_mesh` every pass, even if the body pose, portal plane and partition have not changed; invalid/ended split branches regenerate the full mesh too. The query has no `Changed`/cache gate, and current player/cube model spawns attach the marker. Therefore repeated mesh generation and asset replacement are source-confirmed for the visible reference models. Repeated CPU work and asset change notifications are strong risks; their actual cost or GPU upload behavior was not measured. The former triangle-count test was removed in the October 5 cleanup; the current `spacetime-engine/src/portal` tree has no local test module, and no mesh regeneration, layer-depth or render-target test was found. No tests or runtime were run in this audit.

### Source and historical record

The current module files enumerate the full rendering ownership map: [rendering root](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/mod.rs>), [layout](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/layout/mod.rs>), [material](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/material/mod.rs>), [recursion root](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/mod.rs>), [tree](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/tree/mod.rs>), [camera](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/camera/mod.rs>), [path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/path/mod.rs>), [targets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/targets/mod.rs>), [scene root](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/mod.rs>), [frame](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/frame/mod.rs>), [setup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/setup/mod.rs>), [surface](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/scene/surface/mod.rs>), [shader](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/shader/portal.wgsl>), [split root](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/split/mod.rs>), [split mesh](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/split/mesh/mod.rs>), and [visibility](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/visibility/mod.rs>).

## October 26 — voxel edit authority is cache-durable, but not a saved-world format

### Current edit ownership

The Voxel Hand is a hard-coded Playground item, not a Studio/IDE terrain authoring tool. It raycasts the currently active dense chunks in the selected interaction Scale Slice, removes on primary action, adds on secondary action, and selects ROCK/GLASS/NEBULA with modifiers ([item registration and use](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/voxel_hand/mod.rs>)). It cannot hit a semantic surface that has no active dense materialization in that slice. The operation set is currently a spherical brush with Add, Remove and Paint; the field/material API itself still uses a fixed material lookup ([brush and edit operations](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/edit/mod.rs>), [material behavior](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/field/mod.rs>)).

Shared semantic bodies store body/frame-local `VoxelFrameEdit`s in an append-only `Vec` on `VoxelSemanticAuthority`. A hit is expressed in that stable semantic frame, then applied to resident `VoxelScaleRealization`s whose `VoxelScaleDomain` supports editing. Standalone realizations without that authority use `VoxelModificationLayer`, which keeps another ordered edit vector plus an index from canonical chunk address to edit indices. Chunk samples, surfaces and Avian colliders are derived state: a chunk recipe captures the base and relevant edits, and a worker catches up edits that arrived after the recipe snapshot ([authority](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/authority.rs>), [standalone modification index](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/modification/mod.rs>), [recipe](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/world/recipe/mod.rs>), [generation catch-up](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/mod.rs>)). This is a useful authority/cache separation, but it is two in-memory ownership shapes rather than one persistence contract.

The scale mask is a capability declaration, not the currently selected interaction authority. The celestial fixture marks its supported physical range as editable-capable; demand grants the active `EDITING` role only to the selected interaction scale. The shared body-frame edit log is projected into realizations in its declared editable mask, while slices outside that mask do not consume it ([domain](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/domain.rs>), [active role selection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/intent.rs>), [fixture mask](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/scenery/celestial.rs>)). That distinguishes “this slice can derive edits” from “this slice currently owns editing input.”

### Durability and history limits

Comments call the semantic edit log “persistent,” but the inspected code means persistent across derived cache eviction and regeneration. The authority component and edit types have no serialization contract, and repository-wide search found no terrain-edit save/load or content-authored terrain-operation path. No undo/redo layer or stable operation identity exists in this code path. This does not rule out an external host serializing broader ECS state; it does mean this voxel subsystem itself does not define durable world edits. Do not describe Voxel Hand as player save support or as a procedural-terrain authoring workflow.

The history explains the vocabulary. `2ce923f` adds the first visible Voxel Hand as a direct edit to a single dense `VoxelChunk`. `5efc021` and `65d4ea1` then move toward a reconstructible `base + sparse modifications` world and indexed chunk rematerialization. September 22's USF work introduces body-local `VoxelSemanticAuthority`, separating semantic edit identity from each scale-local realization. October 5 `e987230` deletes the prior chunk, edit, modification, world, streaming and base test modules; the current voxel tree retains only two inline tests, for realization intent and demand-region planning, not edit persistence/replay. October 7 `69780e1` removes the former terrain bands, morphology and cave field, leaving the current spherical base with edit operations. Those changes evolve the representation model and remove tests, but none creates a disk-backed authoring format ([initial tool](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/2ce923fb5e3195c07ce1c37a4a037c3aa7e56157), [base plus modifications](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/5efc021), [USF authority](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/9de6680), [test deletion](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), [terrain retreat](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/69780e125ca9149548a408e9a55447eb0e6bc451)).

This is source/history evidence only. I did not run tests, save/reload a world, or exercise scale transitions; no claim is made about any runtime rendering mismatch or lost player edit.

## October 26 — Studio's Share page combines community publishing and first-party release controls

The current Publish page composes two different release products. The dedicated Studio screen first appeared October 16 in Studio commit [`5ffb2a8`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Studio/commit/5ffb2a8e6eb6ae8c3283b8d4be646b94fbb27758) for Workshop item review. October 17's [`3e8ec88`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Studio/commit/3e8ec880fa0203620c4849ff9209298ab6c0e583) added root Steam publishing as a second tab. Studio moved onto the shared Client service in [`ef6e6b1`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Studio/commit/ef6e6b130ae8e52515b95a64fcf988b32780ba5e), and [`d169e48`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Studio/commit/d169e4859c14496ad3295ef9aa2c3bcc8aa13cef) routed its workflows through that service. The UI is now a facade for both operations, but their different audiences remain combined under the Creator-area Share navigation ([Share membership](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/navigation.rs#L20-L54>), [page composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/publish.rs#L16-L48>)).

Workshop publishing reviews an authored content artifact from the open source workspace. Studio requires a current source list and local catalog, allows a conflict as a visible caution because the workspace source is what will be published, asks for `PUBLISH <id> TO <account>`, and submits `WorkshopAction::Publish`; the service re-stages the source and rejects a changed review before invoking the provider/SteamCMD path ([Workshop UI policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/pages/publish.rs#L76-L245>), [submit boundary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Studio/crates/vapor_studio_ui/src/workshop.rs#L419-L471>), [service/application re-stage](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/publishing.rs#L626-L683>)). The other tab stages/uploads the fixed Vapor root Steam app/depot and can set a beta branch live. That action is classified `Developer` plus `RootPublisher`, but the central capability check only evaluates local tool requirements; its own comment delegates authority to the handler. The root handler validates the review token and exact confirmation before calling `vapor_sdk_core::root::publish::root_publish`, while actual Steam account access is left to Steamworks/SteamCMD ([action profile](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_domain/src/actions.rs#L482-L490>), [shared validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session.rs#L768-L787>), [root handler](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/publishing.rs#L6-L145>)). This is not evidence of an authorization bypass: a valid Steamworks publisher account is still required. It is a source-confirmed product and audience conflation. Owner direction distinguishes creator workflows from stronger official-developer tools; the current navigation does not express that distinction, and no UI run was performed.

## October 26 — Identity operator scripts have non-resumable and partial-apply paths

At Platform Server HEAD `a98770a`, `smoke-identity-auth.sh --no-wait` creates a server-side auth attempt and binds a GitHub device flow to that attempt, prints the verification code, then exits. The subsequent message says to rerun without `--no-wait`, but the script's normal startup path creates a fresh attempt, so polling that new attempt cannot complete the code shown by the first invocation. The runbook uses this mode as a GitHub readiness smoke; that narrow use can verify flow creation, but the “resume by rerunning” instruction is incorrect ([smoke branch](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/smoke-identity-auth.sh#L221-L250>), [attempt/code binding](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Identity-Server/src/session_handlers.rs#L258-L287>), [operator command](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/docs/identity-auth-runbook.md#L128-L148>)).

`configure-identity-auth.sh` updates each requested setting in sequence. Validation is interleaved with writes, so valid earlier options remain applied if a later option is invalid. Individual rewrites use a temporary file and restrictive owner/mode, but the multi-option request has no prevalidation or atomic commit. These are source-proven usability/reliability defects, not evidence that the VPS currently has malformed configuration. No script was executed against the server or locally with a fixture.


## October 26 — Rust Analyzer runs under the Client service, while IDE semantics remain frontend-owned

The current IDE launches Rust Analyzer through the Vapor Client service rather than spawning an unmanaged host process. The service checks that the requested canonical root equals the selected workspace, starts the pinned analyzer via that workspace's managed toolchain, and keeps one process per connected client. Its worker path drains stderr, applies a Windows no-console flag, and bounds LSP messages and queued outbound messages ([dispatch](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server.rs#L545-L584>), [managed process](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server/language_server.rs#L15-L179>)).

The frontend still owns the protocol-level meaning: it sends initialization, document lifecycle updates and feature requests, tracks pending request/document versions, assembles diagnostics and semantic links, and previews accepted text edits. The shipped options disable check-on-save, Cargo build scripts and proc macros ([initialization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_ide_ui/src/language_server.rs#L179-L199>), [Rust Analyzer settings and UTF coordinate/edit helpers](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_ide_ui/src/lsp_text.rs#L59-L170>), [editor controls](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_ide_ui/src/editor_view.rs#L185-L250>), [revision-bound request state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_ide_ui/src/language_server.rs#L84-L123>)). Only `publishDiagnostics` is promoted into a typed protocol event; most other LSP messages cross the service boundary as raw JSON and are interpreted in the IDE ([service adaptation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server.rs#L540-L543>), [protocol type](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_protocol/src/language_server.rs#L32-L139>)).

This qualifies the owner-facing statement that the IDE is nearly absent: source already has substantive navigation, completion, formatting, diagnostics and guarded edit previews. It also qualifies the aspiration that the service is the shared API for all frontends: process/toolchain ownership is centralized, but language-server semantics are currently coupled to the IDE frontend. Since the service map keys analyzer processes by client ID, multiple IDE clients can start separate analyzers for one workspace; duplicate work is possible from source structure but was not measured. The LSP helper and editor-view files were inspected for this slice and are now named in the coverage register; they are not certified as fully reviewed. No GUI, analyzer session, Windows process, build or test was run.

History shows two organizational extractions rather than a new backend architecture. On October 23, [`220cc867`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/220cc86785f77c8ba6f7e0722e22f3bdcc568c2d) moved 1,120 lines of language-server workflow into a dedicated IDE module, and [`80c654ca`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/80c654ca0d629aba955328d774c68a589cad6d52) moved the text/position helpers into `lsp_text.rs`. These made the frontend implementation easier to navigate; the protocol remained IDE-owned and service messages remained mostly generic. The later semantic-workbench plan proposes more deliberate cross-domain structures but is a plan, not proof of implementation ([plan](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-semantic-workbench.md>), [current IDE guide](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/docs/ide.md>)).

## October 26 — Shared service startup is bounded and cross-platform, but conflicting work is rejected rather than queued

The shared service boundary now has an explicit host context, process bootstrap, local transport, versioned protocol, session and resource-aware operation registry. Host resolution derives a default state directory from platform conventions and recognizes workspace paths from client-specific or legacy Studio environment keys; endpoint identity hashes the resolved app root and state directory ([host context](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/host.rs>), [endpoint identity](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/local_socket.rs>)). Unix IPC uses mode `0600`; Windows IPC builds an ACL for SYSTEM and the current user's SID. Bootstrap and service-instance locks are distinct, with a Unix advisory file lock and Windows named mutex ([transport security and locks](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/local_socket.rs>)). These mechanisms address the previously reported Windows startup and multi-frontend races at the source-design level; no Windows execution was performed in this review.

The client first connects to an existing endpoint, starts the packaged service if necessary, then requires a matching protocol version and initial snapshot. The cold-start deadline is 30 seconds; the handshake buffers at most 16 early events. On reconnect, it refreshes the snapshot and does not replay uncertain requests ([bootstrap and handshake](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/process.rs>), [protocol](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_protocol/src/message.rs>)). The service admits at most eight clients, bounds output by frame count and 40 MiB, limits inbound frames to 32 MiB, and exits after 15 idle seconds once clients and operations are gone ([limits and service loop](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server.rs>)). This is a short-lived ordinary process with bounded resources, not a daemon or an OS-installed service.

The service-side operation registry can run non-conflicting resources concurrently, retain a 100-item completion history, and expose originating client identity. Conflicting reservations are rejected immediately rather than held in a service-owned queue ([registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/operation_registry.rs>), [conflict response](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session.rs>), [typed operation model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/operation.rs>)). This is a substantive shared concurrency foundation, but not the requested common queue-first policy; frontends may make different local decisions before sending a request. The distinction matters because observing active operations in a common snapshot does not imply common admission semantics. Source inspection only; no load, race, reconnection, or cross-platform test was run.

## October 26 — Platform Server deployment, backup and restore disagree on Registry ownership

At current Platform Server HEAD `a98770a`, normal deployment builds and restarts five services and the local health check queries all five. The Registry systemd unit points its SQLite database into `${VAPOR_STATE_ROOT}/registry`. Yet `export-state.sh` and `restore-state.sh` each keep a three-service list—Docs, Identity and Diagnostics. Export stops only those processes, recursively copies the whole state root, restarts those processes, then creates the tar; Registry remains live during its database copy. Restore stops only the same three before moving the root and replacing its contents, and restarts only them afterward. **Confirmed:** Registry is absent from the quiesce/restart lists although its DB is included by the root copy. At this head, Registry's HTTP routes are GET-only, while migrations and official seed writes happen during process initialization; ordinary steady-state HTTP mutation is therefore not established. The database is configured for WAL mode ([routes and initialization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Registry-Server/src/main.rs#L18-L61>), [WAL and seed lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Registry-Server/src/db.rs#L1-L29>, </home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Registry-Server/src/db.rs#L100-L160>)). **Conditional risk, not reproduced:** if startup writes coincide with the recursive copy, the result may not be a transaction-consistent database snapshot. SQLite documents WAL-mode state across the database and WAL files and recommends its online-backup mechanism for live database copies ([WAL file contract](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html#the_wal_file), [online backup API](https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html)). Restore has a sharper lifecycle gap independent of current HTTP write traffic: it moves the directory containing an open Registry database, installs new files at the original path, and never restarts Registry. The still-running pool can continue using the pre-restore database while the restored database sits at the expected path; the health check only establishes endpoint reachability. This POSIX rename/open-file consequence was not exercised ([deploy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/deploy.sh#L65-L99>), [Registry unit](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/systemd/vapor-registry.service#L1-L23>), [export ordering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/export-state.sh#L15-L20>), [export copy/restart](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/export-state.sh#L72-L101>), [restore stop/replace/restart](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/restore-state.sh#L13-L18>), [health reachability only](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/health-check.sh#L5-L32>)).

The shared `/run/vapor-server-deploy.lock` is not acquired consistently. The systemd auto-deploy unit holds it around `deploy.sh`; export and restore acquire it internally; the documented operator command invokes `deploy.sh` directly, and the script itself has no lock acquisition. That manual path can therefore overlap a timer/export/restore operation instead of failing fast as intended ([unit wrapper](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/systemd/vapor-deploy.service#L6-L9>), [manual command](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/README.md#L21-L33>), [deploy body](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/deploy.sh#L1-L29>), [export lock](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/export-state.sh#L49-L54>), [restore lock](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/restore-state.sh#L67-L79>)).

Documentation also lags the implemented topology. `operations-evidence-and-recovery-contract.md` calls the root wrapper whole-system recovery but enumerates only docs, identity and diagnostics. Export's manifest says `secrets_included = false` while deliberately excluding `/etc/vapor-server`; the copied Identity DB nevertheless contains profile/role/audit data and, during an active OAuth device flow, a plaintext GitHub device code. Session bearer tokens are represented as hashes. The polling path rejects a device code after its separate expiry and clears it on successful authorization, but expiry alone does not clear the database field: the outer auth attempt is removed only after its own expiry or consumption, with pruning invoked when another attempt is created. This is a scope/retention qualification, not evidence that the archive contains an active session bearer. The export archive is mode 0600 and the default retention is 48 bundles ([recovery document](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/docs/operations-evidence-and-recovery-contract.md#L1-L43>), [Identity tables](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Identity-Server/src/db.rs#L98-L126>), [code lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Identity-Server/src/auth_attempts.rs#L91-L115>), [device-code storage](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Identity-Server/src/auth_attempts.rs#L185-L283>), [bundle retention](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/export-state.sh#L100-L115>)). The validator's `state/` member-kind hole and its later failure point were previously reviewed; this section does not duplicate or retest that defect ([prior analysis](#october-26--restore-validation-rejects-traversal-but-accepts-a-file-in-place-of-the-state-directory)).

Chronology: backup/restore arrived July 23, the periodic exporter July 24, and the archive validator July 25. Registry was wired into deployment and health checks September 7. The remaining snapshot/restart/docs lists stayed at their earlier three-service shape through the October 22 source refresh. This is a composition failure across service lifecycle owners, not simply a missing Registry line in a README. No script, restore, service, or VPS was run.

## October 26 — the shared GUI core is real, but its design-system reach is uneven

`vapor_gui_core` is not an empty promise: it currently owns a common dark `eframe` host, a filterable/virtualized console surface, a syntax-colored text editor, a searchable workspace tree, a compact panel, and severity marks. The important qualification is distribution: these primitives do not yet form a product-wide component system. The generic `Panel` is used by Launcher, while IDE consumes the code editor, workspace tree and console. The inspected Studio UI does not consume the shared Panel or shared ConsolePanelState directly; its presentation and operation views remain largely product-local. Launcher and IDE both have console state, but separate state instances and host-specific command submission. Therefore “shared UI core” describes some common parts, not one cohesive visual grammar or shared layout model.

The common host sets a dark egui theme for each `GuiProduct`, so OS theme divergence has an explicit defense at the host boundary. Product modes still dispatch through the `vapor_gui` router, whose enum includes Chooser, Installer, IDE, Launcher/Play, and Studio. This is one common native host selecting product implementations, not evidence that every product is a fully independent GUI binary/process. The shared editor delegates syntax tokenization to `egui_code_editor`; Rust Analyzer remains a separate IDE feature and the syntax widget alone does not supply language semantics. The console’s `show_rows` limits row widget creation to the visible viewport and caps local history at 4,000 records; this addresses the old “render every row” performance concern, but does not itself establish coherent dock resizing, persistent panel proportions, or the service-to-game event contract discussed elsewhere. The icon module paints console severity symbols from egui vector primitives, not a general icon/logo catalog.

This is a useful foundation for the owner’s requested egui toolkit and preview workflow, but the current implementation is smaller and more uneven than that ambition: common color/host setup, a few standalone widgets and domain helpers exist; composable layout regions, reusable product navigation, broader compact controls, icon vocabulary, and an isolated preview/gallery target are not evidenced in the inspected GUI workspace. Treat the latter as unchecked absence in this source slice, not a proof that no preview mechanism exists outside the checked-out tree. No build or visual inspection was performed.

History matches the ownership shift: October 21 `78d5da0` added the shared editor and workspace tree with the Rust IDE workbench; October 22 `dab912c` extracted the Launcher/authoring console model; October 22 `2360437` added the shared Panel while reworking Launcher lifecycle views. The chronological order is important: each abstraction emerged to serve a specific product path, and no subsequent evidence yet shows a deliberate pass consolidating their API, adoption, responsive layout, or visual QA into a general toolkit. [GUI core host and exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/lib.rs#L1-L77>), [shared editor](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/code_editor.rs#L1-L150>), [virtualized console](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/console.rs#L103-L145>), [visible-row rendering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/console.rs#L311-L370>), [panel primitive](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/panel.rs#L1-L55>), [severity marks](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/icons.rs#L1-L100>), [workspace tree](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui_core/src/workspace_tree.rs#L1-L100>), [IDE editor use](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_ide_ui/src/editor_view.rs#L241-L255>), [Launcher panel use](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_launcher_ui/src/lib.rs#L649-L660>), [mode dispatch](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-GUI/crates/vapor_gui/src/lib.rs#L45-L58>), [editor/tree introduction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/78d5da0), [shared console extraction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/dab912c), [Panel extraction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/2360437).
## October 26 — Developer Lab presets are reversible runtime-variable overlays, not an exclusive configuration owner

`game::devtools::lab` composes the typed runtime-variable registry rather than defining another cvar store. Its four module files divide command adapters, named preset state, and application/rollback logic ([module boundary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/lab/mod.rs>), [preset model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/lab/model.rs>), [console commands](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/lab/commands.rs>), [transaction logic](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/lab/transaction.rs>)). The only preset currently registered is `freecam`, assigning enabled, exclusive control, Follow projection, and Frozen view demand. Apply captures each touched variable’s current string value once as its baseline; later active presets win on overlaps. Clearing a preset resets baselines, reapplies the remaining stack, then discards baselines no longer referenced. This is scoped runtime state for the current process, not a saved profile or a content-authored preset format.

The stack does not own or lock its assigned variables. Generic runtime-variable commands can still set those same freecam values while the preset is active, leaving `DeveloperPresetState.active` unchanged even when the effective setting no longer equals the preset.
