A later clear/rebuild reapplies the stack. Thus “active” means recorded in the overlay order, not continuously enforced as effective state. This is an important state-authority seam for the future developer-role tooling, though the one current `debug freecam` command routes its own on/off/toggle path through the preset helper ([freecam adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/console_commands/runtime_variables/freecam.rs#L118-L158>)).

The generic shape is narrower than its registry names imply: registration is private to this module boundary and only the single built-in preset is registered in current source. Definitions are not validated as a complete set at registration; each path is looked up and each value passes through its normal setter during application. On a failed setter, the implementation attempts rollback using another pass through the same setters and logs rollback failures. That is best-effort recovery, not an atomic transaction guarantee if an adapter can fail both forward application and restoration. The freecam assignments are known static choices and all four corresponding bindings exist, so this conditional path is not evidence of a currently failing freecam preset. No current tests remain in this module; the two small state/registry tests present in the October 2 implementation were removed in the October 5 cleanup. Source behavior is reviewed here; no tests or runtime were run.

### History and confidence

October 2 `05f5a55` introduced the entire 429-line implementation in one `mod.rs`, including the four fixed assignments, console commands, string-baseline stack, rollback attempt, and two narrow model tests. The `developer-lab-preset-stack-v1` marker appeared in that initial implementation but was subsequently removed; no external schema or migration consumer is visible in the current repository. October 5 `e987230` removed the two tests while changing the same monolithic module. October 6 `ab65b8e` split it into `commands`, `model`, and `transaction` files (144 command lines, 83 model lines, 164 transaction lines at extraction), and `0e48843` added the module map. This made the ownership seams easier to inspect but did not add more presets, tests, or a separate persistence/authoring contract. The split is an organizational refactor, not evidence of a new preset lifecycle. The current preset is explicitly useful for composing reversible developer settings; broader extensibility and rollback atomicity remain unproven.
## October 26 — the game console transport is thread-safe at the boundary, but not a full process-output or operation stream

The transport has two distinct FIFO queues behind cloned `Arc<Mutex<...>>` handles: command submissions enter the Bevy-owned dispatcher, while structured `ConsoleRecord`s are consumed by the overlay and terminal adapter ([transport module and exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/console/transport/mod.rs>), [queue implementation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/console/transport/queue.rs>)). The record queue drops its oldest entry at 4,096 pending records; the command queue has no corresponding cap or rejection result. Mutex poison is recovered by taking the contained state. This is an explicit resilience policy, but for commands it can mean unbounded pending memory if a producer outruns dispatch; no load test was run.

The local record wraps the shared `vapor_telemetry::ConsoleRecord` with game-specific `origin`, `kind`, and optional `ConsoleCommandSource` ([record construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/console/transport/record.rs>)). Command source becomes the shared record's `target`; tracing becomes shared `source = "tracing"` and retains tracing target and visitor-collected fields. The record's wall-clock timestamp is Unix milliseconds, while the display label reduces it to time-of-day and discards date/timezone. The tracing visitor preserves named scalar/debug values as strings and suppresses events carrying Bevy's `tracy.frame_mark` field before record construction ([tracing adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/console/transport/tracing.rs>)). The shared record therefore provides interoperable structured values, but the game's `origin` and semantic `kind` remain local wrapper fields and its trace source does not identify Launcher, Studio, IDE, service, or composition.

The native terminal adapter starts a detached stdin reader thread that submits one command per line. It writes command/output/error records to stdout/stderr, clears only an interactive terminal, and deliberately leaves trace rendering to Bevy's ordinary logging layer ([terminal adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/console/transport/terminal.rs>)). It does not capture arbitrary child-process stdout/stderr, progress events, or Vapor Client operation lifecycles. This reconciles with the shared-console ambition only at the record-data and tracing-ingress seam; command execution still targets the game World, and the process/tool console remains another host adapter. The distinction is material: the queue is not the general long-running task/output service implied by users' desired unified console.

The October 6 `ab65b8e` console cleanup extracts a 374-line transport module into queue, record, terminal, and tracing responsibilities (410 inserted lines across the five paths). October 22 `c070bf3` changes the record payload to wrap Vapor's shared telemetry record and updates terminal field access, but retains the local game origin/kind wrapper, queues, and game command source. This is a meaningful data-contract convergence without transport or execution unification; it should not be counted as completion of the multi-product console goal. Existing source and historical diffs were inspected; no queue-pressure, thread-shutdown, process-capture, or cross-frontend integration behavior was run here.
## October 26 — World Draw is a reusable spatial snapshot API with a cached mesh path that rebuilds every collected frame

World Draw deliberately separates spatial marks from textual inspection. The public surface exports scalar range/color-ramp types, primitive and scalar-field descriptions, and a frame/batch submission API; setup installs a frame clear system and renderer ([module/API](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/draw/mod.rs>), [range and color ramp](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/draw/color/mod.rs>), [frame and batch contracts](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/draw/frame/mod.rs>)). A caller builds a `WorldDrawBatch` of lines/arrows/axes/rectangles/crosses/spheres and scalar fields. It submits that batch into a shared `WorldDrawFrame` guarded by an `RwLock`; scalar-field IDs are unique within a frame and duplicates panic, whereas primitives carry no ID or deduplication contract. The lock keeps producers independent from ECS `World` access in their data model, but `submit` is synchronous, has no bounded capacity, and fails by panic on a poisoned lock. The only current scalar-field identity is a static string `DrawId`; no lifetime/owner token is part of that key.

The schedule is the key integration contract. `DeveloperSet::ResolveFocus` clears the previous frame after transform propagation; later ordered sets collect World Draw submissions and finally render them. The renderer sends ordinary primitives through separate world/overlay Gizmo groups ([renderer wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/draw/render/mod.rs>), [primitive realization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/draw/render/primitives/mod.rs>)). The scalar-field side uses a cache keyed by `DrawId`, creates one entity/mesh/material per unseen ID, hides cached entities when a field is absent, and reuses the mesh/entity when that ID reappears ([scalar-field cache and mesh conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/draw/render/scalar_field/mod.rs>)). But it regenerates the complete mesh and replaces the mesh asset every time a field is present; it has no value/transform revision or change gate. The existing thermal coupling visualization submits a fixed 28×28 sample grid, so this source path rebuilds 1,458 triangles (4,374 non-indexed vertices) each frame while enabled. That workload is a source-derived cost, not a measured frame-time claim. Missing IDs are hidden but never removed from the cache, which is safe for the current small set of static IDs but not a reclamation policy for unbounded dynamic producers.

`ScalarRange::normalize` rejects non-finite scalar values and degenerate/non-finite widths, then clamps normalized values. `ColorRamp::sample_scalar` renders invalid samples magenta. However, public custom ramps are accepted without checking stop order, finiteness or duplicate positions; sampling assumes stops are ordered. Likewise `WorldScalarField` carries public resolution, size, opacity, values and height scale and relies on the mesh builder's limited structural checks (minimum resolution and exact value count); it has no whole-descriptor validation boundary. These are extension-contract gaps: fixed thermal producers supply known ranges, IDs and dimensions, but the exported API allows other Rust producers to construct malformed descriptors. No invalid-input or mesh-reuse test was run here.

The authoring boundary is real but still local to the Engine's developer-tooling API: thermal diagnostics and gizmo presentation produce batches; those producers do not own the renderer or alter thermal/gameplay authority ([thermal producer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/world_draw/mod.rs>), [transform-gizmo producer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/presentation/mod.rs>)). This is a good generalized facility compared with bespoke per-domain debug meshes. Its remaining semantics—ID ownership/lifecycle, descriptor validation, change-aware updates, and resource budgets—are not yet generalized into a plugin-managed registration or renderer contract. No rendering, profiling, or tests were run; findings are from current source and the described schedule.

## October 26 — Transform gizmo geometry is shared with picking, while edit authority remains opt-in raw-Transform mutation

The current gizmo has a clear visibility/authority split. It observes a focused entity with `Transform`, offers World/Local presentation settings, and draws translation arrows, rotation rings, scale handles and a center marker. The shared `AxisHandleGeometry` supplies both the rendered endpoints/ring and the hit-testing geometry, avoiding a separate visual-versus-pick model ([geometry and hit-testing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/geometry/mod.rs>), [World Draw presentation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/presentation/mod.rs>)). The transform inspection adapter adds typed translation/rotation/scale fields, but sets them Direct only for explicitly writable, unparented entities; it commits submitted inspection requests into that same runtime `Transform` ([inspection adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/inspection/mod.rs>)). The opt-in `EditorTransformWritable` marker and transient drag/settings state make this authority explicit and local, not a general semantic authoring API ([model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/model.rs>)).

`EditorTransformWritable` is granted by the in-game inspector's per-entity checkbox, not automatically by the presence of Transform. ChildOf entities are refused by both the UI and the mutation queries because the adapter does not preserve parent-space semantics. The in-game editor explains that direct edits may be overwritten by generated or authored sources. That caveat is accurate: this writes the current Bevy Transform and establishes no canonical source update, undo history, save contract or content edit. The direct editor is useful for live inspection/prototyping, but it is not equivalent to the planned Composer's source-aware edits.

Drag uses pointer position projected into the primary embedded viewport; `InputFocus` claims the pointer while a drag is active, and Escape restores the captured start Transform. Each frame reconstructs the candidate from the start snapshot and current cursor instead of accumulating deltas. Translation and rotation honor World/Local mode; scale intentionally stays local even in World mode, a choice visible in the inspector wording and implemented consistently in axis geometry and drag application ([interaction and drag lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/interaction/mod.rs>), [widget](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/widget.rs>), [plugin wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/mod.rs>)). This is a thoughtful direct-runtime gizmo, with a narrower contract than a generalized scene editor: only primary-view embedded interaction exists, all three operations are visible together, transform mode is one global resource, and there is no edit transaction beyond Escape-to-restore while dragging. The generic values/viewport interaction were not executed or tested in this audit.

The 40-segment projected rotation rings and 9-pixel picking thresholds are fixed constants. Gizmo world size is a clamped 12% of camera distance rather than an explicit viewport/FOV pixel-size contract. Scale follows a multiplicative cursor factor with a `0.01` lower bound but no matching upper bound. These are source facts; visual usability, near-plane behavior, high-DPI hit accuracy and extreme-value handling remain unverified. The module map exposes six responsibilities—model, widget, geometry, inspection, interaction and presentation—whose integration is explicit rather than six independent gizmo plugins.

## October 26 — portal domain commands describe a built-in pair, not a validated extensible portal graph

The public domain surface consists of endpoint identity, two persistent endpoint entities, active/sidedness state, a pair resource, traveler markers, optional velocity, and `PortalCommand` messages ([domain exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/mod.rs>), [command contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/command/mod.rs>), [endpoint and pair components](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/portal/mod.rs>), [traveler state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/traveler/mod.rs>)). The command protocol is the intended mutation route, but it is not enforced by visibility: `Portal`, `PortalActive`, `PortalPair`, and endpoint `Transform` are public ECS data, and external systems can write them directly. The command handler only operates the two entities named by `PortalPair`; this is a persistent built-in pair, not an arbitrary endpoint registry or graph. Commands sent before the pair resource exists are drained and discarded. Placement proposals rejected by unit-scale, support-fit, or coplanar-overlap checks are also silently skipped: there is no result message, rejection reason, or diagnostic in this protocol ([command application and validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/control/mod.rs>), [support and overlap policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/placement/mod.rs>)).

Configuration establishes several useful numeric bounds, but uses startup assertions rather than a recoverable validation result. Aperture dimensions and render scale must be positive, endpoint scale must be unit, and visual recursion is capped at four; the configured default depth is two ([configuration and assertions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/config.rs>)). The current portal-placement command separately enforces unit scale, resolves the proposed aperture against one clip-capable host, and rejects positive-area overlap with the other active endpoint. Traversal then detects a plane sign change in portal-local coordinates and checks the interpolated crossing point against the rectangular half-size; rigid mapping is source inverse → local half-turn → destination transform ([crossing math](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/topology/crossing/mod.rs>), [rigid mapping](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/topology/mapping/mod.rs>), [whole-body traversal](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/traversal/mod.rs>)). For a segment that crosses more than one active portal, the traversal loop stops at the first matching query item rather than selecting the smallest crossing fraction. Since query iteration is not a geometric ordering contract, this is a source-confirmed ordering ambiguity for high-distance-per-step motion; no such case was executed. The split traveler follows another path, so this observation is specific to the conventional whole-body fallback.

The type comments explicitly scope `PortalRigidSplitBody` to the current pairwise Avian adapter and distinguish it from generic USF authority partitions; `PortalVelocity` is an optional linear-velocity component for the conventional traversal fallback. This is important restraint against reading “portal topology” as an already-general graph or one unified physics authority. At the same time, the intended API boundary remains documentation-level while the ECS data is writable, and user-visible command failures lack a structured return path. Those are different gaps: one is mutation ownership enforcement, the other is observability. The portal topology debug visualizer is also not wired by `PortalPlugin`; its `configure` function is called from the Loo-Cast Game developer-tools composition and submits into `DeveloperSet::CollectWorldDraw` ([visualizer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/devtools/mod.rs>), [game developer-tools wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/mod.rs>)). This is consistent with the inspected current app but means importing Portal alone does not expose this diagnostic. Rebase refresh and semantic spatial-transition reset are separate Engine event adapters: they rebuild or retire disposable local crossing/split cache without converting canonical USF deltas inside portal state ([cross-cutting adapters](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/systems.rs>), [plugin schedule and module composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/mod.rs>), [simulation responsibility map](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/mod.rs>), [directed-face enumeration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/face/mod.rs>), [domain module map](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/topology/mod.rs>)). The portal command/domain/topology paths were inspected as source; no runtime, test, or collision outcome was exercised in this audit.

## October 26 — stencil fitting is cuboid-specific and currently has no retained focused tests

Portal placement delegates to a public reusable `fit_rectangular_stencil` API, but its current source geometry enum has only `Cuboid`, so “generic” currently means a portal-independent API over one support shape, not general convex or mesh support ([source shape](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/source.rs>), [public fit/support entrypoints](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/stencil_fit/mod.rs>)). Hosts are required to have unit scale. The requested portal normal must align within dot `0.999` of a host face normal and lie within the caller's plane tolerance; fitting snaps the aperture center to that plane, quantizes roll to the nearest quarter-turn orientation, then clamps or magnetizes both tangential coordinates so the full rectangle fits. It reports correction distance and how many edges snapped. Callers provide all tolerances and bounds; negative values are clamped to zero at the API boundary ([axis helpers](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/stencil_fit/axes.rs>), [fit algorithm](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/stencil_fit/placement.rs>), [strict no-correction predicate](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/stencil_fit/support.rs>)). Portal supplies 0.025m plane tolerance, 1.50m maximum center correction and 0.50m edge magnet distance, so its fit permits displacement up to the maximum plus the plane tolerance. Portal config separately requires positive aperture size; the public generic fit API itself does not validate half-size, host extents, or finite transforms, so callers other than the portal path must honor sensible inputs.

The algorithm preserves a useful distinction: `supports_rectangular_stencil` is a strict predicate for callers that want a boolean without correction, while `fit_rectangular_stencil` is a nearby placement resolver. The source geometry enum currently contains only cuboids; adding another shape would also require updating the collision-topology rebuild consumer, not only this fitter. The inspected fit/support files contain no focused tests now. Source history shows they originally had tests; absence is a regression-coverage fact, not proof that a specific geometric case fails. No geometry test or runtime placement was run.

### History and confidence

September 19 `f43573f` introduced the 290-line monolithic fit module plus a 66-line test file. The tests exercised flush support, quarter-turn quantization, fit correction and size rejection. October 5 `e987230` removed those 66 test lines; October 6 `ab65b8e` then extracted axis helpers, placement correction, and strict support into the current three implementation modules, and `0e48843` added the module map and public exports. The split made the distinction between fitting and strict support easier to locate, but it did not restore the removed cases. Current behavior is source-derived; the earlier tests were not executed and their historical presence does not establish passing status. Portal consumption is documented in the [domain/topology review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--portal-domain-commands-describe-a-built-in-pair-not-a-validated-extensible-portal-graph).

## October 26 — collision topology derives real Avian colliders from authored stencil state

`CollisionStencil` is authored ECS state; `CollisionTopologyState` is a system-local index that groups enabled stencils by target host and marks affected hosts dirty. Changes/removals to stencil components and changes to clip-source/host `Transform` mark hosts; active stencil order is sorted by entity bits before fingerprinting/rebuild. The fingerprint includes the host transform only when cuts exist, then the effective stencil entity IDs, transforms, half-sizes and clearances. An unchanged fingerprint avoids replacing the collider. The rebuilt Avian `Collider` is therefore the actual collision surface shared by ordinary casts/contacts, rather than a portal-specific raycast/filter ([stencil and state model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/state.rs>), [dirty-host reconciliation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/systems.rs>), [public module/reexports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/mod.rs>)).

The reconstruction is deliberately lossy in shape support: the immutable source is currently a cuboid, each rectangular cut is converted to six host-local clipping planes, and sequential convex subtraction emits an Avian convex hull or compound of surviving pieces ([source type](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/source.rs>), [CSG decomposition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/csg/mod.rs>)). If the host has non-unit scale or conversion yields no valid collider, the caller falls back to the original uncut collider. That conservative failure mode retains solid collision—an aperture can become blocked—but avoids silently removing the whole host. No diagnostic records that fallback, and no piece/cut budget is enforced by this source. A source-level invalidation gap also exists for external direct writes: `Changed<Collider>` is not a dirty-host trigger, so replacing an already-derived host collider alone does not request reconstruction; a later stencil, source, or Transform change can trigger it.

The collider system queries local `Transform`, not `GlobalTransform`, while stencil documentation calls its geometry world-space. That is coherent for the current unparented host path; for parented clip hosts, the coordinate assumptions would need an explicit parent-aware check before treating this as valid. This is a conditional integration risk, not a confirmed current bad placement. The fitter, CSG and state paths are deterministic in their explicit sort/plane policy, but source alone does not prove convex-hull validity, collision equivalence, or budget suitability. No tests, runtime collision or profile were run.

### History and confidence

September 12 `6241440` introduces the first 588-line collision-topology/CSG source, explicitly replacing portal-specific subtraction logic with immutable source shapes and derived collision topology. September 19 `f43573f` removes the then-large source module while adding the separate stencil-fit surface and tests. On October 5, `e987230` deletes those fitter tests and trims the CSG module; October 6 `ab65b8e` extracts dirty-state indexing and collider reconciliation into `state.rs`/`systems.rs`, while splitting the fitter; `0e48843` adds API/module maps. The progression is from portal-specific collision clipping toward a reusable collision-topology system, then responsibility extraction. It has not yet expanded beyond cuboid sources, added observable fallback results, or reintroduced focused CSG/fit tests. The original architectural premise is source history, not runtime evidence; see the [stencil-fit chronology](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md#september-19october-6-2026--portal-stencil-fitting-separates-surface-snapping-from-strict-support).

## October 26 — input focus is a shared set of manual claims, not a lease or priority arbiter

`InputFocus` is a small global Bevy resource with separate sets of static-string owners for pointer and gameplay claims. A modal helper inserts/removes one owner in both sets; consumers see only whether either set is nonempty. There is no priority, winner, reason, scoped token, RAII lease, or automatic cleanup when an owner despawns. Two producers reusing the same owner string alias one set entry, so one can clear the other's effective claim; current in-tree owners use distinct constants, but the API does not enforce uniqueness ([resource and claim semantics](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/input_focus/mod.rs>)). The `InputFocusSet::Resolve` enum is a scheduling anchor rather than an active resolver system: producers are ordered before it, and concrete cursor/gameplay adapters consume the resulting aggregate state after that point.

The resume epoch is a separate edge-trigger mechanism. Dismissing the console or creative menu increments a wrapping `u64`; `CursorCapture` remembers the last observed epoch and interprets a change as persistent intent to recapture the gameplay pointer. That request remains suppressed while focus is claimed, then can become active after unblocking ([player cursor consumer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/cursor/mod.rs>), [console return path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/console/mod.rs>), [gizmo claim adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/gizmo/mod.rs>)). This keeps one overlay from directly owning cursor visibility and avoids discarding player intent when a modal temporarily borrows the pointer. Its limit is equally clear: claims are manually maintained by every producer, aggregate-only reads cannot explain who blocks input, and a missed release can leave input suppressed. The type itself has no plugin or cleanup policy; callers initialize it and obey the shared scheduling convention. No interactive input test was run.

### History and confidence

September 19 `473314b` introduces the 54-line generic resource, explicitly avoiding knowledge of consoles, editors, inventories or the player; September 20 `52d13eb` adds the gameplay-resume epoch so modal dismissal can restore capture intent. Later editor/gizmo and console integrations reuse that contract rather than giving each UI its own cursor arbitration. The original abstraction is deliberately simple and genuinely shared, but its ownership safety rests on globally unique string constants and balanced set/unset calls. The history does not show scoped claims, stale-owner recovery, diagnostics, or priority; that is a source-limited observation, not proof that current owner callsites leak claims.

## October 26 — view helpers centralize viewport coordinates while the product state remains one global primary view

The `view` module is a contract layer, not a view plugin. It defines the `PrimaryGameView` marker, one global `PrimaryViewPresentation` enum (`Immersive` or `Embedded`), a normalized-ray constructor, logical target/local viewport conversions, and one USF render-layer constant ([view module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/view/mod.rs>)). `ViewportSpace` consistently asks Bevy for the camera's logical viewport rectangle; target-to-local conversion rejects points outside it, and target-to-world ray conversion uses Bevy camera projection rather than hand-built window offsets. Editor shell code remains responsible for translating egui physical/logical coordinates and assigning a camera viewport; cursor, focus badge and gizmo consumers share the conversion helper.

This is a useful, low-cost centralization of coordinate conventions, but it does not itself provide independently owned view contexts. `PrimaryViewPresentation` is a global resource, and many consumers query one `PrimaryGameView` through `Single`; a primary marker can describe a sub-rectangle, but the API does not identify multiple logical views or provide per-view presentation mode. The types also rely on callers: `ViewRay::new` normalizes and rejects a zero direction, but its public fields permit bypassing that constructor, and it does not reject non-finite origin/direction inputs. `local_to_target` accepts coordinates equal to the viewport size, whereas containment behavior is delegated to Bevy's `Rect`. No multi-window, multi-camera, high-DPI or edge-coordinate runtime check was done. The separate USF demand snapshot's multi-camera storage must not be confused with this singular gameplay/editor view abstraction.

### History and confidence

September 19 `473314b` adds the initial 118-line coordinate/view contract. September 23 `8f3eb98` adds `ViewSubjectPresentation` to keep self-visibility as view policy rather than mutating portal or physical identity. Later the same day, `baf3e95` adds `USF_PRESENTATION_LAYER` and documents its semantic-observer camera-origin rule and render-layer ownership. October 6 `0e48843` removes only a redundant blank line in this module; the meaningful API remains essentially the September contract. This chronology shows a deliberately small shared surface accruing one presentation responsibility, not an implemented multi-view manager. The current-state comparison already describes how the in-game editor shell and Vapor IDE differ ([view contract cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#view-coordinate-contract-is-shared-but-the-primary-presentation-resource-is-singular)).
## October 26 — character motor separates device intent, contact truth, and fixed-tick integration

`CharacterMovementIntent` is a device-agnostic component: world-space wish direction, analog speed fraction, speed multiplier, held jump, and a one-shot jump latch. The motor expects adapters to write it before fixed simulation and does not read keyboard, camera, or Player state. Setters clamp scalar inputs, but the fields remain public, so the contract is conventional rather than enforced against arbitrary ECS writes. `CharacterGroundState` is more strongly owned: contact and transition flags are private, groundedness is exactly `contact.is_some()`, and consumers get accessors rather than writable duplicate grounded/entity/normal fields. `CharacterGroundContact` names the collider and support normal; its constructor normalizes the normal but accepts a zero result ([intent](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/input.rs>), [ground state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/state.rs>)).

The fixed controller's order is semantically significant: clear transition flags; depenetrate; refresh support; capture prior groundedness; integrate movement intent and first-half airborne gravity; select a step/slide route and project velocity; apply second-half gravity if still airborne; finalize support; derive landing/leaving flags; consume jump press. A grounded jump removes contact before route selection and therefore enters air acceleration in that same tick. This sequence is concentrated in the controller, while velocity equations live in `movement/`; the module split improves local readability but does not make update order independent ([controller](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/mod.rs>), [integration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/movement/mod.rs>)).

History clarifies that the ownership improvement was deliberate. `83f20d9` introduced separate config, input, math, state, plugin, and controller modules. `6eb90b2` added an adapter-level speed multiplier rather than requiring sprint/crouch adapters to mutate immutable movement tuning. `e2b9282` replaced a public bundle of independently writable grounded/contact/transition fields with private optional contact and explicit transition operations, so contradictory grounded state is no longer constructible through those public fields. October 6 `0e48843` renamed `CharacterMovementInput` to `CharacterMovementIntent`, extracted controller subdomains, and retained the ordered motor orchestration. This is a sound invariant-strengthening move, though public intent fields still bypass scalar validation and no focused motor tests remain in the inspected current source. No build, tests, physics run, or timing experiment was performed. See [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#character-movement-has-three-frame-owners-with-different-update-cadences).
## October 26 — character movement math is Quake-derived with chart conversion only for selected quantities

The standalone math helpers implement Source/Quake-style acceleration: acceleration is bounded by remaining parallel wish speed; air acceleration caps the speed used to compute remaining parallel allowance but intentionally uses uncapped wish speed in the acceleration magnitude; friction drops speed without reversing it; `reject` removes the component along the supplied axis. These helpers assume normalized directions/axes at their call boundary; the motor normalizes planar wish direction and gets locomotion-up from its frame adapter, but the public math functions themselves do not normalize or validate their inputs ([math](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/math.rs>), [motor normalization and use](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/controller/movement/mod.rs>)).

The `source_2013` config is explicit about being a lineage label rather than exact source parity. It keeps SI-labelled dimensions and movement distances, sets gravity response to 2.0720634 (mapping Earth gravity to about 20.32 m/s²), jump to 9.144 m/s, ground speed to 8.128 m/s, air wish cap to 0.762 m/s, and step height to 0.4572 m; its docs call out stronger friction and higher jump than the reference. Chart resolution converts length-like values and physical gravity, with a finite f32 clamp for converted gravity components. Acceleration, friction, surface friction, and min-ground-dot remain unscaled coefficients. That may be an intentional local gameplay response, but no current source contract here establishes whether the entire motor should remain scale-equivalent. Config fields are public and reflected, and unlike the single gravity multiplier there is no comprehensive validation pass before values enter the solver ([preset and dimensional constants](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/character/config.rs>)).

The deleted tests make the evidence boundary unusually clear. Before October 5 `e987230`, math tests checked wish-speed overshoot, non-reversing friction, air-cap parallel gain, and projection; config tests checked the Earth fall-response preset and speed/jump conversion at a nonzero spatial scale. That is useful evidence of intended local invariants, but coverage did not test all coefficients, multiple scales, invalid config values, or integrated collision movement. The cleanup removed 113 lines across the math, config, and frame test modules, and the current character subtree has no replacement focused tests in these files. No tests were run. See [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#character-math-and-tuning-are-si-labelled-but-only-partially-chart-verified).

The character module documents the intended engine boundary: the motor owns movement semantics; Avian supplies collision queries; camera, local-player input, networking, and prediction are adapters. History shows this collector began as `observability.rs`, was renamed to `devtools.rs` during the September 13 developer-tools redesign (`78082f4`), was moved into `devtools/mod.rs` in the September 19 module cleanup (`473314b`), and later adopted the World Draw collection API. The chronology shows integration into shared infrastructure, not a deeper physics trace. No visualization was rendered or profiled. See the [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#character-physics-is-generic-by-contract-but-its-debug-view-is-opt-in-and-shallow).
## October 26 — generic spatial demand and USF residency are separate, but residency expansion has no total-work bound

`SpatialDemandSource` is only a bounded-interest declaration. Collection converts metric-authored extents at the source's current scale, resolves its transform into the canonical chart, and adds a separate, priority-biased demand at a pending relocation destination. The destination is keyed through logical realization ownership so coverage can be prepared before a coverage-gated rechart; a too-small current-chart footprint does not suppress a useful destination request ([demand contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/demand/mod.rs>), [collection and relocation projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/demand/systems.rs>)). Motion hints are kept in a separate snapshot and only finite nonzero canonical velocities are included, so velocity churn need not invalidate the scope snapshot. Sorting scopes by source/scale/priority stabilizes collection order, but does not create a global priority budget or select which subsystem realizes data.

`UsfContextResidency` then turns those scopes into an ancestor-closed set of canonical contexts; it stores direct demand counts/priorities, parent/child topology and a cached range plan. It explicitly does not own voxel data, colliders, fields or render readiness. Equal range plans short-circuit graph construction, while changed plans rebuild the full graph and bump the public revision only if the materialized context map differs ([resident facts and queries](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/model.rs>), [range-to-graph planner](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/plan.rs>), [continuous-to-integer range conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/range.rs>), [request/reconcile schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/systems.rs>), [module contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/mod.rs>)).

The important limitation is resource governance. Range conversion checks finiteness through its checked integer offsets and rejects coordinates outside `i32`, but it does not cap the number of cells in a valid box. The planner synchronously iterates every cell in every range, then walks each cell's ancestors. A large finite extent can therefore produce an enormous update even when every individual endpoint is representable. `first_missing_intersecting` repeats a full-box scan when the entire requested range is already resident. This is a source-confirmed worst-case work gap, not a reproduced hang; ordinary authored extents were not measured. A second semantic caution is that `reconcile_from_scopes` retains the previous graph on conversion failure, so an invalid new demand is logged while stale residency remains visible; callers must not mistake “last valid graph” for current-demand coverage. `UsfContextResidency::iter` exposes `HashMap` values and therefore has no deterministic iteration-order contract. Current voxel use asks membership/missing-context questions rather than depending on this iteration order, but external consumers could accidentally make output order unstable.

The sequence is a substantial redesign rather than a mere cache optimization. September 24's `b454b6f7` replaces context-topology and hierarchical gravity-cache machinery with sparse ancestor-closed residency, while gravity sampling becomes direct over source entities; September 28's `757aab1` adds the range-plan cache to avoid rebuilding when motion stays in the same canonical footprint; October 6's `0e48843` extracts the subsystem into model/plan/range/systems modules. The current cross-reference correctly distinguishes context presence from capability realization and records the unbounded-box risk ([cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#demand-residency-and-realization-bounded-later-work-no-end-to-end-planning-bound)). The intended reduction in cache inconsistency and repeated graph work is visible in code, but a worst-case work bound, scheduling budget, or runtime latency proof is absent. This review read the involved source and relevant diffs; it did not run a stress case or runtime profile.

## October 26 — capability coverage is persistent producer evidence; refinement is a separate branch request

The capability layer has two publication routes: a concrete disposable runtime realization component, or a batched set of bounded facts attached to a producer entity. Reconciliation runs after `UsfCapabilitySet::Publish`, rebuilds only when relevant components change or disappear, sorts facts by lifecycle identity, and indexes them by semantic authority and scale ([capability module contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/capability/mod.rs>), [realization/publication/coverage records](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/capability/model.rs>), [persistent snapshot/index](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/capability/snapshot.rs>), [reconciliation schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/capability/systems.rs>)). A published `UsfScaleCoverage` is an AABB-like scale-local bound plus roles and producer revision; `is_within` tests a point against that bounded box with an optional radius. It does not independently inspect dense voxels, Avian manifolds, query-provider state, or a future motion corridor. That is a deliberate producer-evidence contract: correctness belongs to producers, and callers must not reinterpret “coverage” as complete collision proof.

`UsfScaleRoleMask` separates live realization, presentation, local collision/response, editing and a declared non-authoritative `COLLISION_QUERY` role ([role vocabulary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/capability/roles.rs>)). The query role currently has no Rust producer or consumer; canonical flight uses a direct query-frame/provider path instead. `COLLISION` therefore means backend contact/response capability and must not be treated as the swept-query role. Optional authority-scoped coverage is materially stronger than global `has_near`: a caller omitting authority can be admitted by any nearby same-scale provider with the requested role. Existing call sites use both forms, apparently for different ownership needs; the unscoped form is not safe to summarize as “the controlled body's own capability.”

`SpatialRefinementDemand` separately asks for a finer capability tip. `UsfRefinementPlan` intersects that tip with a supported-slice mask, emits the ancestor branch from coarser context to tip, tapers each step's extent by decimal scale exponent, and attaches a native residency halo and priority ([refinement module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/refinement/mod.rs>), [request component](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/refinement/demand.rs>), [branch policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/refinement/plan.rs>)). The request and plan do not prove that any step has been built or is ready; later producers publish that fact through the separate capability layer. This split cleanly names intent, planning and evidence, but the end-to-end interpretation remains distributed across providers and admission callers.

The source history shows the boundary being made explicit: `2482e0d` creates the generic capability/coverage surface and removes much of the then-monolithic refinement implementation; `65a3b1c` and `295362f` continue its transition/readiness integration; `0e48843` splits current capability roles, facts, snapshot and system into separate modules and extracts refinement demand/plan files. The reviewed source and call sites support that conceptual lineage. They do not establish that every producer publishes correct bounds/revisions, that unscoped readiness is appropriate in every context, or that the unused query role has a committed future consumer. No tests or runtime transitions were run.


## October 26 — scale-local granularity is bounded by policy, but the public solver can still emit infinity

`SpatialRealizationGranularityRequest` is a pure policy calculator: it sanitizes non-finite/negative scalar inputs to fallbacks, clamps desired spacing and validity duration to caller bounds, and chooses spacing from either a desired footprint or a motion/latency guard. Its output carries spacing, aggregate extent, validity radius, and validity duration, but no units or validation status beyond field names ([request and solver](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/realization.rs#L3-L78>), [result accessors](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/realization.rs#L80-L113>)). `positive` and `non_negative` reject NaN/infinity at input, but finite `f64` values may still overflow during multiplication: `speed * validity_seconds` can become infinity, which is then returned as `validity_radius_metres`; `expected * multiplier` can overflow before min/max constrain the value. The solver therefore does not guarantee finite outputs for all accepted finite inputs. This is a source-confirmed numeric-contract gap at extreme magnitudes, not evidence that normal gameplay inputs currently reach it.

The present voxel caller fixes minimum and maximum spacing to the materialization chunk extent, uses one sample and one target aggregate, and consumes only `validity_seconds` to form a predicted offset; it does not consume the solver's spacing, aggregate extent, or validity radius ([caller policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/motion.rs#L5-L82>)). Consequently, the abstraction is presently a general-looking wrapper around one bounded latency-horizon choice, rather than a shared general resolution planner in active use. The generic demand source separately expresses its authored metre extents as `Vec3<f32>` and converts them with a saturating `f32` adapter at the chosen scale ([demand source](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/demand/mod.rs#L26-L80>), [conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/mod.rs#L129-L144>)); this is intentionally bounded for local chart data, but loses the distinction between an out-of-range request and an exact saturated request.

USF chart algebra itself has a clearer boundary: `UsfChart` is a pure origin-plus-scale projection API, while `UsfRuntimeChartState` owns the maintained origin/rebase history in the spatial runtime ([pure chart](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/chart.rs#L7-L49>), [chart delta](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/chart.rs#L51-L104>), [runtime state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/chart/mod.rs#L29-L89>)). Cross-scale rebase first preflights root transforms, physics positions and collider leaves through one shared membership resolver; only then it moves the canonical origin, offsets root transforms in each chart, and emits a representation-change event for the Avian adapter ([scale membership](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/chart/membership.rs#L8-L20>), [rebase transaction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/chart/rebase.rs#L18-L129>)). This is a deliberate representation/authority separation. However, chart projection accepts a caller-provided bound and its chart type carries no metric/error metadata; correctness depends on callers selecting the appropriate bound and handling `UsfPositionError` rather than treating projection as universally available.

History traces the pure chart through September 26 `569c781`, then adds `UsfChartDelta` in September 27 `f13b31c`; October 6 `0e48843` separates runtime maintenance into `spatial/chart` and leaves USF algebra under `usf/chart`. The granularity request first appears on October 2 in `cb094c1`, then is relocated into `spatial/realization.rs` by October 6 `0e48843`. These are small but consequential ownership moves: chart math became an explicit pure USF surface while runtime rebasing remained engine-owned, whereas realization granularity became a public policy type whose only inspected consumer uses a narrow subset of its result. Exact current source was inspected; no tests, benchmarks, or extreme-input execution were run.


### Follow-up — lossy scale re-expression has callers with different semantic needs

The first review identified that `UsfPosition::reexpressed_at` can coarsen a value by folding lower-scale digits into the parent `f32` residual. A callsite sweep clarifies that this operation currently serves several different purposes without a distinct approximate-value type or return flag: `UsfChunkAddress::containing` resolves a coordinate into coarser topology; generic residency rounds a demand center to the demand scale; `VoxelFrame::frame_to_world` returns a query position at the frame scale; celestial terrain initialization re-expresses body origin for each realization; voxel medium sampling projects a body point into its scale-local world; and `VoxelWorld` aligns query points with the world origin's leaf before calculating an integer lattice key ([chunk topology](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/chunk_address.rs#L17-L29>), [residency demand](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/range.rs#L7-L26>), [voxel frame](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/frame.rs#L62-L84>), [celestial realization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_realization.rs#L140-L206>), [medium sampling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/medium/mod.rs#L29-L51>), [world lattice-key conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/world/mod.rs#L111-L130>)). Some are explicitly representation projections; the lattice-key path determines cell identity. This makes the unresolved contract sharper: canonical position storage is hierarchical, but a method named “re-expressed” may discard information when coarsening, and callers that use its result as a new address/key need a stated quantization rule and boundary evidence.

The offset itself is `f32` and bounded to a 1000-native-unit chunk. Its physical resolution therefore changes with the leaf scale: at large metre-per-native scales, one residual ULP may span substantial physical distance. The historical 23-test suite included re-expression round-trip tolerances and an authored-f64 comparison, but was removed at October 5 `e987230`; it did not certify exactness. No current source test, numeric edge execution, or gameplay symptom was reproduced here. The finite-root wrap is an explicit design in the arithmetic comments and earlier plan, while the callsite-specific coarsening/error contract remains unresolved. This distinction prevents a requested finite domain from being mislabeled an accidental defect while still surfacing the user-visible question of precision at topology/materialization boundaries.

### Follow-up — extreme rechart velocity conversion can consume a relocation without applying it

`SpatialScale` accepts the full inclusive S−35…S+35 range, but the transition applier unconditionally computes the native-velocity conversion factor as `10^(previous exponent − target exponent)` in `f32`, before checking whether the subject even has a `LinearVelocity` fallback or uses a policy that needs this factor. A requested S+35→S−35 transition computes `10^70`, rejects the non-finite result, and returns after admission has already consumed the one-shot relocation and marked the target handoff active. Unlike a coverage miss, this branch does not requeue the request, so that requested transition can be lost while the interaction state still records a pending target. The reverse S−35→S+35 factor underflows to zero; it is finite, so a subject with only `LinearVelocity` and `PreserveCanonical` can have that velocity multiplied to zero rather than preserving canonical motion. The factor is also unnecessary for `Zero`, `PreserveNative`, and the branch where `UsfCanonicalMotion` supplies the destination velocity ([scale range](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/mod.rs#L28-L30>), [unconditional factor and early return](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/apply.rs#L134-L145>), [fallback policy branches](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/apply.rs#L15-L44>), [one-shot queue consumption](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/intent.rs#L221-L244>), [admission sets requested handoff before apply](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/admission.rs#L115-L143>)).

This is a source-proven extreme-range failure path, not a reproduced ordinary gameplay defect. The range is part of the advertised 71-scale model, and callers can issue a one-shot request across it; no test was run. The conversion needs to be policy/component-specific and range-aware, and failed application needs to preserve/reject the request explicitly rather than strand its requested handoff state. The same API boundary has a related input limitation: `TransitionCoverageRequirement::new` clamps negative radii but retains positive infinity; the downstream bounded position query rejects a non-finite projection bound, so the result is a permanently unsatisfiable coverage requirement, not permissive coverage ([radius construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/transition/intent.rs#L19-L39>), [bounded projection rejects non-finite bounds](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/relative.rs#L192-L204>)).


## October 26 — semantic frames validate orientation weakly; runtime eligibility checks displacement but not velocity projection

`UsfSemanticFrame` centralizes orientation-only ownership and keeps world position on the ordinary `UsfPosition` component. This avoids a second mutable spatial anchor, and local/world frame conversions are explicit. Its public quaternion constructor checks finite components and a nonzero squared length, then normalizes, but it does not check that `length_squared()` itself remains finite. A finite quaternion with components near `1e200` can overflow its squared norm to infinity; normalization then has no finite-unit guarantee. `advanced` similarly accepts finite angular velocity and time, multiplies them, and passes the resulting axis/angle onward without checking that the product or length stayed finite. Those are extreme numeric-input gaps in a public math API, not observed gameplay failures ([frame contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/semantic_frame.rs#L26-L108>)).

The corresponding physical-motion adapter has a concrete cross-boundary mismatch. `runtime_step_is_representable` decides whether to use runtime physics from the *next displacement* after `f64 → f32` conversion and adding that displacement to the current local position; it applies a 1e-3 relative vector error threshold ([eligibility calculation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/motion.rs#L18-L60>)). The locomotion decision uses this result to choose `RuntimePhysics` versus `CanonicalKinematics`, and the transition code copies canonical velocity into Avian through `native_velocity` ([authority decision](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/state/policy.rs#L183-L215>), [velocity handoff](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/locomotion/runtime/state/systems.rs#L84-L110>)). But `native_velocity` saturates each component at `f32::MAX` rather than reporting an unrepresentable velocity ([adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/motion.rs#L135-L163>)). A sufficiently short step can therefore be position-representable while the velocity value itself is not; authority can move to runtime with a saturated velocity, after which the runtime-to-canonical sync reads that saturated value. This is a source-derived possible loss path at extreme speed/scale/delta combinations. It is not a diagnosis of the reported 147 km/s surface case, and no transition was executed.

`world_to_local_metres` bounds relative chart displacement in native units, converts to metres and rotates, but returns `Ok` without a final finiteness check ([conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/semantic_frame.rs#L97-L108>)). Within the legal 71-scale `UsfPosition` domain the represented physical range is finite and far below `f64` overflow, so this appears protected by the current representation envelope; the public `max_abs_native` parameter alone does not document that dependency. The surrounding types also differ in maturity: `UsfSemanticBounds` is a spherical conservative-envelope component consumed by view observation, while `UsfKinematicFrameState` is a public snapshot combining origin, orientation and `UsfCanonicalMotion` but has no reader in current source ([bounds contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/semantic_bounds.rs#L5-L29>), [kinematic snapshot](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/kinematic_frame.rs#L5-L47>), [view observation consumer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/view/systems.rs#L175-L205>)). The unused value type is authored API surface, not an integrated moving-frame simulation facility.

History shows the semantic orientation and canonical motion arriving with October 6 celestial-motion integration (`117ca494`), while October 6 `0e48843` puts `kinematic_frame.rs` and the related modules into the current Spatial boundary. That reorganization makes the public frame/motion split easier to see; it does not prove the broad kinematic snapshot is consumed or the finite numeric paths are safe. Current source was inspected, but no unit tests, numerical probes, or runtime behavior were exercised.

### Follow-up — the in-game hierarchy has three different trees, with one unreachable-depth boundary

The word “hierarchy” now covers three distinct structures: Bevy `ChildOf` transform parentage; editor-only `EditorGroupOf` organization; and USF semantic→authority-partition→realization relationships. The editor grouping type explicitly avoids transform parenting and simulation ownership, and `Hierarchy` renders its groups above the Bevy-inspector tree after filtering editor artifacts/groups out of that second tree. The separate `Structure` tab instead projects domain-submitted named items for the current focus; it is not a component dump. That separation is a meaningful response to the owner's request for semantic editor grouping without transform side effects, but the UI does not label the three graphs with a common hierarchy taxonomy ([editor group relationship and renderer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/hierarchy/mod.rs#L1-L131>), [tab routing and filtered ECS hierarchy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/tabs/mod.rs#L24-L57>), [Structure item/frame contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/structure/mod.rs#L1-L118>)).

There is a source-confirmed visibility mismatch in editor-group nesting. `can_group` permits ancestor walks up to 64 links, while `draw_group_node` stops rendering at depth 32. A valid insertion can therefore make a nested group and its descendants disappear from the group tree. The one focused test checks cycle rejection and absence of `ChildOf`, but not depth boundaries, duplicate names, orphan cleanup, or the visible/unreachable case. The UI creates groups and can move/remove selected entities, but exposes no rename/delete operation; membership is relationship-backed and updates its target list, while group naming remains generic `Name` data. This is a small editor usability/ownership seam, not a runtime hierarchy or simulation bug. The relationship and test arrived in October 9 `46e1eac`; current source confirms the two limits, but no UI run was performed.

Developer focus is one shared snapshot with precedence pinned→selected→hovered. A `FocusTarget` records both the concrete spatial entity and its semantic entity, which lets the inspector inspect a manifestation while showing its semantic owner. `prune_focus` only checks that both entities still exist; it does not re-resolve or validate the realization→semantic mapping. If a live relationship changes while both entities remain alive, selected or pinned focus can continue to refer to the former semantic owner until another focus action replaces it. This is conditional on ownership changing during a persistent focus and was not reproduced ([focus target/resource and pruning](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/focus/mod.rs#L1-L109>), [focus acquisition from hierarchy selection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/hierarchy/mod.rs#L133-L157>)).

The editor shell is a fixed, in-memory dock layout; all tabs are non-closeable and barred from detached windows, and its default tree is rebuilt from hard-coded 75/20/58/66.6% splits at resource initialization. This means user docking choices are not persisted by the inspected shell resource. F2 embeds/returns the primary Game view, and the editor plugin is installed by `DeveloperToolsPlugin`; the F2 path itself does not check `DeveloperTools::enabled()` or a Vapor role. Those facts describe a developer tool reachable in the current executable, not evidence that player-facing releases expose or should expose it. Tab definitions, toolbar, and viewport conversion are separate source files, but their shared shell state and one docking layout make the current product an in-game editor surface, not the separate workspace IDE shown in the owner's mockup ([shell state/layout and F2 path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/mod.rs#L12-L134>), [tab routing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/tabs/mod.rs>), [toolbar](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/toolbar/mod.rs>), [viewport conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/viewport/mod.rs>)).

### Follow-up — the scalar workbench validates by execution and hides live-call failures

The “Compile” path is not syntax-only for the one bound target. `compile_and_validate` compiles the Rhai source, then invokes `transform(preview_input)` for `debug.freecam.speed`; changing the preview input repeats that call, and `commit` compiles/executes again when no candidate matches the exact current buffer. Since the host registers `print`/`debug` and explicit logging functions, these preview/commit operations can emit Bevy logs. The advertised scalar contract is therefore type/finite-output checked at a sample input, but not purity checked or side-effect free ([document target and validator](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/script_workbench/document.rs#L25-L45>), [candidate/commit lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/script_workbench/document.rs#L145-L230>), [host logging registrations](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/script_workbench/host.rs#L110-L163>), [workbench module ownership map](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/script_workbench/mod.rs#L1-L29>)).

More importantly for observability, `transform_live_scalar` calls the committed AST at the actual runtime input and returns the original input on *any* call error, including non-finite output, operation-limit error, or a function failure. It neither logs nor updates the script document diagnostic. A script that passes the fixed preview input can therefore fail for another runtime value while remaining marked Live and Committed, with behavior silently reverting to the Rust-provided speed. This fallback is fail-soft and protects the caller from invalid output, but erases the evidence needed to understand why the script seems ineffective. This is confirmed in source; no failing script was executed ([live call and fallback](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/script_workbench/workspace.rs#L94-L103>), [finite-output error](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/script_workbench/document.rs#L231-L245>)).
## October 26 — semantic Inspector editing is request-based in the editor, while raw direct editing remains a separate capability

The inspector has two materially different paths. `draw_sections` clones an `InspectValue`, renders an edit widget, and emits a typed `InspectEditRequest`; a domain owner is expected to validate and commit that proposal. The Bevy in-game editor also uses `edit_inspectable` to mutate a Rust value directly, but only fields whose metadata is `InspectAccess::Direct`; authority/transactional modes are shown as requiring an adapter. These are explicit ownership boundaries, not interchangeable UI styles ([section request path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/sections/mod.rs>), [direct and registered visitor paths](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/inspectable/mod.rs>), [field authority model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>)).

The reusable egui widget registry keys widgets by concrete Rust `TypeId` and optional widget ID; a named widget falls back to the type's default widget, and later registration replaces an existing identical key. The renderer is thus extensible across host-registered Rust types, but the registry is process-local and Rust-type-directed; it is not a stable cross-process semantic object protocol. The current in-game non-egui inspector is a separate text-only projection, while the editor uses egui widgets ([widget registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/registry/mod.rs>), [egui composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/mod.rs>), [text-only inspector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/inspector/mod.rs>)). This is a real reusable semantic foundation, but not yet the common runtime the owner wants shared by in-game editing and Vapor IDE.

One numeric edge is source-confirmed: `NumberWidget` edits `f32` through an `f64` temporary, accepts any finite f64, then casts it back to f32. A finite value larger than `f32::MAX` passes the check and casts to infinity. The metadata bounds clamp the f64 temporary, but are not constrained to the representable range of the registered concrete type; the helper returns `changed` even when the f32 cast is non-finite ([f32 adapter and shared numeric edit](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/widgets/mod.rs>), [number-input metadata](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>)). This is an edge case in a developer-only direct editor, not evidence of a player-facing failure; it matters because the generic widget boundary claims reusable editing but leaves type-range enforcement to each adapter. No egui interaction or runtime test was performed.

Formatting uses Unicode glyphs for em dash, ellipsis, multiplication sign and superscript digits. This is compact, but correctness of those glyphs depends on the active font coverage; the source here does not establish that every deployed platform font renders them. The user's observed missing-glyph squares are consistent with that gap but are not attributed to this exact widget without runtime evidence ([value formatting](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect_ui/formatting/mod.rs>)).

## October 26 — thermal boundaries are explicit, but coordinate and clock contracts differ by path

The current thermal subtree has a real layered contract: `ThermalBody` owns the compatibility aggregate; optional `ThermalField` owns cell energy; `ThermalMaterial` derives cell capacity/diffusivity; `CombustibleMaterial` and `Fuel` feed derived `Combustion`; `ThermalImpulse` and `ThermalPointImpulse` are inputs; flame and world-draw systems are projections. The public plugin chains `ThermalSet::{SpatialInput, Evolution, SpatialOutput}` during `Update`. Evolution then applies aggregate impulses, updates ignition/fuel, propagates heat, and cools bodies; the separate spatial adapter conducts fields and applies point impulses before evolution, then reconciles aggregate energy after it. This is the same compatibility bridge recovered from the deleted architecture note, now pinned to its call order ([thermal root and sets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/mod.rs>), [domain exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/mod.rs>), [body state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/body/mod.rs>), [combustion/fuel domain](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/combustion/mod.rs>), [impulse message](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/events/mod.rs>), [injury policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/injury/mod.rs>), [evolution ordering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/mod.rs>), [aggregate impulses/cooling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/energy/mod.rs>), [combustion lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/combustion/mod.rs>), [environmental heat transfer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/heat.rs>), [spatial API](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/mod.rs>), [spatial phase/reconciliation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/simulation/mod.rs>), [domain-owned tool commits](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/devtools/commit/mod.rs>), [thermal inspection collection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/devtools/inspection/mod.rs>), [DevTools adapter schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/devtools/mod.rs>), [Heat Ray producer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/heat_ray/mod.rs>)).

The point-impulse API calls its position `world_position`, but its adapter fetches the target's local `Transform` and computes the field-space point from that transform. This is correct for the currently inspected root manifestations; for a parented manifestation, the local transform is not the world transform, so the named world point would map to the wrong cell. The combustion propagation path likewise reads local `Transform.translation` and multiplies by each manifestation's metres-per-native factor; it does not compose parent transforms before comparing samples. These are conditional source-level coordinate risks, not observed failures in current fixtures ([point-impulse contract and conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/simulation/mod.rs>), [manifestation-space heat pass](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/heat.rs>), [scale-layer lookup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/mod.rs>)).

The thermal solver also has mixed time cadence. Internal conduction accumulates `Time::delta_secs()` into a clock capped at 0.25 seconds and advances in 1/60-second steps; aggregate cooling, fuel burn, environmental propagation, and game injury consume the current Update delta directly. Because ignition/extinction and field-to-aggregate reconciliation are nonlinear/stateful, this is not one uniform fixed-step simulation contract. The cap may be a deliberate hitch policy, but a long frame or custom time configuration can advance aggregate mechanisms by more time than conduction; the source has no shared thermal tick or explicit discarded-time report ([conduction clock](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/simulation/mod.rs>), [conduction stability solver](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/field/conduction.rs>), [aggregate cooling and fuel systems](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/energy/mod.rs>), [combustion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/simulation/combustion/mod.rs>), [game injury adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/thermal_injury/mod.rs>)). This is a source-confirmed cadence mismatch; no alternate-frame-rate or hitch scenario was run.

Several component constructors validate their initial values, but the represented invariants are not durable type invariants. `ThermalBody` exposes heat capacity and cooling publicly; material, combustion-policy and injury fields are public; `ThermalMaterial::new` checks density/specific heat/conductivity, but its public fields can be changed after construction. The thermal inspector validates its specific editable fields through domain commit code, yet other ECS/Reflect writers can bypass that adapter. Downstream field-capacity, temperature and energy equations assume positive finite properties. The constructors and inspector therefore provide a good authored path, not an invariant enforced for every mutation ([body fields/constructor](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/body/mod.rs>), [material properties/validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/material/mod.rs>), [combustion policy fields](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/domain/combustion/mod.rs>), [validated editor writes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/devtools/commit/mod.rs>), [field calculations](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/field/mod.rs>)).

Thermal debug visuals mix scale-local coordinates with SI-authored dimensions: sample locations come from `GlobalTransform`, while transfer radii, field cell sizes and the 20-metre coupling-field plane are drawn as raw runtime-chart distances. Those overlays are therefore only dimensionally faithful at a metre-scale view unless a separate presentation transform happens to compensate; these collectors do not query the sample's scale layer or convert metres to native units ([World Draw collectors](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/world_draw/mod.rs>), [focused thermal gizmo](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/devtools/gizmo/mod.rs>), [thermal presentation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/presentation/mod.rs>)). The simulation's `ThermalField` itself is authored in metres, so this is specifically a visualization interpretation gap, not evidence that its energy equations use the same raw-distance path.

The compact field model and O(n²) pair discovery are explicitly described as a first slice and future spatial-index replacement point, so this audit does not call that known tradeoff a hidden defect ([field model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/spatial/field/mod.rs>), [coupling kernel](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/thermal/coupling/mod.rs>)). The subsystem history confirms the intent: September 19 `7402cc6` moved aggregate thermal behavior, spatial refinement, and focused tests into Engine while retaining game injury; October 5 `dc69de6` removed the three focused test modules; October 6 `0e48843` removed the 99-line architecture note. Thus the current compatibility boundary is still deliberate, while its strongest local regression evidence and explanation were removed. See the [thermal history account](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md), [deleted-note comparison](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-25--thermal-subsystem-cross-check-against-its-deleted-architecture-note), and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#thermal-evolution-keeps-an-aggregate-compatibility-bridge-but-does-not-have-one-clock-or-one-coordinate-contract). No tests, builds, or runtime checks were performed.

### October 26 — voxel demand is priority-aware, but planner bounds and rank invalidation are incomplete
