The [streaming-demand facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/mod.rs>) keeps residency planning separate from generation workers. The [motion model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/motion.rs>) estimates build latency, asks the generic granularity solver for a 1–4 second lookahead, saturates the native-velocity projection to f32, and turns motion into priority/bounds rather than semantic authority. [Work ranking](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/rank.rs>) orders collision, editing, presentation, realization, then request priority, boundary-focus distance, trajectory distance and local distance.

The planner has a 65,536-entry nominal maximum, but that maximum does not bound all intermediate enumeration. Stationary/non-view scopes traverse the complete region into a `HashMap` before the final ranked vector is truncated. The moving predictive path also enumerates the complete local box before checking its budget. Therefore a large but representable scope can spend memory and CPU far beyond the selected desired-count cap before the cap takes effect. In addition, predictive-tube collection stops as soon as the shared map reaches budget; it handles each scope in input order and performs the final rank sort only after collection. Since scopes are ordered by realization/source/scale/role rather than global work rank, an earlier scope can consume the predictive allowance before a later collision- or higher-priority scope is considered. The local-first comment is implemented per scope, not across all scopes. These are concrete source-level bound/fairness mismatches; no pathological runtime case was executed.

Plan invalidation is also coarser than the ranking data it caches. `VoxelDemandPlanKey` tracks discrete chunk bounds, quantized motion, roles, request priority, and view revision, but not `priority_focus` or sub-chunk relative position. When that key is unchanged, `refresh_demand_plan` returns without rebuilding demanded-chunk scores or re-sorting `pending_desired`. A moving boundary focus or changed continuous distance can therefore leave pending order stale until a discrete plan-key transition occurs. Separately, `merge_demanded_chunk` unions capability roles but chooses scalar priority/focus/trajectory from the candidate using priority then focus then trajectory, while the final comparator places role priority first. For a chunk covered by overlapping requests, the merged rank can combine one request's stronger role with another request's score; that aggregation does not match the published lexicographic ordering. These are ranking-coherence gaps, not confirmed starvation in a running game.

The [region traverser](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/plan/regions.rs>) recursively culls by the view frustum and, for view-owned celestial demand, a sphere-shell test. Its comment says one chunk of shell slack while the margin is two chunk sizes. The one current test checks all eight octants and rejects deep interior/far air; it does not check culling cost or cap behavior. The [predictive tube selector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/plan/tube.rs>) seeds local work, samples a rounded centerline, then grows a six-neighbor frontier by trajectory score. The [plan owner](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/plan/mod.rs>) incrementally applies box-slab deltas only to stationary cuboids; moving demand is a sparse tube, so its AABB overlap is not a sufficient delta and it correctly takes the full planner. The [residency reconciler](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/demand/systems.rs>) then checks migration candidates against dense/derived/collision/editing readiness, prioritizes pending work, and keeps a bounded warm inactive cache. If a plan cannot be represented in the current canonical residency context, it retires stale desired residency and retries next frame.

The broader path joins [voxel intent](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/intent.rs>), resolved [capability scopes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/realization/model.rs>), streaming plans and the [generation batcher](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/batching/mod.rs>). Demand selection and worker generation are distinct owners, but a 65,536 desired-set cap is still large enough to represent substantial per-world retained queue/memory, and this source pass did not profile its real cost. The frame-planning loop stops iterating worlds when the shared Planning token cannot be acquired; absent an explicit fairness mechanism, later query entries can wait for another frame, a conditional scheduling risk rather than proven starvation.

History explains why the current policy is hybrid. `d8f0e3a` adds a fast entering/leaving slab-delta path for moving windows. `ab65b8e` later restricts that optimization to stationary cuboids because a swept AABB is not the sparse predictive tube and retained overlap cells may no longer belong to the new tube. `eb6814f` adds view-owned spherical-shell culling with an octant test. `f588206` removes the old pinned-shell demand path, leaving explicit source/view intent as the work owner. On October 5, `e987230` deletes tests for adaptive budget size, moving-plan hysteresis, high-speed forward ranking, stationary ordering/geometry, predictive horizon and disjoint-plan jumps. The current plan tree retains only the region-shell octant test; no tube, rank merge, stale-focus invalidation, intermediate-enumeration bound or fairness tests were found. This records lost regression evidence and unproven source risks, not a measured runtime failure. See [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-streaming-uses-predictive-priority-but-the-desired-work-bound-is-not-an-enumeration-bound).

### October 26 — generation has bounded publication, but failure paths can strand active work

The [generation scheduler](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/mod.rs>) divides the pipeline into asynchronous dense generation, ordered per-frame publication, stale-ticket retirement and candidate-world scheduling. It uses global worker slots, rotates candidate worlds round-robin, and re-ranks each round by capability rank, migration status, distance from the interaction scale and scale exponent. Critical is assigned only to collision/editing jobs; presentation jobs are latency-sensitive singleton batches but use the ordinary worker lane. The [batch planner](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/batching/mod.rs>) reserves per-key tokens, lazily rejects stale queue nodes, groups background jobs by aligned processing scope, and keeps collision/editing/presentation work out of larger throughput batches. [Generation scopes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/generation_scope/mod.rs>) are scheduling groups; the runtime manifestation and materialization key remain chunk-granular.
+
+Publication has a separate priority gap: it walks tasks in ECS query order and spends the per-frame publication budget on each task's ready FIFO before considering later tasks. `VoxelGenerationTask` does not retain its critical/latency-sensitive rank. Thus the worker queue can admit collision work as critical, yet already-completed lower-priority batch results may consume publication slots ahead of it. This is a conditional contention risk; no saturation runtime trace was captured.
+
+Two error paths can drop active work without re-queueing it. In the [batch planner](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/batching/mod.rs>), a popped desired key whose `VoxelGenerationScope::containing` fails is logged and skipped; it is not restored to `pending_desired`. If the demand key remains unchanged, the plan reconciler will not necessarily rebuild that queue. More directly, in [result publication](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/mod.rs>), failure to reconstruct a completed key's address continues after popping the output, but before removing its tracked key/token or calling `fail_generation`. The store's [reservation contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/residency/mod.rs>) leaves it `Pending` until failure, publication or deactivation. If this conversion error occurs while the key is active, it can remain a non-dense reservation with no result left to retry. Both are conditional canonical-address error paths, not observed failures.
+
+The [immutable generation recipe](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/world/recipe/mod.rs>) captures canonical address, world origin, procedural base, relevant edits and applied-edit count. At publication, new authority edits are caught up before the token-checked store publishes dense data; `needs_surface` depends on current streaming roles. Worker failure calls `fail_generation` for all unpublished tokens, stale work is dropped only when none of its keys remain active, and normal publication is bounded both by `generation_publish_budget_per_frame` and the shared reconstructible Publication budget. The [materialization store](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/residency/mod.rs>) prevents stale tokens from resurrecting deactivated data. These are strong lifecycle protections, but not every early `continue` follows the same release/retry policy.
+
+No tests are present in the inspected generation scheduler or batching subtree. History shows the growing ownership: `e7efce5` revised batching and async publication; `d8f0e3a` added the slab-delta residency optimization that later needed the stationary-only correction; `0e48843` reorganized world scheduling around shared worker capacity and per-world rank rounds. No historical change demonstrates the current publication ordering or the address-error recovery paths are verified. No tests were run. See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [generation cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-generation-has-stale-token-protection-but-publication-order-and-error-recovery-are-incomplete).


### October 26 — the materialization store separates semantic residency from disposable caches, but its warm LRU is keyed only by address

The store owns canonical materialization entries independently of ECS entities. A reservation begins as `Pending { token }`, then becomes dense data only when the active entry and token still match; worker failure becomes `Failed`, and deactivation removes pending/failed reservations or moves dense data into a warm inactive cache. Uniform generated fields are marked derived immediately because they prove no surface exists; non-uniform dense data can be published before a surface is requested, and later role activation re-arms derivation. Dense edits invalidate the current derived revision, while surface jobs clone a dense snapshot and publish only if its revision is still current. Render surfaces are a separate cached product, and the store's capability revision advances when consumers' usable facts change. This is a coherent authority split across [store state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/mod.rs>), [residency transitions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/residency/mod.rs>), [derived work](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/derived/mod.rs>), [render access](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/render/mod.rs>), and [active-count reporting](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/store/metrics/mod.rs>).

One cache-policy mismatch is concrete in the current transition code: inactive LRU entries store only the address, and reactivation decrements the inactive count but does not invalidate that address's old queue node. If the same materialization is reactivated and later deactivated again, the old node now sees the entry as inactive and can evict this recently reused data before older inactive entries. This affects warm-cache retention order, not semantic correctness: regeneration can recreate evicted dense data. The small `active_count` scan is O(all entries), but its current caller computes the adaptive warm-cache bound only after the desired plan changes or a migration candidate commits, rather than on every unchanged frame. `ensure_derived_dirty` also does not check `derived_failed_revision`; it can enqueue one retry that `begin_surface_build` then rejects for the same revision. This is bounded redundant queue work, not an infinite retry loop.

The focused store subtree has no current tests. History did have one targeted test proving uniform generated chunks become current without a surface; commit `e987230` removed it along with related derived/residency checks. The store's larger lifecycle evolved from cache and delta optimization (`48f6002`, `8bea1d6`) to async generation reservations and failure state (`e7efce5`, `e987230`) and then dense-type/store reorganization (`0e48843`). Those transitions explain the present state machine, but source history does not establish regression coverage for token mismatch, failure retirement, repeated warm reactivation, stale surface revisions, or eviction ordering. No runtime behavior was measured and no tests were run. See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [store cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-materialization-store-separates-canonical-residency-from-derived-and-render-caches).


### October 26 — voxel workers are bounded and lane-aware, but cancellation is cooperative and one lane has no caller

The [worker facade](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/mod.rs>) owns a fixed Bevy task pool, durable shared queue, per-lane admission and typed result tickets. [Executor submission](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/executor.rs>) sizes the pool to roughly three quarters of available parallelism (one worker for one or two cores), catches task panics into a terminal ticket result, and estimates latency from per-lane outstanding work and moving-average job time. [Admission](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/admission.rs>) bounds generation and derivation independently to twice worker capacity and bounds planning to one; the [queue](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/queue.rs>) uses a 2:2:1 normal-work service wheel and caps critical bursts at four before normal work receives service. [Tickets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/ticket.rs>) distinguish pending, success and terminal failure; [profiling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/worker/profiling.rs>) observes capacity, running/queued counts and average duration without choosing work. The [derivation consumer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/async_pipeline/mod.rs>) and [generation consumer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/streaming/generation/mod.rs>) share this facility.

The lane model has one currently unused branch: no source call submits `VoxelWorkLane::PresentationPlanning`, although it has a dedicated admission limit, queue slot, weighted-service share and Tracy plots. This is dormant machinery rather than active scheduling behavior; its plots will remain zero and its planned share is not currently consumed. Cancellation is also cooperative: dropping a ticket flips a flag, but a queued closure stays in the queue and retains captures (including any cloned work inputs) until a worker dequeues it and observes cancellation. Admission bounds the number of such jobs, but does not reclaim their queue position or captured memory immediately. Finally, panic results preserve only `Panicked`, not the payload/context in the ticket; any diagnosis relies on the process's panic hook/log path. These are source-observable lifecycle and observability limits, not measured throughput or memory failures.

The worker pool was introduced as a monolith and then divided into `admission`, `executor`, `queue`, `ticket` and `profiling` modules by `d806e3d` on October 8. Earlier October commits (`d06b3f3`, `e7efce5`, `e987230`, `0e48843`) expanded lane admission, cancellation leases, critical service and global scheduling; the old monolith had focused tests for worker sizing, priority/fairness, lane bounds and compute-lease lifetime. Those tests were removed during the `e987230` cleanup, and none are present in the current worker subtree. The exact scheduling invariants therefore have historical test intent but no current regression checks. See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [worker cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-worker-pool-bounds-work-and-prioritizes-lanes-but-cancellation-does-not-remove-queued-jobs).


### October 26 — semantic voxel sweeps and rigid material collision disagree for non-rigid edits

The [canonical collision provider](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/collision_query/mod.rs>) broad-phases celestial sphere and all authority-edit bounds, then [refines](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/collision_query/resolve.rs>) the combined signed-distance field in body-local SI space. It intentionally bypasses dense chunk residency, Surface Nets and Avian collider presence, which is the right structural route for high-speed queries; incomplete or exhausted traces return `Unknown`. Separately, extracted [surface materials](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/mesh/mod.rs>) filter rigid triangles using `VoxelMaterialBehavior`, and the [physics adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/physics/mod.rs>) builds trimesh colliders from that filtered topology. The material contract is explicit in [field policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/field/mod.rs>): `NEBULA` has `VoxelCollisionMode::None` while ROCK and GLASS are rigid.

The two collision authorities disagree for the currently exposed tool path. [Voxel Hand](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/voxel_hand/mod.rs>) lets a player add NEBULA by holding Control. The edit is recorded in the canonical [body-local authority](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/authority.rs>) and projected through [frame edits](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/frame.rs>). But `local_edits` in the swept resolver discards the Add material, models every Add as a solid sphere, and skips Paint; therefore an added non-rigid nebula affects high-speed semantic collision, while mesh-derived collision excludes its triangles. Paint also cannot change the semantic sweep's collision policy. This is a confirmed semantic mismatch in source, though no runtime reproduction was performed. It may explain divergence between swept flight contact and local trimesh contact for those edit types; it does not establish that this caused the user's previously reported Moon braking failure.

There is also a scaling duplication in the query schedule: [provider publication](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/collision_query/mod.rs>) calls `candidates()` and then `resolve()` for the same request; both call `collect_candidates`, so the sphere/edit broad phase runs twice. Narrowing then reconstructs the full local edit list for every candidate and evaluates every edit at every trace sample, up to 256 samples per candidate. [Authority](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/authority.rs>) is an append-only `Vec` without a spatial index; generation recipes also filter the whole edit history per chunk. This is bounded per trace but not bounded by edit-history size or candidate count, so long edit histories can multiply work. No profile was captured. The data model already separates canonical edits from dense projections in [edit operations](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/edit/operation/mod.rs>), [brushes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/edit/brush/mod.rs>), [finite bounds](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/edit/bounds/mod.rs>), [query positions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/edit/position/mod.rs>), and [dense application](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/chunk/editing/mod.rs>), but shared-authority collision and recipe paths have not gained the corresponding derived index.

The chunk-local [raycast](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/chunk/raycast/mod.rs>) samples every 0.25 units until caller-supplied `max_distance`; it does not reject infinity or detect when f32 increments stop changing the accumulator. Its current only caller passes the fixed 64-unit `TOOL_RANGE`, so no current gameplay path enters that loop condition, but the public method has no bounded-input contract and can loop indefinitely for infinite or sufficiently large distances. [Sampling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/chunk/sampling/mod.rs>) returns `None` outside the padded local chart, and the Voxel Hand caller uses this as a local interaction path, not as high-speed physical collision. Keep that scope distinction explicit.

History places the canonical narrow phase in `46e1eac` (October 9), after the broader September/October work to separate semantic collision from disposable collider residency. The implementation adds bounded tracing but no material-aware collision semantics for Add/Paint; the inspected subtree has no regression tests for agreement between semantic and mesh collision. No tests or runtime runs were performed. See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [collision cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-collision-queries-disagree-with-rigid-material-policy-and-repeat-edit-work).


### October 26 — celestial dense sampling is a bounded sphere adapter, but failed coordinate preparation becomes empty terrain

The [celestial field definition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/celestial_field/mod.rs>) currently defines one sphere radius and coarsest detail scale; it is not a terrain algorithm catalogue. [Body sampling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/base/celestial/field.rs>) resolves a chunk origin to body-local SI once, then [prepared sampling](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/base/celestial/sampling.rs>) applies scale-local deltas and clamps the signed distance to the local `EMPTY_DISTANCE` range. The canonical center/radius stay independent of the realization scale, so this path has one spherical field across scale slices. Current material is derived only from distance sign as ROCK/VOID; the `CelestialFieldSample` material member is carried but the prepared sampler reconstructs that same binary mapping.

Preparation failure is not represented as a generation error. [Base preparation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/base/mod.rs>) falls back to the per-sample canonical adapter when the fast chunk sampler cannot be prepared; for a celestial body that adapter calls `sample_at`, which retries coordinate preparation per sample and converts failure to `VoxelSample::empty(EMPTY_DISTANCE)`. A failed canonical transform can therefore silently publish an all-empty chunk and repeat the failing setup for every sample. The fallback preserves a usable value shape but loses failure provenance and can turn unsupported/unrepresentable coordinates into terrain absence. This is conditional on preparation failure, not a known current fixture case. The other canonical fallback branch returns `empty(f32::INFINITY)` if local translation fails, so unavailable samples also have two different sentinel magnitudes, though both are classified empty. No runtime case was reproduced.

The current [canonical chunk address](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/world/address/mod.rs>) keeps the core cache identity in checked `[i64; 3]` lattice offsets and converts through the owning world. That is the robust Pass-B path. A hidden [compatibility coordinate](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/world/address/mod.rs#L13-L39>) remains public and its `origin()` multiplies an `IVec3` by ten without checked arithmetic; the actual playground map caller currently supplies only small fixed coordinates. Thus the unchecked overflow is in a legacy adapter, not the core sparse address flow. Historical context is material: `69780e1` removed the former multi-feature terrain builder and replaced it with a sphere, while current field code still has only this sphere; the detailed deleted feature comparison is recorded in [world-generation review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--world-generation-currently-means-stable-construction-facts-celestial-terrain-is-a-sphere). See the [timeline](loo-cast-vapor-history-timeline.md) and [sampling cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#celestial-sampling-preserves-one-spherical-field-across-scales-but-failure-falls-back-to-empty).

### October 26 — rigid portal box partitioning trusts its inputs beyond the portal placement boundary

`PhysicalBoxHull` rejects non-finite/negative half-extents at construction and remains the intended physical shape authority. `SpatialSplitBox` converts that shape to chart-local `f32`, and `partition_box_by_plane` partitions it by inverse rotation/translation; this is coherent for the portal subsystem's enforced unit-scale rigid transforms. The split helper itself is public and accepts a public `SplitPlane` whose fields can bypass `SplitPlane::new`. Even through the constructor, a finite normal paired with a non-finite point is accepted, and the resulting signed distances and partition points become non-finite. `from_size_native` also accepts non-finite dimensions. These APIs rely on caller validation rather than enforcing finite geometry at the reusable boundary. The current portal placement path does enforce unit scale, but it does not turn these public geometry helpers into validated types ([hull](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/hull.rs>), [split geometry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/topology/split/mod.rs>), [portal transform constraints](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/config.rs>), [placement check](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/control/mod.rs>)).

The helper also consumes `Transform`, not `GlobalTransform`, and intentionally ignores `transform.scale`; the current portal path's unit-scale check makes that valid for portal endpoints, but parented bodies or other future callers would need to pass a composed rigid transform explicitly. This is an ownership/precondition that the function signature does not communicate. Current inspected callsites are portal collision/render split paths and supply queried body transforms; no parented-body reproduction was run. `SpatialScale::metres_to_native_f32` clamps individual conversions to finite f32, but later doubling a large half-extent for collider dimensions can still overflow. This is a boundary/extreme-value concern, not a demonstrated normal gameplay failure.

The geometry had four focused tests for centered partition, outside-plane behavior, rotation support radius and query exclusions. `e987230` removed all four test functions; `0e48843` then only reformatted the imports and removed the topology module's test-only import. This audit did not run tests or runtime portal crossings. The removal leaves the current reusable geometry contract without local regression coverage, but does not by itself prove a behavior regression ([test-removal diff](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), [follow-up cleanup](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e488433dd26b35a937dba8c5f755b52615e8eaf)).

### October 26 — exact gravity is a deliberate reference evaluator, with its foundational checks removed

The live gravity model is intentionally small: `RadialGravitySource` stores radius, a chosen numerical field scale and surface gravity; `GravityFieldQuery::sample` loops every source, evaluates radial acceleration analytically, and sums contributions in canonical `DVec3`. Sources too far to represent as bounded `f32` displacement at their chosen field scale return no contribution; the loop still increments `evaluated_source_count`, so that field means sources considered, not necessarily sources contributing. Fixture celestial bodies choose their field scale from radius, which is the only inspected source-authoring path. The exact O(source-count) cost is an explicit reference backend pending real profiling and source-count evidence; this is not hidden hierarchy/caching complexity ([gravity domain](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/mod.rs>), [query and sample](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/query.rs>), [source law and bounded range](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/source.rs>), [fixture field-scale selection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/scenery/celestial.rs>)).

The source constructors validate finite positive radius and finite non-negative surface gravity, but permit any finite `f64` radius; squaring an extreme accepted radius can overflow the exposed gravitational parameter. This is an extreme-value API boundary, not a current authored celestial radius issue. Gravity sample projection also maps an unrepresentable canonical receiver coordinate to a default zero sample, making “outside the source's chosen numeric chart bound” indistinguishable from no gravity in the component. Current fixtures choose scales intended to represent their local domain; no remote-scale test or numerical stress run was performed ([source constructor/parameter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/source.rs>), [projection fallback](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/mod.rs>)).

Four local gravity checks were removed by `e987230`: surface gravity, inverse-square exterior, linear interior, and gravitational-parameter conversion. The same commit removed the exact-superposition/cancellation test from the query. The direct model is documented as the deliberate simplification from earlier hierarchy/cache experiments, but its strongest local numerical oracle was deleted; this is a verification gap, not evidence the equations regressed ([removal diff](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), [gravity history](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commits/main/spacetime-engine/src/physics/gravity/)).

The topology module is genuinely reusable in ownership: split peers and manual-query exclusions are generic, and the exclusive-World helper mirrors the ECS ownership traversal for the current semantic→partition→realization graph. Current producers/consumers are still portal-centered; its claim is a reusable boundary, not evidence of multiple independent topology users ([topology module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/topology/mod.rs>), [ownership/exclusion query](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/topology/query/mod.rs>), [ownership graph query](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/manifestation/query.rs>)).

### October 26 — collision topology dirties changed sources but fingerprints only transforms and stencils

The reconciliation query explicitly marks a host dirty when `CollisionClipSource` changes. It then computes `topology_fingerprint` from host transform (only when stencils exist) and stencil identities/transforms/sizes/clearance; the source geometry itself is not included. If the source cuboid changes while an `AppliedCollisionTopology` record exists and the effective stencil set is unchanged, the newly computed fingerprint equals the old one and the system skips rebuilding the collider. The same occurs with no stencils: the empty-topology fingerprint is constant, so replacing the source shape does not update the derived collider. This is a confirmed invalidation defect in a mutable ECS component path, although normal authored hosts may treat the source as immutable. The component's doc calls it immutable, but the type does not enforce that policy ([dirty-host query and fingerprint gate](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/systems.rs>), [fingerprint inputs](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/state.rs>), [source type and geometry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/source.rs>)).

A second lifecycle gap occurs if `CollisionClipSource` is removed while the host survives: `changed_hosts` requires `With<CollisionClipSource>`, so removal does not mark it dirty, and the system has no retained original geometry from which to restore the Collider. The previously clipped collider can remain attached with no semantic source owner. Whether source removal is a supported lifecycle operation is undocumented; the implementation neither prevents it nor handles it. The host-removal case is different: it simply causes the dirty entity lookup to fail ([host query and clipped realization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/systems.rs>), [source ownership contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/collision_topology/mod.rs>)).

Collision CSG has three fitting-policy tests in its stencil module (edge support, snap-to-edge, quarter-turn quantization), all removed in `e987230`; no current ECS-level invalidation/lifecycle test exists. The topology was introduced in September 12 `6241440`, and October 6 `ab65b8e` decomposed the original large module into source/state/stencil-fit/systems. The later split improved ownership readability, but the new source-fingerprint omission is visible in the resulting boundary; it is not proven to have caused a live portal collision report ([introduction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/62414407ba7431d9286114f6d6e00f7f2abdbab4), [module split](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/ab65b8e2190a42e81f1bbae6b22a090297d8d987), [removed geometry tests](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b)).

### October 26 — canonical USF position arithmetic preserves hierarchy, while coarsening is a lossy projection

`UsfPosition` keeps balanced integer digits across the finite S-35…S+35 hierarchy and a bounded f32 leaf offset. Translation propagates carries from the leaf to the root using checked integer arithmetic; the final root carry is intentionally discarded, making the finite stack cyclic. Relative queries first refine both operands to a common finest leaf, subtract/normalize digits, and only then project the difference into a bounded requested chart. This is the central safeguard against flattening universe-scale identity into one float ([position type and invariants](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/mod.rs>), [carry/translation arithmetic](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/arithmetic.rs>), [relative projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/relative.rs>)).

A terminology seam remains around coarsening. `reexpressed_at` describes the result as the same canonical location, but coarsening clears finer integer digits and folds their value into a coarser f32 offset; that cannot retain arbitrarily fine distinctions below the new leaf resolution. The voxel wrapper more accurately says that representation precision changes and tells callers to retain the original when finer detail matters. Address construction, residency ranges and frame conversion intentionally use coarser representations as projections, while bounded relative queries avoid coarsening. The source therefore has both a strong exact-identity path and an explicit precision-reduction path, but the word “same” overstates exact equality for the latter. This is a contract/documentation issue with boundary-sensitive rounding consequences, not a demonstrated address misclassification ([re-expression and scale translation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/arithmetic.rs>), [chunk containment](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/chunk_address.rs>), [voxel coordinate wrapper](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/voxel/edit/position/mod.rs>), [bounded demand conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/residency/range.rs>)).

The f32 and f64 bounded-relative adapters also disagree on a negative bound: f32 clamps it to zero, while f64 compares against the negative value and rejects even a zero displacement. Callers currently pass positive bounds in the inspected paths, so this is a public helper contract inconsistency, not an active failure ([f32/f64 relative adapters](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/relative.rs>)). Decimal display builds ordinary decimal text from integer terms and shortest round-trip f32 decimal digits, rather than converting the full scale stack to a float. The October 6 `ab65b8e` module split moved the former 971-line position model into arithmetic, construction, decimal, display and relative modules without changing the overall contract; current code has no inline position tests. No arithmetic stress, round-trip or boundary tests were run ([decimal composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/decimal.rs>), [display](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/usf/position/display.rs>), [module split](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/ab65b8e2190a42e81f1bbae6b22a090297d8d987)).

### October 26 — game control and item APIs separate intent from device adapters, but remain fixture-oriented

The control model separates semantic controller/subject relations from runtime markers and exposes request/applied/rejected transfer messages; this is a sound authority boundary. Player death also follows semantic Player identity to the current LocalControlSubject, then disables locomotion/propulsion, clears transient movement/contact state and removes the character motor. Thus death while piloting affects the ship runtime rather than only the hidden player manifestation. The state transition is coordinated in one adapter but has no reviewed respawn/recovery counterpart in this slice ([control contracts](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/control/model.rs>), [death adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/lifecycle/mod.rs>), [player presentation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/model.rs>)).

Stance is similarly ownership-conscious: it runs only for the locally controlled Player on the detailed Character kernel/slice, blocks standing if the proposed hull overlaps geometry, then updates transform, `PhysicalBoxHull`, Avian Collider, stance state and portal traveler's cached position together. Camera eye height is explicitly another presentation owner. This is a well-integrated narrow transition rather than a generic character ability system ([stance transaction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/stance/mod.rs>)).

The generic item layer is metadata + semantic `UseItemRequest`; device input is upstream and concrete plugins own effects. That boundary is promising but current item definitions and adapters are all registered by built-in playground plugins, and `ItemAim` is one shared local actor/ray snapshot. `AimRay` normalizes direction but accepts public finite/zero-unsafe values without rejecting non-finite origin/direction; current player input is expected to provide sane rays, but the reusable public constructor does not establish that invariant. `ItemView` resolves current catalog names only when its own component changes; the built-in catalog is startup-populated and callers update item selection, so no current stale-label path was identified ([item API](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/item/mod.rs>), [action and aim request](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/item/action/mod.rs>), [catalog](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/item/catalog/mod.rs>), [item view](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/item/presentation/mod.rs>)).

The playground UI composes a catalog-backed creative menu, one cursor-held item, one hotbar, status/FPS/crosshair and contextual action text. Unicode bullets and en-dash are emitted in HUD text, so font coverage is a deployment-dependent concern consistent with the user's tofu-square report, though no rendered build was inspected here ([HUD composition and status](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/ui/hud/mod.rs>), [contextual action policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/ui/hud/context_actions.rs>)).
