### October 26 — surface telemetry is a semantic observer; fixture discovery and presentation remain authored

`SurfaceContext` is read-only telemetry, deliberately separate from gravity-up, contact normals and collision truth. It resolves the runtime subject to semantic position, measures each authored celestial candidate in that body's coarse f64 chart, uses procedural surface altitude only when the subject scale is realized, otherwise reports nominal-radius altitude, subtracts oriented hull support for clearance, and asks the coverage snapshot whether collision capability is nearby. This directly avoids interpreting a rebased local Transform as global position. Candidate selection scans every field for each subject, so work is O(subjects × bodies) and currently relies on a small fixture count; no profile was run ([surface type, measurement and schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/surface.rs>)).

The fixture scenario is still an authored Earth–Moon composition: it selects a canonical region from `WorldSeed`/construction facts, instantiates matching bodies, registers landmarks, then attaches orbital propagation to those with an available authored primary. Landmarks expose ID/kind/aliases, one display scale, coordinates and a fixed +Z arrival offset at nine body radii; they are not a dynamic universe index or player-authored navigation catalog. Lighting is a separate fixed scene policy (black clear color, ambient + one directional Sun). These are useful authored fixture adapters, not the general procedural planet/world lifecycle implied by older terrain plans ([fixture assembly](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/scenery/mod.rs>), [landmark index and arrival](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/fixture/landmarks.rs>), [lighting](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/lighting/mod.rs>), [teleport consumer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/console_commands/teleport.rs>)).

### October 26 — authored geometry has a clear asset/compiler/runtime seam, but generator validation does not bound execution

The geometry subsystem has a coherent small pipeline: a public RON schema, `.spacemap` loader and validation pass feed a private compiled-node representation; runtime reconciliation rebuilds disposable scene entities, while generic markers let game adapters decide gameplay meaning. This is an explicit and useful boundary, not a gameplay-specific engine compiler. The map validator checks IDs/references, scalar domains, convex-prism winding and a 20,000 generated-object budget ([plugin and public seam](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/mod.rs>), [asset schema and exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/mod.rs>), [schema](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/schema/mod.rs>), [loader](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/loader/mod.rs>), [validation module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/validation/mod.rs>), [scalar and sweep constraints](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/validation/constraints.rs>), [definition rules](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/validation/definitions.rs>), [map-wide validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/validation/map.rs>), [object dispatch](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/validation/objects.rs>)).

Two concrete generator-boundary defects make that budget weaker than its name suggests. First, `sweep_count` estimates `floor((end-start)/increment)+1`, while both compiler loops use an extra quarter-increment tolerance. For a span of 1.8 increments, validation counts two instances but compilation emits three; many such objects can exceed the claimed map-wide 20,000 output cap. Second, the compiler loops advance a `f32` accumulator without checking that it changed. A valid step sweep with `start_height == end_height == 100_000_000` and `increment == 1` passes the one-item estimate, but adding 1 does not change that f32 value; its loop condition remains true indefinitely. Slope sweeps have the same structure. These are input-triggerable correctness/resource hazards in the current validator/compiler contract, derived directly from the implementation; no executable reproduction was run ([sweep count](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/validation/constraints.rs>), [step/slope compiler loops](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/compile/generators/mod.rs>), [dispatch and compiled representation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/compile/mod.rs>), [compiled nodes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/compile/model.rs>)).

The asset reader also reads the entire file into an unbounded `Vec` before parsing, and the re-exported `AuthoredMap` has public fields, so callers that insert it directly into Bevy `Assets` can bypass loader validation. This matters if geometry maps become mod-provided input; the checked-in campus map is authored and currently small. Runtime rebuild otherwise has clear ownership: remove prior manifestations, materialize materials, compile, spawn, then clear dirty state. Convex prism rendering uses a fan triangulation appropriate to validated convex input and creates a matching convex-hull collider; primitive/generator compilation and authored oscillation remain separate ([unbounded read and loader validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/loader/mod.rs>), [public schema](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/schema/mod.rs>), [rebuild lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/runtime/rebuild/mod.rs>), [spawning](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/runtime/spawning/mod.rs>), [mesh construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/mesh/mod.rs>), [primitive compilation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/compile/primitives/mod.rs>), [lighting compilation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/compile/lighting/mod.rs>), [motion simulation and origin rebasing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/runtime/motion/mod.rs>)).

History clarifies the review gap: September's authored-map work established the RON asset pipeline and its initial tests; October 5 `e987230` removed the asset-validation and generator-compilation test modules, and the October 6 `ab65b8e` split validation/compiler code into smaller owners without restoring those checks. The campus map README still describes validation and the 20,000 cap as if they protect malformed edits, but does not describe finite-progress or exact generated-count invariants. This review did not run the removed tests or a runtime asset reload ([asset usage guide](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/assets/maps/README.md>), [test-removal diff](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), [validation/compiler split](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/ab65b8e2190a42e81f1bbae6b22a090297d8d987)).
### October 26 — semantic inspection separates meaning from writes, but its shared frame is engine-local and has two render paths

The current inspection layer has strong authority semantics: producers publish structured sections, fields and actions into a frame; edits and actions are messages carrying a focus target; the owning domain must recheck and commit. Field metadata distinguishes read-only, direct, validated, transactional and command access. The Inspect trait and InspectTypeRegistry add explicit compile-time type registration and erased field visitors, while values include typed quantities, units and ranges. This is a real semantic model, not just reflected ECS dumping ([inspection exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/mod.rs>), [frame and request protocol](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/frame/mod.rs>), [metadata/access](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>), [semantic values and sections](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/model/mod.rs>), [registration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/registry/mod.rs>), [field traversal contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/traits/mod.rs>), [plugin schedule and integration](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/mod.rs>)).

The UI-agnostic claim is scoped: the model avoids egui types and callback pointers, but it remains an in-process Bevy Resource/Message protocol with Entity-typed targets and values and Rust TypeId registration. It is not yet a serializable service API that Vapor Studio, CLI or a language server can consume directly. Rendering is also split: immersive inspection uses a text-only Bevy UI panel; the embedded editor uses richer egui widgets. Their shared input is meaningful, but the two hosts do not yet present one consistent inspector experience ([immersive inspector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/inspector/mod.rs>), [UI configure seam](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/mod.rs>)).

The feature palette and focus badge are small, intentionally bespoke projections: F4 creates a Startup-time flat button list of registered visualizations, and the badge displays only the focused hit's entity name at its projected point. DeveloperView keeps observer and interaction ray separate from focus, a useful ownership distinction. These are game-embedded devtools, not the generalized multi-surface Vapor UI toolkit; runtime visualization registration after Startup would not get a button from the current palette construction ([tools palette](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/tools/mod.rs>), [focus badge](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/focus_badge/mod.rs>), [screen UI composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/mod.rs>), [view state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/view/mod.rs>)).

Two contract edges remain: InspectionFrame::submit panics on duplicate global section IDs, so separately authored adapters must coordinate string IDs; and numeric input metadata is explicitly a UI hint, not domain validation. The owning systems revalidate by design, but those checks need to remain the only authority. Historical docs made this split and several future editing invariants unusually explicit; they were removed on October 6, so current source module comments no longer carry the same full roadmap. No cross-process consumer, duplicate-ID failure or UI screenshot was tested ([duplicate-section assertion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/frame/mod.rs>), [input-hint contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>), [October 6 architecture/roadmap deletion](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e488433dd26b35a937dba8c5f755b52615e8eaf)).
### October 26 — portal splitting shares candidate policy, while character and rigid solver adapters retain different motion authority

The portal stack separates a persistent physical endpoint pair and command protocol from placement, traversal, rendering and solver adaptation. `PortalCommand` is the intended mutation boundary; placement rejects scaled transforms, resolves one stable collision host and rejects positive-area overlap with the other active aperture. The built-in setup creates reciprocal destination links and a `PortalPair` once. Split candidates require active source and destination endpoints and a valid side, then use a single linear-velocity projection for predictive opening and aperture fit. Character split resolution owns kinematic collider partitioning and destination-space remainder movement; the rigid adapter owns a disposable Avian peer, with mass/gravity/external force on the authority body and solver deltas folded back through substep hooks. This is a deliberate adapter boundary, not one universal split-body implementation ([domain](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/portal/mod.rs>), [commands](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/command/mod.rs>), [placement/control](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/control/mod.rs>), [candidate policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/candidate/mod.rs>), [character lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/character/mod.rs>), [rigid adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/rigid_split/mod.rs>), [schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/mod.rs>)).

The shared candidate model predicts only center translation at constant current velocity. It does not integrate acceleration or body rotation across the tick before evaluating aperture fit. That is a confirmed model limitation; this review did not establish a missed traversal in an actual accelerated/rotating case. The active split stores source and destination IDs, but validity currently checks only that both entities still exist and are active; it does not revalidate reciprocal `Portal.destination` links or endpoint identity after activation. The normal command path does not mutate those links, and built-in setup creates a reciprocal pair, so this is an ECS-invariant weakness if another system writes the public `destination` field, not an observed ordinary-path defect. Likewise, the command system deliberately consumes placement requests that fail validation without emitting a result/diagnostic; the caller cannot distinguish rejection from a command that has not yet been processed using this protocol alone.

The code's strongest integration boundary is its USF bridge: split peers receive a temporary logical realization in a sibling authority partition, while canonical spatial transitions retire that temporary partition and reset local crossing history. The `PortalSplitTraveler` comments explicitly constrain the reserved Avian peer to an adapter rather than claiming the general 1..N authority model is pairwise. Current verification limits are material: `e987230` removed the topology tests that checked crossing orientation, one-sidedness, crossing fraction and mapping inversion, and the current portal test subtree has no replacements for those invariants. The focused rigid/character solver subtrees have no tests visible in the current source. No test, build, runtime traversal or high-speed/rotating case was run for this audit. The findings describe current contracts and gaps, not observed portal runtime failure.


The adapter comparison exposes a sharper failure path. Rigid preparation treats a missing peer as a reason to retire the split and restore the full authority collider ([rigid preparation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/rigid_split/preparation/mod.rs>)); `materialize_peer` returns failure for an invalid plane or missing partition half, and its caller deactivates/restores. Character materialization instead `continue`s when its peer entity is missing or when `portal_plane(source)` cannot be formed ([character materialization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/character/materialization/mod.rs>)). In those states the function does not restore a previously clipped authority collider or disable the peer. Peer despawn or invalid externally-mutated transforms can therefore leave stale physical manifestation state. This is a confirmed asymmetric cleanup contract from source, conditional on those invalid lifecycle states; no despawn/invalid-transform runtime test was run.

Character activation also requires `UsfLogicalRealizationOf`, `UsfScaleLayer` and its peer query result; preparation captures `tick_start`, validates the active pair/reach, retires the sibling partition when needed, and excludes only the peer from kinematic queries ([character preparation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/character/preparation/mod.rs>)). Resolution accepts only a center-plane crossing whose interpolated hull still fits the aperture, maps the crossing pose/control/velocity, simulates the unused destination fraction in four `MoveAndSlide` steps, then flips active source/destination and commits traveler position ([resolution](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/character/resolution/mod.rs>), [remainder](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/character/resolution/remainder/mod.rs>)). That is a useful explicit anti-tunneling structure, but four fixed subdivisions are not an error-bounded solver guarantee; no convergence test or fast thin-obstacle case was executed. Rigid crossings use the same center/aperture rule, map both linear and angular velocity, and swap which endpoint is source while preserving the same temporary partition ([rigid crossing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/rigid_split/reconciliation/crossing/mod.rs>)); completion uses support radius plus clear margin, or retires on invalid endpoint existence/activity ([completion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/rigid_split/reconciliation/completion/mod.rs>)).

Portal presentation is a separate, explicit derived-view system: directed `PortalFace`s map each front/back aperture to a render-layer branch; recursion builds camera/image/material paths once at Startup, with depth capped at four. Render targets are resized to the active `PrimaryGameView` viewport and existing material handles are touched so bind groups refresh; light layers are mirrored into derived/presentation layers. This adapts well to embedded views without treating the host window as the view. However, the render tree and spawned face surfaces are constructed only in `Startup`, while `PortalConfig` remains a mutable Resource and runtime visibility only responds to endpoint activation. Changing `sidedness` or recursion depth later does not reconstruct branch cameras/surfaces; render scale is the exception because resize reads it continuously. The API therefore exposes mutable-looking configuration with mixed live-vs-startup semantics ([render plugin](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/mod.rs>), [tree construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/tree/mod.rs>), [recursion config](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/config.rs>), [face identity](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/domain/face/mod.rs>), [target resizing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/recursion/targets/mod.rs>), [visibility](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/visibility/mod.rs>)).

Split visuals rebuild the two halves from the same partition point sets used by physics, hiding the cut cap for the seam and restoring the full authority mesh when split state clears ([visual adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/split/mod.rs>), [convex mesh](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/rendering/split/mesh/mod.rs>)). This is a strong cross-domain source-level consistency claim; no image comparison was made. The recursive renderer also has no current portal-local test coverage; its deleted topology test history does not establish shader, layer, resize or visual correctness.

### October 26 — playground semantics route item actions cleanly, but one split-peer lifetime is not owned

The playground is an in-game proving adapter, not a separate content system: each item plugin registers `ItemDefinition`/action hints and consumes `UseItemRequest`, while the single input adapter owns mouse/keyboard bindings and constructs shared `ItemAim`. Portal Gun emits `PortalCommand` instead of editing portal state; Projectile Gun emits `FireWeaponRequest`; Heat Ray emits `ThermalPointImpulse`; Voxel Hand records semantic body-local edits or world-local inline edits. Damageable cubes and Chunkloading Cubes demonstrate how a game-side plugin composes health, thermal state, physics, USF relationships, demand and presentation ([playground root](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/mod.rs>), [item plugin boundary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/mod.rs>), [input adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/input.rs>), [object identity](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/object/mod.rs>), [items](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/portal_gun/mod.rs>), [projectile](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/projectile_gun/mod.rs>), [heat](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/heat_ray/mod.rs>), [voxel editing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/voxel_hand/mod.rs>), [chunk demand](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/chunkloading_cube/mod.rs>), [damageable/split object](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/damageable_cube/mod.rs>), [shared item assets](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/assets/mod.rs>)). This is a credible static composition shape, but these are hard-coded Bevy plugins and fixtures, not Vapor-authored or discoverable content. `PlaygroundPickable.half_extents` is populated but has no current read site; picking uses physics raycasts instead.

The root lifetime mostly follows the generic USF relationship graph: semantic `UsfEntity` owns linked-spawn authority partitions; partitions own linked-spawn logical realizations. The split Damageable Cube additionally creates each `SpatialSplitPeer` as a separate entity with `CollisionLayers::NONE`; it has a `SpatialSplitPeer` back-reference and a presentation child but is not initially a `UsfLogicalRealizationOf`. It is attached to a temporary partition only while the portal split is active. Playground erase and death cleanup despawn the semantic root; therefore an unsplit reserved peer is outside the linked-spawn cascade and can remain as a disabled ECS entity after its authority is gone. This is a confirmed conditional lifecycle leak from the current relationships and cleanup systems, not a runtime observation. During active splits, its temporary USF relation does make semantic-root teardown cascade into it ([USF ownership contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/manifestation/components.rs>), [erase/death lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/lifecycle/mod.rs>), [split peer construction](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/damageable_cube/mod.rs>), [temporary split partition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/portal/simulation/split/mod.rs>)).

This also shows the ownership graph is semantic, not uniformly a Bevy parent tree: presentation projections are deliberately non-linked, while authority/realization links cascade downstream. Cleanup code must account for that distinction explicitly. No runtime count of entities after erase/death was taken, and no playground test was run.

### October 26 — Vapor Client is a real local service boundary, but conflict policy is reservation/rejection rather than shared queuing

The current Vapor service architecture is not just a UI wrapper. `vapor_client` owns frontend bootstrap, shared-service process supervision, local IPC and framed transport; `vapor_client_service` owns the session, provider access, persistence, operation registry and snapshots. Product identity is attached to every request as `ClientOrigin`; the protocol is versioned and represents operations, events, snapshots, structured service errors and LSP traffic as separate frame types. The service is a per-installation local singleton, identified by an endpoint hash over app root and state directory; Unix endpoints are owner-only, while Windows named pipes receive a user-SID ACL. It caps local clients at eight, caps inbound frames at 32 MiB, bounds per-client outbound frames and bytes, and disconnects a client that cannot keep up rather than letting stale state accumulate ([client crate](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/lib.rs>), [host context](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/host.rs>), [process/bootstrap](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/process.rs>), [IPC](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/local_socket.rs>), [transport](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/transport.rs>), [service entrypoint](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/main.rs>), [host](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/host.rs>), [server](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server.rs>), [session](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session.rs>), [protocol](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_protocol/src/message.rs>)).

Startup has multiple intentional protocols: a file lock serializes singleton creation, local endpoint readiness is separate from protocol readiness, the first frontend may supply a legacy-state seed, and a valid client is not usable until it has a matching protocol version and snapshot. The client starts the service only after local connect fails; after service loss, reconnect refreshes state and never replays potentially already-applied requests. The service exits after 15 seconds with no clients and no active operations. This fits the owner's “ordinary app, not OS daemon” preference, but it does not guarantee shutdown immediately when a frontend closes. The language server is separately started/stopped per authenticated IDE client and its JSON-RPC traffic bypasses application-state snapshots ([client lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client/src/process.rs>), [server lifecycle](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server.rs>), [language server host](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/server/language_server.rs>)).

The service's operation registry now has typed resource keys and rejects conflicting reservations. It does not itself queue conflicting actions: callers receive conflict state and must decide whether to surface, retry or queue. Any frontend-local queue is therefore not automatically shared across CLI, Studio, Launcher, IDE and Installer. Conflict relationships are also explicit and currently narrow (same resource, same-workspace scan/edit, same-workspace edit/workspace, plus whichever keys a caller assigns); this is not a general dependency scheduler. Current service session source contains focused registry tests, but no tests were executed during this audit ([registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/operation_registry.rs>), [operation contracts](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/operation.rs>)).

The history shows a fast but causal consolidation rather than a service present from Vapor's beginning: `f9e8b13` (Oct 18) extracts client domain/protocol/provider/application crates; `d7e21dc` (Oct 19) moves operation ownership into a shared service; Oct 19–21 adds bounded queues, client limits, startup locking and readiness handshakes; Oct 21 splits GUI products and hardens cross-target bootstrap; Oct 22–23 adds workflow tiers, origin tracking and structured diagnostics/LSP events. These changes make the shared process boundary increasingly concrete, but leave a wide compatibility surface across protocol, service session, provider, frontends and installer. No build, integration, process-tree or cross-platform launch test was run here; source comments/history document intent, not current runtime proof.



## October 26 — Installation setup is App-rooted, while uninstall and role lifecycle remain split across owners

`VaporInstallation` validates an installed `App.vapor.toml` `[root]` and discovers from `VAPOR_HOME` or executable ancestry; it intentionally excludes authored-workspace discovery. Its mutable state lives under the OS user-data root with a legacy in-app migration path ([installation model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/installation.rs>)). Base install then initializes external state, the canonical `~/Vapor`-style Superworkspace and machine PATH integration ([install workflow](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/install.rs>)). This confirms the installed app is not supposed to contain `Workspace.vapor.toml`; the Developer workspace command discussed above has a separate, intentional requirement.

The role model defaults an absent role file to Player; promoting beyond Player reconciles tools before persisting the higher role, and demotion deliberately retains tools and local data ([role transitions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/role.rs>), [tool reconciliation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/developer_environment.rs>)). The Installer GUI nevertheless runs base install/PATH and player setup directly, then uses the Client service for role transitions. That can leave base setup applied when the service transition fails, and it means not all setup is represented in one service operation ([Installer routing](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Installer/crates/vapor_installer_ui/src/lib.rs>)).

Uninstall has conservative, transactional preflight and explicit purge flags, but the current UI calls it with default options only. It confirms removal while preserving user data/source; no Danger Zone exposes the available app-external or Superworkspace purge options ([preflight and purge model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/uninstall.rs>), [UI call site](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Installer/crates/vapor_installer_ui/src/lib.rs>)). The purge is not an unconditional wipe: source-tree removal requires expected first-party origins and clean checkouts. This is a good safety contract, but only the safe default reaches users today.

Windows integration contains a concrete ABI asymmetry. A GNU Windows executable derives its PATH entry from `HostTarget::triple()` as `bin/x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm`; removal only handles a binary compiled for the MSVC environment and hard-codes the MSVC path ([target identity](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/host.rs>), [install PATH](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/install.rs>), [uninstall PATH](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/uninstall.rs>)). The mismatch can leave a stale per-user PATH entry after uninstall; this is source-confirmed, not laptop-reproduced. September 15 `666c815` made purge preflight transactional. October 21 introduced first-launch setup and role selection; October 22 tied role transitions to accepted service-operation identities. The present split shows the service operation identity covers role reconciliation but not the complete installer lifecycle.

## October 26 — content graph meaning is centralized, while catalog and protocol facts are string projections

`vapor_content` defines all ten canonical kinds, `VaporId`, exact `ContentVersionId`, dependency constraints, provider-neutral candidates, and generic graph / Packagepack composition validation. Its role-specific manifest parser and resolver use those types directly. That is an established strength: the type vocabulary and compatibility rules do not need to be reinvented independently by each frontend ([kind and dependency rules](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/content.rs>), [identity types](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/identity.rs>), [candidates](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/catalog.rs>), [resolution](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/resolution.rs>), [source-authored manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/authored_manifest.rs>)).

The catalog-facing model is intentionally broader than a resolved candidate: it merges local Workspace/Cache/Installed observations, fingerprints, conflicts, and Workshop association. However, this model and the stable protocol projection represent content ID, version, kind, dependency IDs/requirements, relationships, and Workshop IDs primarily as strings. The service parses the string kind to derive a separate `CatalogItemRole` for UX routing; unknown kinds map to `Other`, and action projection later reparses kinds for compatibility decisions. Composition persistence converts strongly typed resolver results into string-backed exact references and kinds, then performs explicit validation when reconstructing the graph. These are real adapter/validation boundaries; they are not evidence that the shared resolver rules themselves are duplicated or wrong ([catalog merge](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_domain/src/catalog.rs>), [protocol fields](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_protocol/src/state.rs>), [service projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/catalog.rs>), [durable graph conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_domain/src/composition.rs>)).

The key risk is ambiguity between four different facts: canonical content identity/kind, provider provenance, local lifecycle state, and frontend workflow role/action. Current types can represent these independently, but many are colocated in a single catalog row, while validation is split between source manifest parsing, catalog projection, action projection, and resolver rehydration. A consumer that treats an observed `Installed` location as subscription ownership, or `RuntimeContent` as a canonical kind, would be crossing boundaries the model does not equate. Conversely, flattening the projections into one universal type would discard meaningful distinctions. `ChildContentRef` in Core is a small unifying gap: it reuses canonical `ContentType` but retains a raw ID string instead of shared `ContentReference` ([Core reference](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/content.rs>)).

History supports a gradual assembly rather than a single designed cutover: Client/domain extraction introduced shared identity and resolver ownership on October 18 (`f9e8b13`); catalog names and provider observations followed; Workshop type preservation and Packagepack-owned Auto-Install rules arrived October 22 (`b32fec7`, `25aeced`, `28cc768`). That order explains why the canonical graph layer is more typed than its lifecycle and UI projections. It does not prove the string-backed protocol was accidental; compatibility and frontend decoupling are plausible reasons, and would need design/history evidence before any recommendation to replace it ([extraction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/f9e8b13), [catalog name propagation](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/74e13a2), [Workshop type preservation](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/b32fec7), [Packagepack ownership](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/25aeced), [ownership cleanup](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/28cc768)). No build, tests, or runtime behavior were exercised.

## October 26 — Packagepack Cargo generation handles Engine+Game only and is not wired into Client

The shared resolver can represent a complete typed content graph, but the current Cargo realization adapter reduces that graph to one Engine and one Game. It generates an isolated package with a fixed `engine::run(|app| game::install(app))` glue function, builds/runs with the managed toolchain and a development cache, and explicitly errors when any EngineMod, GameMod, or ExtensionMod is present. It does not add Crate nodes, realize arbitrary dependency edges, or stage a portable executable/distribution. `generate_local_cargo_realization`, `build_cargo_realization`, and `run_cargo_realization` have no in-tree callers in the checked Vapor source; this is export-only machinery today, not the current service-backed composition workflow ([generator and adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/cargo.rs>), [public exports](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/lib.rs>)).

A separate reconciler verifies and repairs only direct Cargo dependencies for a resolved Crate, refusing to overwrite conflicting Cargo declarations. Its docs explicitly reserve arbitrary behavioral Content for future work. Thus three capabilities exist separately—generic Vapor graph resolution, direct Crate dependency reconciliation, and simple Engine+Game generated-app compilation—but no current pipeline joins the full resolved content graph into a final Packagepack executable. This is a confirmed implementation boundary; no compile/run or target-platform test was performed ([Crate reconciler](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_core/src/cargo_reconciliation.rs>)).

Historical context matters: generated Cargo realization was part of the September 4 rewrite/bootstrap design; its early implementation arrived in that same Phase 0 sequence. Later Premium Docs retain tentative language (“may generate derived Cargo realization”) and assign actual integration APIs to Engine/Game/Mod. The October 22 workflow-boundary plan still lists documenting the distinction between composition metadata/Cargo realization and source authoring. This supports “unfinished vertical slice whose design remained open,” not “fully delivered contract” and not “proven abandoned” ([initial rewrite baseline](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/fedee52084150de4c373a00b3c51ec5a77ab8678), [later Crate reconciliation](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Client/commit/f9e8b13), [architecture text](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Premium%20Docs/Development/Vapor%20Rust,%20Cargo%20And%20Toolchain%20Model.md>), [workflow plan](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-22-workflow-boundaries.md>)).

## October 26 — Workshop publication copies outputs from a dev build; Vapor and Cargo dependency graphs remain authored separately

The in-use Studio authoring route builds the active workspace with the managed Cargo provider, then packages one selected Vapor artifact by copying its authored tree and declared binaries/libraries into a deployed artifact. Workshop Stage and StageBatch build **all** workspace Cargo projects in `BuildMode::Build`, then stage the chosen package; Publish re-stages and compares the reviewed fingerprint before upload. The packager expects outputs under `output/dev` and reads the `debug` profile directory, so this route publishes development-profile outputs; it does not select `BuildRelease` or strip symbols in the content package step. This is source-confirmed policy, not a measured shipped-binary problem ([authoring route](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/authoring.rs>), [Workshop stage/publish dispatch](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_service/src/session/workshop.rs>), [build profile and target dir](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/workspace_build.rs>), [deployed package staging](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_provider/src/content/packaging.rs>), [reviewed upload](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_client_application/src/publishing.rs>)).

The semantic and physical graphs are distinct and both are meaningful. Vapor manifest dependencies describe content identity, kind, compatibility and Workshop acquisition; each content Cargo manifest separately declares its Rust package/path/alias dependencies. Current staging reads both domains but does not derive or cross-validate the Cargo graph from the Vapor graph. The example Packagepack repeats Engine/Game/Mod composition semantically and in its Rust `Cargo.toml`. This is a manual integration invariant, not proof that Cargo should be replaced as the physical resolver. The dormant generated Cargo proof is a third path and is not the Studio publishing path. The long-term authoring design needs to decide where Vapor checks that a selected composition's actual Rust executable links the required semantic content ([example manifest](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/Packagepack.vapor.toml>), [example Cargo graph](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-Examples/content/hello-world-packagepack/Cargo.toml>), [semantic content model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_content/src/resolution.rs>)). No build, test, or publication was run.

### Identity file coverage and bounded auth findings

The 15 Rust files and six repository-level files are individually inventoried and described in the [current-state file disposition](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#identity-server-file-by-file-current-state-disposition--2026-10-26). Important implementation details that affect the cross-service model:

- Browser and API sessions are random opaque tokens; SQLite stores their SHA-256 hashes. No JWT is created, despite README terminology. The export route returns schema, metadata and row counts, not a restorable account/role backup.
- The root-only browser flow is the only flow that issues a dashboard session. Legacy direct provider routes are verification/link probes; GitHub-only verification does not create a standalone profile.
- Auth-attempt proof linking is transactional, but later attempt consumption/session creation are separate writes. Browser callbacks similarly validate an unconsumed state before provider/database work and consume it later. This creates a possible duplicate/concurrent completion window; this is inferred from ordering and was not reproduced.
- The sole-root safeguard is sequentially tested, but aggregate root count is checked before the role-revocation transaction. Concurrent revocations can invalidate that invariant; source-level inference only.
- `public_origin` trusts `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Host` when no configured origin is present. The default bind is loopback and deployment is expected behind a reverse proxy; safety depends on that proxy replacing incoming forwarded headers. Proxy behavior was not inspected in this batch.
- SQLite startup uses idempotent schema creation and records versions 1–3, but does not dispatch migrations by version or reject a future schema. Treat it as a small bootstrap schema, not a general upgrade system.

The accepted identity contract remains unimplemented in runtime: no introspection route and no production consumer in Client, Registry, Docs or Diagnostics. Existing account/role behavior is real and separate from that missing ecosystem authorization bridge. No tests were run.

### October 26 — Diagnostics upload exists, but retention and export/import remain promised rather than delivered

The Diagnostics service accepts reports without a server credential when `consent=true`, with a 2 MiB request ceiling, four allowlisted text artifact names, typed coarse platform fields, a regex redactor, and staged per-run files. Listing and retrieval require `VAPOR_DIAGNOSTICS_ADMIN_TOKEN`. This supports the player-accessible opt-in upload goal, but the boolean consent field is an assertion supplied by the caller rather than verified consent evidence ([upload model and route](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L25-L58>), [route/auth policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L201-L315>)).

The implementation does not fulfill the broader local product contract. `GET /export` emits metadata TOML only; it omits the stored logs and there is no import endpoint. Storage quota overflow rejects new uploads; there is no retention policy or delete route. Each accepted upload synchronously recursively measures the full run tree while holding a process-local mutex, so cost grows with stored history and the guard does not coordinate multiple service processes. Redaction recognizes a fixed set of token/key patterns and is not a blanket privacy guarantee ([export and quota](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L313-L359>), [quota/store path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L390-L465>), [redaction patterns](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L640-L686>)). These are source findings; no uploads, quota exhaustion, multi-process run, or tests were executed.

The mismatch is historical, not a newly added request: July 23's service brief already names storage/indexing and authorized developer retrieval; the README later adds export/import and retention; July 25's “report v2” adds quota and redaction, and “collapse report API” keeps one generic text-artifact request. Current source has implemented a conservative upload/retrieve slice, but its docs still overstate lifecycle completion. Identity authorization is likewise only an accepted direction: current read paths use the local diagnostics admin token. See the [per-file disposition and path history](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#diagnostics-server-file-by-file-current-state-disposition--2026-10-26).

### October 26 — operator smoke checks can persist data and public coverage is asymmetric

The root `deploy/scripts/smoke-diagnostics.sh` posts a deliberately synthetic report, downloads it to verify redaction, and removes only its local temporary files. The current router has no report-delete route, and `VAPOR_DIAGNOSTICS_MAX_STORED_BYTES` rejects an upload that would exceed the aggregate quota rather than deleting or expiring old records. Consequently each successful manual smoke leaves one persistent synthetic report in server state. This follows directly from the script and route/storage code; no smoke was run and the VPS state was not inspected ([smoke workflow](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/smoke-diagnostics.sh#L18-L79>), [routes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L237-L244>), [quota behavior](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/src/main.rs#L470-L491>)).

The docs themselves distinguish intent from implementation unevenly: the Diagnostics README says the service enforces a retention policy, while the contract says exceeding the aggregate quota rejects a new upload without deleting existing reports and explicitly excludes automatic destructive retention. The code agrees with the latter. “Retention metadata”/policy intent should not be read as an implemented lifecycle; aggregate-size admission is the only observed storage bound ([README](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/Vapor-Diagnostics-Server/README.md#L1-L17>), [contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/docs/diagnostics-report-contract.md#L87-L101>)).

Public validation also has different coverage by entrypoint. The local health check passes all five service bases, including Registry. The manual `public-http-check.sh` passes only four and has no Registry health/status/ecosystem assertion. The GitHub deployment workflow does check those Registry routes, but its public smoke is conditional on the optional public-base setting. Thus the manual check is not a complete public counterpart to local health; this is source-defined coverage, not a live outage or an executed check ([local health arguments](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/health-check.sh#L18-L32>), [manual helper](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/public-http-check.sh#L10-L27>), [optional workflow checks](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/.github/workflows/deploy.yml#L112-L150>)).

### October 26 — timer persistence flags are inert and Caddy install is not rollback-safe

Both checked-in timers use only monotonic triggers: deployment has `OnBootSec=5min` and `OnUnitActiveSec=5min`; export has `OnBootSec=15min` and `OnUnitActiveSec=1h`. Both also set `Persistent=true`. The authoritative systemd timer manual says `Persistent` has an effect only with `OnCalendar=`, which neither unit defines. The post-boot and recurring interval still run, but the flag itself does not supply calendar-miss recording/catch-up semantics. This is a source/configuration finding; the timers were not installed or queried on the VPS ([deploy timer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/systemd/vapor-deploy.timer#L1-L11>), [export timer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/systemd/vapor-state-export.timer#L1-L11>), [systemd.timer manual](https://freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.timer.html)).

`install-caddy.sh` similarly places validation after destructive replacement of the on-disk config: the template pipeline redirects straight to `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`, then `caddy fmt --overwrite` mutates that same file, and only afterward does `caddy validate` run. If rendering or validation fails, the prior file has already been lost and the replacement remains on disk; a later restart can therefore fail even while the currently running Caddy process may still hold its old in-memory config. The installer enables but does not restart Caddy; `deploy.sh` later restarts it. This is a conditional recovery hazard, not an observed outage or induced failure ([installer sequence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/install-caddy.sh#L15-L40>), [deployment restart sequence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Platform-Server/deploy/scripts/deploy.sh#L85-L98>)).


### October 26 follow-up — shell-local metadata, tool readiness, and host adapters

A source-root session eagerly rebuilds its Cargo index during `ShellState::open_paths`: if the selected source has a root `Cargo.toml`, `CargoIndex::inspect` invokes bundled Cargo metadata (`--format-version 1 --no-deps`) and retains either the parsed index or an `Unavailable` diagnostic. This is not compilation and a failed metadata call does not reject the source, but it is synchronous work on source activation and therefore can delay a shell-open action while Cargo starts or resolves metadata ([Cargo index policy and process boundary](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/cargo_metadata.rs#L11-L51>), [activation path](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/state.rs#L106-L157>)). The CLI’s own command-model and `ShellState` retain the current directory, nearest content context and this rebuildable index; these are interactive-shell projections, not durable service-owned workspace identity ([command/session types](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/command/model.rs>), [shell state](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/state.rs#L82-L157>)).

App-local tool inspection is also a frontend preflight, not a provisioning operation. `require` reports the explicit setup scripts and says it will not install; Rust status sorts discovered toolchain directories by a numeric version-name prefix and accepts the first whose required executables pass `--version`. It does not compare that selected directory with the canonical pinned toolchain, while aggregate “complete” status additionally requires the cross-toolchain and SteamCMD groups. Consequently, “tools ready” here means discoverable and launchable, not “the exact pinned environment is present”; this source does not establish which toolchain a later service-owned build actually selects ([readiness and require contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/app_local_tools.rs#L68-L145>), [candidate selection and process probes](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/app_local_tools.rs#L156-L307>), [cross-toolchain adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/cross_toolchain.rs>)). This is a status-semantics gap to reconcile with the pinned-toolchain authority, not proof of a build mismatch.

Several intentionally local developer adapters remain outside Client operation identity. Git resolution checks `VAPOR_GIT`, a persisted executable path, PATH and common OS locations; linking verifies `git --version` and writes one path to app state, but does not model credentials or repository authorization. Documentation opening resolves a local `docs/<topic>/index.html` and launches the platform viewer detached; the topic is joined without a containment check, so a local topic containing parent traversal can select an `index.html` outside the docs directory. That is a local path-handling issue, not a remote code path or a reproduced exploit ([provider resolution and persistence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/git_provider.rs#L67-L129>), [documentation lookup and viewer spawn](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/documentation.rs#L6-L39>)). Installer bootstrap and PATH-registration scripts are likewise explicit host adapters: the first writes a limited local app manifest/binary, while the second edits shell startup files. Source review noted that PATH registration is a direct rewrite and its marker-removal logic can consume the remainder if a start marker exists without the end marker; paths containing apostrophes are also interpolated into shell text without escaping. These are conditional developer-script risks, not evidence that a script was run or damaged a profile ([bootstrap script](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/scripts/bootstrap-local-app-deploy.sh>), [PATH registration script](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/scripts/register-vapor-path.sh>)).

The shared console integration is a line-oriented terminal renderer over service operation and output events. It maps status/severity, action, phase, progress, origin, stream, operation, process and composition fields into `vapor_console_core` records, uses ANSI colors only for a TTY without `NO_COLOR`, writes stderr separately, and flushes each output line. This proves shared record semantics in the CLI adapter; it does not establish a virtualized GUI console, durable log storage, or equivalent filtering/history across products ([event rendering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/console.rs#L6-L85>)). Metadata reporting is a side-effect-free snapshot, and `ValidationPlan` checks only declared prerequisites without installing or repairing them; JSON report schema is currently a separately versioned surface ([metadata snapshot](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/metadata/mod.rs#L34-L112>), [targeted validation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/metadata/validation.rs#L5-L45>), [report model/rendering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/metadata/report/mod.rs>), [human/JSON renderer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/metadata/report/render.rs>)).

The remaining terminal units are predominantly grammar, workflow-selection, prompt and executable wiring, with the notable `composition` command adapter sending typed actions through the service. `lib.rs` forbids unsafe code and missing public docs; `main.rs` turns returned errors into stderr plus exit status 1. Those crate-level boundaries do not erase the already documented direct SDK/Core routes ([composition actions](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/command/composition_commands.rs>), [workflow selection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/workflow.rs>), [prompt adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/prompt.rs>), [library policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/lib.rs>), [binary entrypoint](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor-CLI/crates/vapor_cli/src/main.rs>)). The reviewed CLI source layer contains 48 units; the following register adds path reach for every source unit not already cited in this implementation review. Citation reach is not a claim that each file has a complete semantic disposition.
