### October 26 follow-up — diagnostics sampling and telemetry delivery contract

The diagnostics plugin gives these observations a defined cadence and ownership: frame/system/physics sampling runs every 0.25 seconds; physics timings are accumulated after Avian's last step system and finalized per rendered `Update`; world/archetype sampling runs every 5 seconds. The exported snapshot is statically typed, with separate frame, world, physics and host-system fields. The frame-history buffer is capped at 600 samples, while ECS memory reports registered inline component layout multiplied by live instance counts and retains only the 24 largest entries. World entity/archetype counts exclude resource archetypes, empty archetypes and `DeveloperArtifact`; inline memory explicitly omits allocations held inside `Vec`, `String`, maps and other heap-owning values. These numbers are bounded diagnostics, not total memory accounting or a per-entity profiler ([plugin cadence and wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/mod.rs#L33-L87>), [snapshot model and memory qualification](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/model.rs#L1-L102>), [fixed-step accumulation and window reset](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/physics/mod.rs#L10-L218>), [frame sampling and low-FPS calculation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/runtime/mod.rs#L5-L76>), [world and inline-memory counting](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/world/mod.rs#L1-L74>)).

Telemetry is a separate, optional adapter. The engine only constructs its emitter when `VAPOR_TELEMETRY_ADDR` exists and accepts a TCP connection during plugin build; otherwise the typed Bevy resources remain available without telemetry. When connected, runtime metrics and the ECS memory snapshot are published as separate payloads. The shared emitter uses a bounded 256-event producer queue and `try_send` returns a boolean on full/disconnected queues; the engine call sites discard that return value. Its background writer stops after a write/flush error, so later failed publications also have no visible diagnostics-side signal. Therefore this path is intentionally non-blocking/best-effort, but metric or snapshot loss can be silent to the in-game consumer. This is a source-derived delivery limitation; no queue pressure, socket disconnect, telemetry broker, server upload or profiling UI was exercised ([optional telemetry wiring](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/mod.rs#L65-L70>), [publication call sites](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/telemetry/mod.rs#L5-L10>), [world snapshot publication](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/diagnostics/telemetry/mod.rs#L193-L232>), [bounded emitter queue and ignored-result contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_telemetry/src/lib.rs#L25-L30>, </home/leslieghf/Vapor/Vapor-Client/Vapor/crates/vapor_telemetry/src/lib.rs#L217-L273>)).

The USF implementation is also clearer when read through its module contracts. `ecs::manifestation` documents semantic identity → authority partition → logical realization → presentation projection, with view ownership orthogonal to what is presented. Only semantic→partition and partition→realization use downstream `linked_spawn`; presentation and view teardown remain owned by render/view consumers. `UsfOwnershipQuery` is read-only and traverses the first three levels; it has no cache or graph-construction validation. Recursive constituency is a separate Bevy relationship and does not itself encode lifetime ownership. That separation is semantically useful, but it leaves consistency between the two graphs and the relationship targets to callers; the public module currently exposes raw relationship components and iterators ([ownership/lifetime contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/manifestation/mod.rs#L1-L31>), [relationship components](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/manifestation/components.rs#L5-L149>), [query contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/manifestation/query.rs#L1-L49>), [independent constituency relation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/constituency/mod.rs#L1-L29>), [ECS public module surface](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/mod.rs#L1-L20>)). The source/history review records the September graph test deletion and October cleanup separately; this follow-up sharpens the present contracts but does not claim runtime integrity.


## October 26 — Combat: typed hit-to-health flow, endpoint collision and scale-local execution

The combat boundary is small and intentionally staged. `FireWeaponRequest` enters a weapon-bearing runtime entity; the adapter normalizes direction, moves the spawn point half a physical metre forward, converts authored muzzle speed into that entity's current native scale, and spawns a `Projectile` with `PortalVelocity`, `PortalTraveler`, `UsfScaleLayer` and a mesh. `Update` then advances its `Transform` directly by `PortalVelocity × Time::delta_secs`, decrements lifetime and despawns expired projectiles. The plugin orders weapon realization, motion, collision and generic health consequence through Game/Simulation sets ([domain model and schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/mod.rs#L15-L99>), [asset setup](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/assets/mod.rs#L1-L20>), [weapon request realization](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/weapon/mod.rs#L5-L39>), [projectile lifecycle and hit detection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/projectile/mod.rs#L5-L81>), [playground item adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/items/projectile_gun/mod.rs#L11-L45>)).

Hit detection is a brute-force same-chart point test: for each live projectile, the system scans every eligible `DamageableBounds + Collider` manifestation in the matching scale, calls `Collider::contains_point` only at the projectile's current transform, and chooses the nearest containing target center. It does not test the travelled segment, use the projectile mesh radius, or route collision through Avian's contact event stream. A fast or long-frame projectile can therefore cross a thin target between endpoints without a hit; this is source-defined tunneling exposure, not a reproduced failure. Work scales with projectile count × eligible damageable count. `DamageableBounds` gates candidacy here, but its `half_extents` are not used by collision; health-bar presentation does use them to size the bar. Split-peer eligibility is special-cased so inactive peers are excluded and active peers can be targeted ([endpoint query](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/projectile/mod.rs#L23-L81>), [bounds and Health model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/mod.rs#L19-L76>), [manifestation health-bar use](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/world/mod.rs#L52-L107>), [split-peer ownership/scale adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/topology/query/mod.rs#L45-L82>)).

The semantic consequence path is the stronger part: a hit target is mapped through `UsfRuntimeOwnershipQuery::semantic_of` (falling back to the raw entity), then emitted as generic `Damage`; only Health owns the authoritative amount/death transition. The hit's projectile ID and impact position are not consumed by this bridge, so the present path exposes no impact-position effect there. `Weapon` has speed, lifetime and damage only—no ammo, cooldown, projectile radius, faction or fire-policy state—and its default is 20 m/s, 3 seconds and 25 damage. Health rejects non-finite/non-positive damage, but combat request/weapon values do not have a separate validated constructor ([hit conversion](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/damage/mod.rs#L5-L19>), [Health validation and Damage contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/mod.rs#L19-L83>), [damage application](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/damage/mod.rs#L5-L22>)). The raw-entity instigator exclusion also is not semantic-owner equality; current player split peers do not carry `DamageableBounds`, so this audit does not claim a present self-hit bug, but the generic collision API would need semantic comparison if damageable alternate manifestations are introduced.

History connects this current shape to the earlier gameplay experiment. The September 10 first combat tranche described Projectile→Hit→Damage→Health→Died; September 19 extracted Health and consequence ordering, then `d523d73` renamed `Hitbox` to `DamageableBounds`. October 5 `e987230` added scale-aware muzzle conversion and filtered collision candidates to the projectile's Scale Slice, while switching hit shape authority to Avian `Collider::contains_point`; October 6 reorganized the modules. The progression is an important integration step into USF, but it did not introduce swept collision or retain focused combat tests. Combat and Health remain under `spacetime-engine/src/game`, while `loo-cast-game` installs the Game plugin from the Engine crate; the chronology shows internal cleanup ahead of the content/artifact ownership split, not proof that combat's current placement is correct ([initial combat commit](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/68717b4), [scale/collider change](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), [October module roots](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/combat/mod.rs#L1-L12>, </home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-game/src/lib.rs>)). No build, test or gameplay run was performed.


## October 26 — Health presentation: semantic values, disposable bars, and single-player assumptions

Health owns the value and damage/death transition; `health::presentation` projects that value into two views: one fixed-position player HUD fill and cached world-space frame/fill entities. The player HUD uses a 320×16 px absolute node centered 78 px above the bottom edge, samples the first `Player` realization, resolves it through generic USF ownership to the semantic Health component, and displays zero when either lookup is absent. There is no per-player view state or explicit selection contract in this projection; its `iter().next()` encodes the current one-local-player assumption. It does not present maximum/current numbers, a dead-state label, or a configurable/responsive layout. These are source-visible product constraints, not claims about how the HUD appears at runtime ([presentation scheduling and constants](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/mod.rs#L19-L68>), [player HUD construction and projection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/player/mod.rs#L8-L53>), [Player realization creation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/spawn/mod.rs#L98-L105>)).

World bars are disposable render manifestations, keyed in a cache by the active source manifestation. Every `PostUpdate`, after transform propagation, the system scans eligible realization/split-peer entities, resolves their semantic owner and Health, excludes the player's semantic entity, and creates or refreshes two unparented cuboids. The bars face the first player camera, position above rotated/scaled `DamageableBounds` (or a 0.5 m fallback), and resize fill from the normalized Health fraction. A zero fraction hides only the fill, leaving the frame. There is no distance/frustum/visibility culling in this producer, so every eligible Health manifestation remains a candidate every frame. If there is no player camera, the system returns before refreshing or retiring the cache; stale visuals can persist until a camera returns and the normal reconciliation runs. This is a resource/performance and lifecycle edge inferred from control flow, not measured or reproduced. The cache’s paired-entity repair is deliberate: if one visual disappears, `d806e3d` retires the surviving half and rebuilds the pair rather than keeping a partial entry ([world query and reconciliation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/world/mod.rs#L52-L143>), [pair repair](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/world/mod.rs#L146-L233>), [billboard/bounds geometry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/health/presentation/world/mod.rs#L236-L275>), [repair extraction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/d806e3dc7c8f6bd30e0bc23578c1b9eeb0acacff)).

The ownership query differs intentionally by scope: the HUD needs only a normal logical realization, while world presentation uses `UsfRuntimeOwnershipQuery` so active split peers resolve to their authority realization. That runtime adapter wraps the generic `UsfOwnershipQuery`; this is not two competing Health stores. The common normalized fraction is correctly derived from the one semantic Health value rather than copied onto view entities. However, Health presentation still uses raw Bevy entities and a private cache rather than a reusable UI/view projection contract, and its dimensions/colors are hard-coded beside scheduling. The presentation is coherent for the current single local player and small damageable-world case, but its player cardinality, view policy, culling and lifecycle behavior are not yet generalized. No UI runtime, multi-player scenario, camera-less transition, test suite or performance measurement was run ([generic ownership traversal](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ecs/manifestation/query.rs#L1-L49>), [runtime split-peer adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/physics/topology/query/mod.rs#L29-L83>)).

History explains the boundary churn. `5489776` first moved the health bars from playground UI into `combat::presentation::health`; `356aa47` then extracted Health, generic damage/death application and the same presentation into `game::health`, with `HealthSet` establishing damage-before-health ordering. `d523d73` renamed the old `Hitbox` marker to `DamageableBounds`, while `0e48843` documented the Health presentation submodules and switched world projection to USF ownership plus active split-peer eligibility. `d806e3d` isolated cache refresh/spawn helpers and corrected half-missing bar recovery. The direction is from an ad-hoc playground widget toward a health-owned projection with semantic-state lookup, but both presentation and Health remain in `spacetime-engine/src/game` despite the separate `loo-cast-game` artifact. The history shows intent and movement, not why this functionality should ultimately belong to Engine versus Game ([move into combat presentation](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/5489776d43a453ded0911e8ae14e416d65c7cbc3), [Health extraction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/356aa47fb7c16cf342a5eedaa58ff9f72a745613), [bounds rename](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/d523d73d2cfb3575abcc04a004544da9f26fd907), [USF and split-peer integration](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e488433dd26b35a937dba8c5f755b52615e8eaf), [cache repair](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/d806e3dc7c8f6bd30e0bc23578c1b9eeb0acacff)). No build, test or game run was performed.


## October 26 — Engine UI foundation: shared tokens exist, but layout and layering remain bespoke

`spacetime_engine::ui` is a real, centrally installed style policy: `SpacetimeEnginePlugin` adds `UiFoundationPlugin`, which initializes one mutable `UiTheme` resource. The theme provides seven text roles, two default font sources, three colors for text, two panel colors, one scrim, and base spacing/padding; consumers can derive `TextFont` and `TextColor` from the same style. It is used by the world selector, creative menu, spatial debug panel and several Developer UI surfaces, so it does establish a shared typography/color seam. However, the module explicitly declines to own layout structure or application state. It contains no shared panel, button, list, input, scrolling, resizing, responsive-layout, focus, virtualization or console/editor primitive. Thus it is a small token/style layer rather than the general egui-like library the product family needs ([engine plugin installation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/lib.rs#L80-L101>), [UI root and z-layer declarations](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ui/mod.rs#L1-L39>), [theme roles and values](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ui/theme/mod.rs#L8-L103>)).

Adoption is partial where consistency matters most. The flight HUD constructs its own text sizes, colors, panel tint, spacing and placement instead of consuming `UiTheme`, despite using the shared `UiLayer::HUD`; the world selector and creative menu do consume theme tokens. Developer panels likewise share theme text/panel values but specify individual widths and raw action styles. The layer constants are only a partial ordering convention: HUD/Modal/Drag are 0/100/110, while debug panels use 1,840–1,950 and the world selector 20,000. The code does not define how those ranges relate, so each subsystem can still leapfrog another through literal z values. This is not evidence of a visible overlap in the current runtime, but it is a demonstrated ownership gap in the supposed shared layering contract ([flight HUD styles](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/player/hud/layout.rs#L1-L130>), [themed world selector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/world/selection/mod.rs#L36-L108>), [Developer Tools panel](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/tools/mod.rs#L50-L82>), [focus badge layer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/focus_badge/mod.rs#L37-L65>), [spatial debug layer](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/devtools/panel/mod.rs#L11-L50>), [creative menu layers](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/ui/creative_menu/layout/mod.rs#L5-L35>)).

The font policy leaves the reported missing-glyph concern unresolved by design: both `regular_font` and `data_font` are `FontSource::default()`. The code comment says a bundled Unicode-capable project font is deferred until the asset is actually shipped; no in-repository custom font file was found in the inspected engine tree. This does not prove that default-font glyph coverage caused any particular square glyph, but it confirms the UI layer does not yet provide the planned project-controlled font. The same comment refers to “Stage 6”; a repository-wide Markdown search found no matching stage definition, leaving this as an unlinked planning label ([default font policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/ui/theme/mod.rs#L48-L83>)).

History shows a deliberate but limited first foundation. `f908398` introduced the theme/resource and semantic text roles on September 13; same-day `0e8611e` added font sources, title/compact roles, `TextFont` helpers and scrim policy while keeping Bevy defaults. `f9cbfda` added the coarse `UiLayer` convention on October 1 as the number of HUDs/overlays grew. October 6 `0e48843` moved the theme file under a `theme/` module and documented the boundary without expanding its component/layout capabilities. This sequence is internally consistent with “shared policy, separate app layouts”; the gap is that this very small policy seam is currently the only shared UI machinery while many interfaces still rebuild their own interaction/layout details. No change to source was made; no UI was rendered or tested ([first theme](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/f908398d64e4b9b9df1191bf637b1e09d024c496), [font and role expansion](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e8611e602794593cdbf19753d3bc9ad0e9a1278), [layer convention](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/f9cbfda9071aaad9f20853d980412b42f41aa776), [module move](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e488433dd26b35a937dba8c5f755b52615e8eaf)).


## October 26 — Loo-Cast developer adapters: clean semantic seams, primary-view limits

The test Game contributes `LooCastDeveloperAdaptersPlugin` separately from `LooCastGamePlugin`; the authored `loo-cast-game` wrapper installs both. That is a sound product boundary: the Engine owns generic `DeveloperView`, `DeveloperFocus`, `InspectionFrame` and schedule, while Loo-Cast adds camera/cursor resolution, gameplay collision focus, portal-aperture picking and identity/USF inspection. The generic view and focus remain distinct models (observer/ray versus selected target), and inspection contributors submit an ephemeral structured section rather than owning the inspector UI. This is a concrete example of a game-specific adapter over an engine facility, although the adapter implementation itself still physically resides under `spacetime-engine/src/game` ([adapter composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/loo-cast-game/src/lib.rs#L11-L17>), [Loo-Cast adapter schedule](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/mod.rs#L13-L62>), [generic view contract](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/view/mod.rs#L7-L34>), [generic focus and selection precedence](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/focus/mod.rs#L13-L100>), [per-frame inspection snapshot](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/frame/mod.rs#L29-L83>)).

The view adapter requires exactly one `PrimaryWindow` and one `PrimaryGameView`. It stores that camera as observer, suppresses the ray outside developer mode unless the view is embedded, and uses the captured cursor's viewport center or the live cursor when it is inside the camera target. The focus adapter requires exactly one `Player`; it raycasts to 250 world units, excludes all runtime representations of that subject, separately intersects active portal apertures because they are not ordinary supporting colliders, and chooses a portal when within one millimetre of the solid hit. These are focused single-primary-view policies, not multiwindow/multiview infrastructure. The `FOCUS_RANGE_METRES` name and `FocusHit::distance_meters` claim metres, but this adapter passes the number directly into chart-local `ViewRay`/Avian coordinates and does not consult `UsfScaleLayer` or convert by `SpatialScale`. The physical meaning of the range at non-reference scales is therefore not established by these files. It also discards Avian's normal and stores `normal: None`, so a consumer cannot get a surface normal from this ray path ([view resolution](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/view/mod.rs#L5-L33>), [focus ray and portal tie-break](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/focus/mod.rs#L5-L68>), [portal plane intersection](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/focus/mod.rs#L86-L112>), [world-space ViewRay](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/view/mod.rs#L54-L67>), [scale-bearing runtime component](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/spatial/slice/mod.rs#L97-L112>), [hit normal/distance model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/focus/mod.rs#L5-L25>)).

The inspection adapter resolves the selected spatial target to its semantic owner, emits the identity and hit position, labels logical realization versus split proxy, reports runtime representation count and split-peer status, and debug-asserts that a resolvable target still maps to the selected semantic entity. The generic inspector frame is cleared in `ResolveFocus`, then contributors submit during `CollectInspection`; the scheduled set chain makes these observations a current-frame projection. Focus pinning uses a hard-coded `P` key only while Developer Tools are enabled, whereas generic Editor selection is another acquisition mode with precedence over hover but below pin. The inspection is useful and domain-neutral at the model boundary, but the key binding, primary window/camera/player cardinality and scale-distance policy are adapter-local and not represented as configurable shared contracts ([identity contribution](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/inspection/mod.rs#L5-L95>), [generic frame clearing/submit](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/frame/mod.rs#L29-L83>), [DeveloperSet ordering](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/mod.rs#L67-L112>), [pin key](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/devtools/focus/mod.rs#L70-L84>)). No source changes, build, test or visual/runtime interaction were performed.

History: `f43573f` extracted the view/focus/identity functions from a 239-line monolithic game adapter into three responsibility-named modules without changing the plugin boundary. September 27 `b0990cc` replaced direct manifestation queries with `UsfRuntimeOwnershipQuery`, making focus exclusion and identity inspection aware of split peers. October 6 `0e48843` documented the module map and reorganized related devtools code. The evolution is toward reusable engine contracts plus narrow game adapters; the current implementation does uphold that at runtime wiring, though its source still lives inside the Engine package until the Game artifact migration is completed ([module extraction](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/f43573f8ffb02757b55fdeddfdfafa728b2fb6e7), [runtime-ownership integration](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/b0990cc), [module contract pass](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e488433dd26b35a937dba8c5f755b52615e8eaf)).

## October 26 — embedded Developer Editor: real viewport projection, transient layout and selection

The in-game editor is a genuine docked shell over the live Bevy world: it composes Game, Hierarchy, Structure, semantic and ECS inspectors, Gizmos, Resources, Assets and Developer visualizations; the Game tab's egui rectangle is converted from logical points to a clipped physical-pixel `Camera::viewport`. When the shell is immersed, the primary game camera stays active without an embedded viewport; when embedded, the camera receives the docked panel viewport and becomes inactive if the panel is absent or smaller than two physical pixels. This is meaningful integration of the general-purpose inspector with an actual game view, not a separate text-only editor mockup ([shell state and F2 transition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/mod.rs#L1-L153>), [tab composition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/tabs/mod.rs#L1-L91>), [toolbar](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/toolbar/mod.rs#L1-L39>), [pixel viewport adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/viewport/mod.rs#L1-L40>)).

The current boundaries are deliberately limited but have consequences. Dock state and selected entities live only in an in-memory `EditorShell` resource; no editor layout/selection persistence contract is present here. `F2` entering embedded mode promotes the current focus to selection only when there is no selection already, then synchronizes hierarchy selection. Returning to immersive mode always clears focus selection and structural selection. That makes the transition predictable for the current single shell, but selection does not survive a full enter/exit cycle as an editor document state. The viewport adapter silently returns when the primary game camera cardinality is not exactly one; the editor does not report a structured viewport error. Dock tabs cannot close or become detached windows. These are source-level product constraints, not observed malfunction ([F2 state transition](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/mod.rs#L75-L106>), [single-camera update and viewport measurement](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/mod.rs#L11-L31>), [tab policy](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/shell/tabs/mod.rs#L62-L81>)).

Developer visualization registration is a second, intentionally smaller route: plugins register a stable ID, label, order and default state; `DeveloperTools` holds a flat `HashSet` of selected IDs plus one master-enable flag. The editor tab sorts and renders all specifications as checkboxes. It has no grouping, per-visualization typed settings, discoverability/search, activation prerequisites or persistence. Domain settings are expected to live in typed resources, which avoids a generic arbitrary-value graph but leaves the editor presentation as a flat toggle list. The F4 tools palette is another presentation of the same registry; its registration is shared, while its UI is separately authored. That is reuse at the state/API layer, not a shared UI component system ([registry/model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/tools/mod.rs#L1-L130>), [editor visualization tab](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/editor/visualization/mod.rs#L1-L26>), [standalone palette](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/tools/mod.rs#L1-L91>)).

History: `f43573f` split the monolithic shell implementation into tab routing, toolbar and viewport modules, while introducing hierarchy grouping; this was a responsibility extraction, not a new docking framework. Current use of `egui_dock` and Bevy's inspector widgets is established, but the selected dock-state resource is not serialized. Thus, the embedded editor is a strong live-inspection foundation with honest immediate ECS editing, while project/file authoring, durable workspace layout, multi-view policy and structured feature discovery remain outside its current contract. The editor's explicit UI is not evidence of the separate future Vapor IDE's project model. No editor was launched or rendered during this audit ([extraction change](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/f43573f8ffb02757b55fdeddfdfafa728b2fb6e7)).
